case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 13th day of August, 2018 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4008 of 2017)
full_judgment:
Jahangir Hossain J. Delay of 298 days under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 in filing the instant civil petition for leave to appeal is hereby condoned. 

2. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 13th day of August, 2018 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4008 of 2017 disposing the Rule. 

3. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that after completion of all the requirements, writ-petitioner No.1 was appointed in Al-Gazzali Islamia Tamil Madrasa, Darulhuda, Bhandaria, Pirojpur as Principal on 03.10.2015 and joined in his respective post on 04.10.2015; writ-petitioner No.2 was appointed as Lecturer in the Bengali department of the said Madrasa on 20.10.2015 and joined in his respective post on the same day; writ-petitioner No.3 was appointed as Lecturer in the Arabic department on 20.10.2015 and joined on the same day; writ-petitioner No.4 was appointed as Lecturer in the Arabic department on 20.10.2015 and joined in his respective post on 21.10.2015; writ-petitioner No.5 was appointed as Lecturer in the department of Islamit. History and Culture on 20.10.2015 and joined in his respective post on the same day; writ-petitioner No.6 was appointed as Assistant Moulavi in the said Madrasa on 20.10.2015 and joined in his respective post on the same day; writ-petitioner No.7 was appointed as Assistant Teacher (Social Science) on 20.10.2015 and joined in his respective post on the same day and writ-petitioner No.8 was appointed as Assistant Teacher (Computer Studies) in the said Madrasa on 16.05.2015 and joined in his respective post on the same day and since then they have been serving in their respective posts of the said institution without any adverse remarks till today. 

4. It is further stated that the writ-petitioners sent applications with necessary papers to writ-respondent No.2, the Director General, urging him to grant their Monthly Payment Order (MPO) of salary but their names were not included in the list of MPO till date by the concerned authority. The writ-petitioners further tried to convince the authorities concerned showing relevant documents as required but went in vain. Therefore, finding no other alternative, the writ-petitioners moved the High Court Division and obtained a Rule Nisi. 

5. Writ-respondent No.2 contested the Rule Nisi by filing affidavit-in- opposition. 

6. Upon hearing the parties, the learned Judgment of the High Court. Division disposed of the Rule Nisi directing the writ-respondents to release the government portion of salary in the form of Monthly Pay Order (MPO) of the writ-petitioners with arrear and other benefits, if any, within 1(one) month on receipt of the judgment and order without any fail. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the writ-respondents preferred this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Court. 

8. Mr. N. K. Saha, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, contends that the High Court Division committed an error of law by ignoring the mandatory provision as laid down in the Circular vide Memo No.37.00.0000.074.29.005 (Khulna-13/12) dated 08.09.2015 issued by the Ministry of Education directing to send applications for enrollment in the MPO through online system. He further submits that the High Court Division also erred in law in not holding the view that the writ-petitioners failed to meet the requirements of appendix gha (ga)(1) and clause 13 of বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান এর শিক্ষক ও কর্মচারীদের বেতন-ভাতাদিও সরকারী অংশ প্রদান এবং জনবল কাঠামো সম্পর্কিত নির্দেশিকা, ২০১৩. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to apply its judicial mind in not holding the view that there is no rationality in enlist-ing the names of writ-petitioners in the Monthly Payment Order (MPO) within the ambit of clause 5 and 11 of the বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান (মাদ্রাসা) জনবল কাঠামো ও এমপিও নীতিমালা, ২০১০. He finally submits that the issue of enlisting any Madrasa as well as its teachers in the Monthly Payment Order (MPO) totally depends on policy decision of the Government and the same cannot be challenged under writ jurisdiction as decided by our apex court in different cases. 

9, Per Contra, Mr. Syed Mamun Mahbub, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent Nos.1-8, by supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, contends that the respondent-writ petitioners after fulfilling all the requirements, have been performing their functions regularly till today as per the provisions of the said জনবল কাঠামো সম্পর্কিত নির্দেশিকা, ২০১০. He further contends that the respondents are legally entitled to get Monthly Payment Order (MPO), but the writ-respondents denied to pay government portion of the salary in the form of Monthly Payment Order (MPO) to the writ-petitioners. He also contends that the applications were addressed by all the writ-petitioners to writ-respondent No.2, the Director General, requesting him to release the Government Monthly Payment Order (MPO) in favour of the writ-petitioners. 

10. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division along with connected documents on paper book. 

11. The claim of the writ-petitioners is that since there is no adverse remark against them in the service record, they are competent enough to be included in the list of MPO. They made representations to the authority concerned to consider their claim like other colleagues, but the writ-respondents kept silent without considering their claim or giving any reply. They also served 'Notice Demanding Justice' dated 07.03.2017 against inaction of the writ-respondents, but went in vain. Now, the moot question is whether the writ-petitioners have legal entity to be included in the list of MPO and they are legally capacitated to invoke the writ jurisdiction in the form of Mandamus under Article 102 of the Constitution for a direction upon the writ-respondents to include their names in the WO list of the institution. 

12. First of all, it is evident that writ-petitioners did not file their application for getting enrollment in the list of MPO through on line for non-government Madrasa Teachers as per circular (paripatra) dated 08.09.2015 issued by the Ministry of Education. Secondly, the Mandamus is a summary writ. It may issue on the existence of a specific legal right of the applicant to insist upon the performance by the public authority of definite duty. Mandamus commands a public functionary to do what he is under legal duty to do. Here, in the present case, we are to see whether tile concerned authority has legal obligation to meet the claim of the writ-petitioners as prayed for. 

13. On perusal of the record, it reveals that the writ-petitioners are the teachers of different departments of a non-government Madrasa serving since their appointment. At the time of their appointment in the said non-government institution, the public authority, i.e. the writ-respondents had no commitment or legal bounding obligation that they would include the names of the writ-petitioners after their appointments. So, there is no question of right of the writ-petitioners curtailed or infringed by the Government nor were they deprived of their legal entitlement as the concerned authority being silent on their representations. Inclusion in the list of MPO means inviting them to get financial benefits to be paid by the Government. In that respect, there must have financial sanction on the authority concerned to reimburse the salary payable to them. In the absence of such financial sanction, the writ-petitioners' claim is not justifiable. Earlier this Division expressed same opinion in other cases, preferably in the case of Government of Bangladesh and others-Vs-K. M. Ekbal Hossain and others in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.3882 of 2018 which is quoted below: 
"The legislature, executive and judiciary have to functions with their own spheres demarcated under the constitution. No organ can usurp the functions assigned to another. Function of democracy depends upon the strength of independency of State organs. Legislature and executive have the powers maintenance, distribution and control of finance of the State. Judiciary has the power to examine and to ensure that aforesaid two organs of the State functionaries have been working within their constitutional limits and in accordance with law. The constitution does not permit the ,Court to direct or advice the executive in the matter of policy or to sermonize qua any matter which under the constitution lies within the sphere of legislature or executive, provided these authorities do not transgress their constitutional limits or statutory powers. Judiciary also must guard against encroaching the limitations. The scope of judicial enquiry is confined to the question whether the decision taken by the Government is against any statutory provisions or is violative of the fundamental rights of the citizens or is opposed to the provisions of the Constitution. It is the executive and legislature who are entitled to frame polices and take such administrative decision as they think necessary in the public interest. The Court should not ordinarily interfere with policy decisions, unless clearly illegal or unconstitutional. 
Here, in this case, the High Court Division in fact, passed the impugned order to compel the executive to pay government portion of salaries inasmuch as the government did decide as yet to pay salaries to them or even did not assure them that the government would pay the same. In absence of the statutory obligation, the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution is not justified in issuing mandamus for payment of salary since a mandamus cannot lie in the absence of a legal right based on the existence of statutory duty. The mere fact that recognition and registration have been granted to an institution or, for that matter, for conducting new course or subject would not give rise to a presumption of a financial sanction. A financial liability cannot be foisted on the Government to reimburse the salary payable to the teachers and staffs of the private colleges on the basis of such presumption. No mandamus can issue for payment of salary by the Government in the absence of the prior sanction of the Government. 
Considering the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the High Court Division exceeds its jurisdiction in passing the impugned command of compelling the executive for enlisting the names of the writ petitioners in the monthly payment order and to pay the arrear salaries and other benefits." 
Quoting the said observation, this Division in the case of.
 
14. Government of Bangladesh and others-Vs-Md. Saidur Rahman in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2584 of 2018, held that "Since this Division has expressed its above quoted views earlier in an identical matter, the instant writ petition was not sustainable. We do not find any exception in this case." 

15. It is the Government whose decision can solve in extending list of MPG of non-government institution. Unless, such policy decision is made by the Government, no one can claim for his inclusion in the list of MPO as of right and is legally capacitated to invoke writ jurisdiction in the form of Mandamus under Article 102 of the Constitution for a direction upon the concerned authority. 

16. In the case of Government of Bangladesh and others-Vs-Md. Nazrul Islam and others, reported in 27 BLT (AD)167, this Division also observed that "In the ease in hand the petitioners did not allege that the writ respondents have violated any legal right of them. The granting of M.P.O. is the policy decision of the Government. Therefore, the petitioners could not claim the same as of right. This Division is of the view that teachers and staffs of the Non-Government School and College could not claim the M.P.G. as a matter of right and as such, direction could not be given unless infringement of legal right or violation of law." 

17. Having considered the all aspects and discussions made above, we are constrained to hold that the writ-petition filed by the writ-petitioners was not maintainable. Therefore, we find merit in the present leave petition. However, it is better to dispose of the same without granting leave as the writ petition was not maintainable. 

18. Accordingly, this petition is disposed of. The judgment and order dated 13.08.2018 of the High Court Division is hereby, set aside. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 29th day of May, 200 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2317 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 29th day of May, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2317 of 1997 making the Rule absolute. 

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.21 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh seeking declaration of title and recovery of khas possession alleging, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff, Abdur Rahman, who while possessing the suit land, transferred the same to the defendant with a condition to redeem the same and delivered possession in his favour. But the defendant did not register the deed of re-conveyance in his favour, consequently he instituted Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966 against him for redemption of the suit land and got a decree on 30.10.1968 and subsequently got the registration of the deed through Court. After the death of Abdur Rahman, the present plaintiff got delivery of possession of the land on 18.12.1980 through Court. The plaintiffs were living in other place, other than the suit land. In the month of February, 1981, the defendant forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land and as such, they filed the suit. 

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending, inter alia, that Abdur Rahman while owning and possessing the suit land sold .26 acre land to the defendant and his sister, Mosammat Ayesha Khatun alias Amena Khatun by a registered sale deed dated 03.08.1960. Subsequently, it was decided in a meeting to retransfer the said land, accordingly an agreement was executed on 03.08.1960 which was registered on the next date. Thereafter, Abdur Rahman filed Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966 against him for specific performance of the said agreement, which was decreed on contest. Said Abdur Rahman thereafter brought Title Execution Case No.06 of 1972. During pendency of the execution case, said Abdur Rahman expressed his intention to sell the suit land including the structures thereon. On receipt of an agreed price, fixing taka 8,500.00, said Abdur Rahman executed and registered a deed on 19.08.1974 in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Mymensingh and since then defendant has been possessing the suit land. In the deed of sale, it was wrongly mentioned the year of the decree of the execution case as 1969 in place of 1972, but there has been inserted the exact number of such execution case. On the basis of that registered deed, the defendant got his name mutated and paid rent to the Government by opening separate Khatian bearing No.311. The alleged story of get-ting possession through the Court by the plaintiff and subsequently dispossessed by the defendant are all false and fabricated and accordingly, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. The trial Court framed 8(eight) issues for the purpose of determination of the real controversy and consideration of case and considering the evidence on record along with documents, decreed the suit declaring the plaintiffs title over the suit land and also awarding a decree of recovery of khas possession by the judgment and decree dated 17.05.1993. 

5. Against the judgment and decree dated 17.05.1993 passed by the trial Court, the defendants preferred Other Class Appeal No.108 of 1997 in the Court of Additional District Judge, Mymensingh. The Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, heard the appeal, dismissed the same and thereby affirmed those of the trial Court dated 17.05.1993. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree, the defendants moved before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule and the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. 

7. Against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division, the plaintiffs as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2130 of 2008 and leave was granted to consider the following submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners:- 
"Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Senior Advocate, submits that the learned Judge of the High Court Division travelled beyond the pleadings and the evidence on record and recorded finding that the Courts below committed error in cancelling the deed of the defendants as there was no question raised against the defendants deed exhibit-`G' not any issue was framed nor the defendants were given any opportunity to prove their documents and the observation were all made surmises and conjecture based on misconception of law. The learned Counsel further submits that the concurrent finding of facts of the Courts below regarding defendants sale deed dated 17.12.1974 which was made long before the acquisition of title by defendants vendor, the plaintiff on 17.03.1976 by sale deed executed and registered through Court in execution of a decree for specific performance of contract and got possession thereof on 18.12.1980 and that the defendants title deed dated 17.12.1980 and that the defendants title deed dated 17.12.1974, being a forged document, and thus, the same being void abnitio does require at by the High Court Division "Unless and until and defendants deed, is cancelled in a property constituted suit, the title and possession of the defendants cannot be said to be illegal and unauthorized" is erroneous. The learned Counsel next submits that a suit for specific performance of contract against the defendants were filed, which was decreed and in execution of the said decree the plaintiffs obtained a kabala and the possession of the claim of defendants that the said decree is not binding on them is completely false and concocted and lastly Mr. Quayum submits that in view of the concurrent findings of the Courts below relying upon and believing the documents exhibit-2 as well the depositions of PWs 3 and 4 the finding of the High Court Division that as the process server could not state the alleged date of delivery of possession, inference cannot be drawn up from exhibit-2 that the plaintiff got delivery of possession through Court on 18.12.1982, is misconceived and misleading." 

8. Mr. AKM Jaglul Haider Afric, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division finds that the Courts below have committed mistake in cancelling the defendant's deed (exhibit-Thha'). He further submits that the defendant had acquired title the suit land vide his alleged title deed dated 17.12.1974 (exhibit-Thha') prior to his vendor who acquired the same vide a sale deed executed on 15.03.1976 and registered on 17.03.1976 (exhibit-1) through Court in execution of the decree and they also got delivery of possession on 18.12.1980 through exhibit-'2' and as such, the High Court Division ought to have considered that the defendant's deed in question being out and out forged and void abinitio does not require to be cancelled and in that view of the matter, the findings of the High Court Division that "unless and until the defendant's deed is cancelled, his title and possession cannot be said to be illegal" is mis-conceived and cannot sustain in law. He further submits that the defendant having not executed and registered the deed of re-conveyance in favour of the plaintiff in terms of the Court's decree as well as the plaintiff having got the deed executed and registered and delivery of possession of the suit land through Court in execution of the decree as aforesaid the defendant's alleged claim of satisfying the decree is nothing but a false, fraudulent and concocted plea to frustrate the Court's decree and grab the suit land. He further submits that in view of the concurred findings of the Courts below made relying upon and believing the Court's document (exhibit-2) as well as the depositions of PWs 3 and 4, the very findings of the High Court Division that "as the process server could not say the exact date of delivery of possession is also misconceived." 

9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for respondent Nos.1(b)-1(c), submitted that the appellate Court being the last Court of fact as well as the learned Judge of the trial Court has committed mistake in cancelling the deed being No.21734 dated 17.12.1974 of the defendant even though the plaintiff (petitioner) asked for any relief against the said registered instrument as well as no issue was framed thereof-and as such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division has rightly made the Rule absolute. He further argued that the plaintiff produced the document showing delivery of possession (exhibit-2) and a report of the concerned process server who examined as so also PW4 but could not be able to prove the same and as such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division did not make any error in law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Courts below. He lastly argued that the plaintiff failed to prove the fact as to when they were dispossessed from the suit land and as such, the judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below erred in awarding decree of the suit. 

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. 

11. It is admitted by the parties that one Abdur Rahman was the owner in possession of the disputed land who obtained a decree of re-conveyance in Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966 on 30.10.1968. The appellants as plaintiffs have come with an allegation that they acquired the title of the suit land by way of inheritance from aforementioned Abdur Rahman as his heir who duly got delivery of possession of such land on 18.12.1980 through Court in execution of aforesaid decree, but in the month of February, 1981, the defendant-respondent dispossessed them from the suit land forcibly. 

12. On the other land, the defendant-respondent denied the aforementioned contention of the plaintiff-appellants and counter claimed that after obtaining decree in Other Class Case No.144 of 1966 and during pendency of its execution case, Abdur Rahman sold out his subsisting interest in their favour on executing a kabala dated 19.08.1974 after taking consideration of taka 8500.00 and that they have been possessing the same after mutating their names in suit khatian. It has been further alleged that the alleged story of the plaintiff-appellants in respect of obtaining possession through Court and that the fact of their dispossession is false and concocted story with a view to defeat the right of the defendant-respondent. 

13. The learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants strenuously argued that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff-appellants acquired the right, title and interest over the suit land by dint of decree of re-conveyance and obtained possession through Court in execution of such decree and as such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division ought to have held that the alleged deed of the defendant in question is out and out false, forged and concocted but instead of doing so, the learned Judge of the High Court Division reversed the concurrent finding of the Courts below which is not sustainable in law. 

14. On the other hand, Mr. Mahbubey Alam, leaned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondents controverted the aforesaid argument of the plaintiff-appellants and counter argued that though the suit being Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966, it had been established that the kabala dated 13.04.1960 in favour of the predecessor of the defendant-respondents was a mortgage deed and not out and out sale deed and the Court of first instance on the basis of such observation directed this defendant to re-convey the suit land in favour of Abdur Rahman. He also argued that the present defendant-respondents instead of challenging such order in an appellate forum, he has waived his claim of out and out sale and abode by such order of the Court and as a result of which, aforesaid Abdur Rahman acquired absolute right and title over the land in dispute and thereafter, the defendant-respondents again purchased the suit land by kabala dated 19.08.1974 at a consideration of taka 8500.00 from said Abdur Rahman. The learned Senior Advocate further argued that there is no anomaly or irregularity or illegality in such purchase which has been held before execution of the decree passed in Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966. Over and above, he argued that the plaintiff-appellants failed to prove the facts of aforementioned execution since the process server failed to disclose the date of delivery of possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff-appellants. 

15. At the very outset, let us proceed to examine the evidence on record and see therefrom as to how far the defendant-respondents have been able to establish the existence of this kabala dated 19.08.1974. 

16. The defendant while deposing as PW 1 stated that after pronouncement of judgment, the plaintiffs' side filed an execution case and thereafter, he approached Abdur Rahman to sell the suit land again to him and at one point of time, he agreed to sell the same at a consideration of taka 8500.00 and accordingly, Abdur Rahman executed a sale deed on 19.08.19 14 on receiving consideration money. The defendant-respondents filed the original kabala dated 19.08.1974 before the trial Court which has been marked as exhibit-'Chha'. He further deposed that in the recital of such kabala, it has been stipulated that Abdur Rahman has sold out the subsisting interest of the suit land after being satisfied regarding the execution case of the decree passed in Other Class Case No.144 of 1966. He also deposed that he has been possessing the suit land since 1960 from the date of his first purchase on mutating his name in suit khatian and thereafter erected pucca structure therein after obtaining plan from the municipality and the fact of dispossession dated 26.02.1981 is false and concocted story. He also deposed that in this regard, he has filed an information slip issued by the Court (exhibit-'G') from which it is seen that there is no date of delivery in the execution register and as such, the writ of delivery of possession has been created for the purpose of this case with a view to defeat the right of the defendant-respondent. 

17. We would like to quote the recital of the deed dated 17.12.1974 which runs as follows: 
“কস্য সাফ কাওলা দলিল পত্র মিদং কার্য্যাজ্ঞাগে আমি আমার স্বতৃ দখলীয় নিম্ন তপছিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি ইং ১৩/০৪/১৯৬০ তারিখে রেজিষ্ট্রারী যুক্ত সাফ কবলা বর্ণিত সীর বাবত আমার বরাবরে ফেরৎ কবালা করিয়া না দেওয়ায় উক্ত ফেরৎ কাওলা আদালত করুক আমার বরাবরে সম্পাদিত ও রেজিষ্ট্রারী হওয়ায় প্রার্থনায় আমি জিলা ময়মনসিংহের সদর ২য় মুন্সেফী আদালতে ১৯৬৯ইং সালের ৬নং অন্য ডিক্রিজারী খাজনা দায়ের করিয়াছি। এবং কাওলার মুসাবিধা ও আবশ্যক ষ্ট্যাম্প দাখিল করিয়া বানিয়াই এবং তাহা আদালত কর্তৃক সম্পাদিত ও রেজিস্ট্রারী হওয়ায় অপোয় আছে। এবং সম্পাদিত আইন কাননে জঠিলতার দরুন তাহা বিলম্বিত হইতেছে এই ক্ষণ আমার টাকার বিশিষ্ট প্রয়াজন হওয়ায় এবং নিম্��� তপছিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় ভিন্ন অন্য কোথাও উপায় না থাকায় এবং নিম্ন তপছিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তির আমার বরাবর কাওলা কখন হইবে তাহা অনিশ্চিত বিধায় এবং আপনি তাহা খরিদ করিতে ইচ্ছুক হওয়ায় শপথ করণে উহার সর্বোচ্চ বাজার মূল্য মং ৮,৫০০/- যাহার আট হাজার টাকা সাবস্থ করিয়া অদ্য হাজিরান মজলীসের মোকাবিলায় আপনার নিকট হইতে উক্ত সাক্ষ্য সাকুল্য টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইয়া আমার প্রাপ্ত উপরোক্ত ডিক্রি আপনার নিকট সাফ বিক্রয় করিলাম উক্ত ডিক্রি মূলে জিলা ময়মনসিংহ সদর ২য় মুনসেফ আদালত আমি যে ১৯৬৯ সনের ৬নং অন্য ডিক্রী জারী মামলা পরিচালিত করিতেছি উহার বাবত আমার সাকুল্য প্রাপ্য উক্ত টাকা দ্বারা বোঝ প্রবোধ পাইয়াছি। এবং উক্ত ডিক্রী জারী মামলার আমার সাকুল্য প্রাপ্য পরিশোধিত ও Satisfied গণ্য হইয়াছে এবং উক্ত বিক্রীত ডিক্রিজারী বাবত আমার আর কিছুই প্রাপ্য বা দাবী দাওয়া পাই ও রহিল না এবং উক্ত ডিত্রী স্থলবস্তীগণ ক্রমে কেহই কোনও দাবী দাওয়া করিব না ও করিতে পারিব না। অদ্য হইতে আমার লব্দ জিলা ময়মনসিংহের ২য় মুনসেফ আদালত উক্ত ১৯৬৬ সালের ১১৪নং অন্যত্রকার মোকদ্দমা ডিক্রী আমার যাবতীয় স্বত্ব আপনি অত্র খরিদ মূলে স্বতৃবান মালিক দখলকার হইয়া ওয়ারীশ স্থলবর্তি ত্রমে উক্ত ডিক্রীর কাল নিজ নামজারী ক্রমে ভোগ তছরূপ করুন ও করিতে রহেন। ইহাতে আমি বা আমার ওয়ারিশ স্থলব্তীগন ক্রমে কাহারও কোন প্রকার ওজরাপত্তি নাই বা রহিল না। এবং করিলেও তাহা সর্বোচ্চ অগ্রাহ্য ও অশুদ্ধ হইবে । আমার উক্ত ডিক্রী আপনার নিকট বিক্রয়ের মর্মে ও বিক্রয় লব্দ অর্থ দ্বারা তিন ডিক্রী ও ডিক্রিজারী করত: আমার সাকুল্য প্রাপ্য পরিশোধিত ও Satisfied হইয়াছে মর্মে আদালত উক্ত ডিক্রীজারী মাজরা Satisfaction Certificate দাখিল করিয়া আমার ডিক্রিজারী আমার চূড়ান্ত নিষ্পত্তি করাইয়া দিয়াছি। এতদ্বার্থে সুস্থ দেহ ও স্বজ্ঞানে অত্র সাফ কাওলা দলিল আপনার বরাবর সম্পাদন করিয়া দিলাম ইতি সান ১৩৮১ তেরশত একাশী এবং ২রা দোষরা ভাদ্র ইং তাং ১৯/০৮/১৯৭৪ (উনিশ আট চৌয়াত্তর)।”

18. The aforementioned recital of the deed has been corroborated by the testimony of DW3, Abdul Matin, a man of 73 years who has a shop by the side of this suit land. DW3, Abdul Matin deposed that Abdur Rahman settled to sell the suit land in favour of Abul Hashem at consideration of taka 8500.00 and talk of such settlement was held in his shop in between the parties and he was present there as well as in the Sub-Registrar's office on 19.08.1974 and the payment was made in his presence. He also deposed that Abdur Rahman executed the deed in his presence and he identified the signature which has been marked as exhibit-2(2). Having considered the aforementioned testimonies of DWs 1 and 3 along with the recital of the deed dated 19.08.1974, we have no hesitation to hold that the defendant has been able to prove that the existence of such kabala dated 19.08.1974 on adducing proper evidence. We also hold the view that during continuance of the execution proceeding of Title Execution Case No.06 of 1969 both the parties agreed to sell the suit land and again in favour of the defendant-respondent and accordingly kabala dated 19.08.1974 has been registered. 

19. Now, the learned Judge of the trial Court put forth an objection in his judgment to the effect that why the stamp paper of the kabala in question has been collected from Netrokona instead of Mymensingh since the same has been registered in the Sub-Registrar Office in Mymensingh and also as objection as has been raised in the judgment that there is no explanation as to why the kabala has been registered four months after the execution. This finding of the trial Court has been approved by the Court of appeal below but the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has controverted those concurrent finding and decision of the Courts below raising allegation on point of mis-appreciation of evidence on record coupled with non-consideration and misreading the same. 

20. The provision of 114(e) of the Evidence Act provides every official work has to be presumed to have been rightly and regularly performed. We have reason to believe that the Sub-Registrar had a duty to oversee the fact as to whether the deed in question was properly presented and stamped and we have reason to be believe that the (Sub-Registrar) has done his job properly in this respect. The Sub-Registrar has got his authority to refuse the act of registration if the deed has been presented after expiry of schedule date. There is also reason to believe that the document was properly explained to the executants who admitted its execution on receipt of consideration money and whole proceeding and endorsement etc were properly done. Thus, the finding and decision made by Courts below have no leas to stand upon.

21. We have already seen that there is no date of delivery of possession in the relevant execution register as has been seen from the information slip (exhibit-'G') issued by the trial Court. In this respect, DW4, Mozibar Rahman, the Seristadar of the trial Court deposed that there is no note in the execution register to the effect that any kabala has been registered in pursuant to such decree of re-conveyance as against the relevant execution case number. Had there any existence of execution such deed of re-conveyance through Court, the same would have been surely entered in this register with a note regarding result of execution. He also deposed that no possession has been delivered to the decree-holder in pursuant to such decree as it appears from such register. On the other hand, the process server who was appointed for handing over the delivery of possession of the suit land while deposing as PW2 directly admitted to the effect that he could not say as to whether he delivered possession of the suit of land in favour of the plaintiffs or his predecessor and it is not possible on his part to say only seeing this certified copy of writ of delivery of possession. Thus, it is evident that the decree-holder, Abdur Rahman, instead of obtaining possession through Court in execution case, has sold out the suit land in favour of the defendant. 

22. PW3, Majharul Anowar, a nephew of PW1, also deposed in his cross-examination that he could not say the exact date of delivery of possession in favour of the plaintiffs by the defendant. PW4, Md. Abdul Majid, a carpenter, also deposed that he failed to remember the date, name of day and month of giving delivery of possession in favour of the plaintiffs. Those evidence on record led us to hold that the plaintiffs -hopelessly failed to prove the actual date of delivery of possession, the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division has adverted the findings of the Courts below on holding that PW2 and PW4 tried to prove the fact of giving delivery of possession but have not been able to prove the same. It has been further held that he is unable to hold that the plaintiffs' contention regarding dispossession on the date as alleged was proved in any way but even though the Courts below having not gone through the evidence most -arbitrarily held that the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land on the date as alleged and thereby most illegally decreed the suit. 

23. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division after proper appreciation of facts and circumstances arrived at a decision that the plaintiffs failed to prove the facts of getting delivery of possession through Court as well as the date of dispossession by the defendants. It has been further held that since the defendants found to have obtained title of the suit land by way of registered sale deed dated 17.12.1974 from the original owner, Abdur Rahman and remained in possession thereof, unless and until the said deed is cancelled in a proper suit, the title and possession of the defendants cannot be said to be illegal and unauthorized and as such, the suit must fail. 

24. Having considered those facts, circumstances and evidence on record, we find that the learned Judge of the trial Court as well as the appellate Court below failed to assess and appreciate the evidence on record which is full of misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record. 

25. Thus, we hold that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division was justified in reversing the concurrent finding of the Courts below. We also hold the view that there is no illegality and infirmity in the impugned judgment which calls for no interference. 

26. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1263 of 2017
lawyer:
Mr. A. M Aminuddin, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners

Mr Prober Neogi, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr Mohammad Abdul Hai, Advocate-on-Record -------- For Respondent No.1

For Respondent Nos.2- 11 -------- None represented
parties:
Kabir Ahmed Chowdhury and another ------ Petitioners

-Vs-

Sreemoti Sukladas Bhowmic and others ------- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 28th day of August, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in F.M.A. No.185 of 2011)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 28th day of August, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in F.M.A. No.185 of 2011 dis-missing the appeal. 

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the petitioners as pre-emptors instituted the original Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.40 of 2004 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 in the 1st Court of the Joint District Judge, Cumilla for getting an order of preemption of 113/4 decimals land transferred on 18.11.2002 by a sale deed stating that 37 decimals land appertaining to Plot No. 1824 corresponding to B.S. Plot No. 4106 of R.S. Khatian No.600 under Mouza-Kandirpar of Police Station-Kotwali, District-Cumilla originally belonged to one Sushila Sundori Pal who died intestate leaving behind her legal heirs three sons, namely, Priyalal Pal, Chuni Lal Pal and Manindra Kishore Pal. At the demise of Manindra Kishore Pal, his share devolved upon his two sons, namely, Tarun Kanti Pal and Jhantu Pal. Priyalal Pal, Chuni Lal Pal and Tarun Kanti Pal transferred 37 decimals land in favour of one Mohini Mohan Dastidar by a sub-kabala dated 15.01.1974 which was subsequently gifted by Mohini Mohon to his three sons, namely, Dolon Ghosh Dastidar, Raton Ghosh Dastidar and Sadhan Ghosh Dastidar on 31.07.1985. Thereafter, Dolon Ghosh Dastidar transferred his 11 decimals land in favour of one Bhupesh Chandra Datta by a sale deed dated 28.01.1986. Sadhan Ghosh Dastidar sold out his 03 decimals land corresponding to Plot No.1824 in favour of one Sheuli Chakraborty by a sale deed dated 23.01.1986 who sold that land in favour of Kabir Ahmed Chowdhury (Pre-emptor No.1) on 24.07.1993. Ratan Ghosh Dastidar and two others transferred 04 decimals land in favour of one Shyamal Chandra by a kabala deed dated 01.02.1986 who transferred some land in favour of Md. Yousuf Chowdhury Babul (Pre-emptor No.2) by a sale deed dated 09.03.1986 and 04 decimals land by another sale deed of the same date. Bhupesh Chandra Datta, thereafter, transferred the case land in favour of pre-emptee-respondent No.1 by the case kabala dated 18.11.2002. No notice was ever served upon the co-sharers and the pre-emptor-petitioners as co-sharers in the case holding. The further case of the pre-emptor-petitioners is that the purchaser (respondent No.1) is the stranger to the jute and knowing about the case kabala after obtaining certified copy of the trans-fer deed on 02.09.2004, the pre-emptor-petitioners filed the original case for get-ting the land pre-empted. 

3. Pre-emptee-respondent No.1 contested that the pre-emptor-petitioners have no locus standi to institute the pre-emption miscellaneous case as they are not co-sharers in the case land. He further contended that in pursuant to his purchase of 03 decimals land from Sheuli Chakraborty in the year 1993, pre-emptor-petitioner No.1 and his predecessor got their names mutated in respect of the said land vide Mutation Case Nos.471/1988-89 and 92/1993-94 and thereby ceased to be a co-sharer in respect of the case land. He further contended that in pursuant to purchase of 04¾ decimals land from Shyamal Chandra Pal in 1986 and 1988 respectively, pre-emptor-petitioner No.2 got his name mutated in respect of the said land vide Mutation Case No.563/1988-89 and in this way, preemptor-petitioner No.2 also ceased to be a co-sharer in respect of the case land. He also contended that the predecessor of respondent No.1, namely, Bhupesh Chandra Datta got his name mutated in respect of the case land vide Mutation Case No.702/1988-89. Apart from this, the case of the preemptee-respondents is that the preemption case is barred by the principle of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence. 

4. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Cumilla after holding trial of the original case, dismissed the same on contest by his judgment and order dated 02.06.2011 having examined the witnesses from the sides of the respective parties. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the trial Court, the petitioners preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No.185 of 2011 in the High Court Division and having heard the appeal, the Division Bench dismissed the same affirming the judgment and order dated 02.06.2011 passed by the learned Joint District, 1st Court, Cumilla, in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.40 of 2004; hence, this petition for leave to appeal. 

6. Mr. A. M. Aminuddin, Senior Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the provisions of section 24 of the Non-Agricultural. Tenancy Act, 1949 in its true sense and thus wrongly held that the pre-emptors had no locus standi to seek preemption of the case holding. He further submits that the findings of the High Court Division to the effect that the pre-emptors ceased to be a co-sharer in the case land due to separation of case jote by way of mutation Khatian is not in accordance with law because of the fact that in a case of preemption if filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and if a co-sharer tenant owns a portion of land in any plot, he is to be a co-sharer in the entire plot even if the land of that plot is recorded in more than one khatians and as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with by this Division. He further submits that the High Court Division has committed error of law in disallowing the appeal and dismissing the case without following the provisions of Order XXXIX, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

7. Mr. Probir Neogi, Senior Advocate, appearing for respondent No.1, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. Mr. Neogi further contended that the trial Court was quite justified in holding the view that the pre-emptors are not the co-sharers in the case land and they have no right of preemption since by way of the separation of joma through mutation their co-sharership in the case holding has been ceased prior to filing of their case and thus they have no locus standi to file the original miscellaneous case for getting the case land pre-empted under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. He further contended that both the pre-emptors have mutated their land and separated the joma pursuant to their earlier purchase and opened a separate khatian and are paying rent to the Government separately and thereby in respect of the case land, they are not entitled to preempt the land by virtue of their cosharership in the case holding. He adds that in the year 1989 and 1.993 respectively, pre-emptor No.1 and his predecessor-in-interest got their names mutated vide Mutation Case Nos.471/1988-89 and 92/1993-94 and pre-emptor No.2 has also got his name mutated pursuant to Mutation Case No.563/1988-89 and besides this, the predecessor-in-interest of the pre-emptee-respondent, namely, Bhupesh Chandra Datta also got his name mutated in respect of the case land by virtue of Mutation Case No.702/1988-89 and all the relevant papers have been produced from the side of the pre-emptee-respondent during trial of the original case and after proof under the purview of Evidence Act, those papers have been marked as exhibits. He also contended that the trial Court during disposal of the original case on merit rightly after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law in its true perspective arrived at a conclusive decision that the pre-emptors ceased to be the co-sharers in the case land. 

8. It is admitted by the parties that the land in suit jote original belongs to one Shushila Sundhuri Paul who died leaving behind 03 (three) sons named Priyo Lal, Chuni Lal and Monindhro Kishore Paul and their after Monindhro Kishore Paul died leaving behind two sons named Tarun Kanti Paul and Zahantu Paul. It is also admitted by the parties that Priyo Lal, Chuni Lal and Tarun Kani transferred .37 acre land out of suit jote in favour of one Mohini Mahon Ghosh Dhostidhar by the kabala dated 15.01.1974, who gifted his property in favour of their sons named Dholon Ghosh Dhostidhar, Ratan Ghosh Dhostidhar and Shadhan Ghosh Dhostidhar. 

9. Now the petitioners (pre-emptor) have come with an allegation that Ratan Ghosh Dhastidhar, Shadhan Ghosh Dhastidhar and Dholon Ghosh Dhastidhar transferred .08 acre land to one Shaymol Ghosh who subsequently transferred .04 acre land in favour of petitioner No.2 (preemptor), Yusuf Chowdhury wherein he reconstructed his dwelling, house. It has been further alleged that Shadan Ghosh Dhastidhar transferred .03 acres land to one Sheuly Chakraborty who transferred the same to petitioner No.1, Kabir Ahmed who is pre-emptor No.1. 

10. Bhupesh Dutto transferred the case land behind the back and knowledge of the petitioner who filed this pre-emption case on 16.08.2004 after being aware of the fact of such transfer. 

11. Now the moot question that falls for determination is whether the pre-emptors are being co-sharers of the suit jote or their co-sharership has been ceased by way of mutation and thereby whether they have lost their locus standi to file the pre-emption case. 

12. In this respect, pre-emptor No.2, Yusuf Chowdhury while deposing as PW1 stated during his cross-examination that he has purchased his portion of land from Shyamol Paul in the year 1986 and 1988 and constructed his dwelling house and he has separated the jama vide Mutation Case No.563 of 1988-89 and a separate Khatian being No.1686 has been created in his name on splitting the holding. He further deposed that petitioner No.1, Kabir Ahmed Chowdhury purchased 03(three) acres land from Sheuly Chakraborty who purchased the same from Shadan Dhastidhar and that he could not say as to whether Sheuly Chakraborty mutated her name and thereby separated her portion of land vide Mutation Case No. 441 of 1988-89 and that his father, Kabir Ahmed Chowdhury, also separated his portion of land vide Mutation Case No.92 of 1993-94 and thereby created a separated Khatian being No.1664. Thereafter, he deposed that he could not say as to whether there was a separate Khatian being No.1687 in the name of Bhupesh Dutto which has been created vide Mutation Case No.702 of 1988-89. 

13. Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 argued that the petitioners (pre-emptor) are no more a co-sharer in the suit khatian inasmuch as pursuant to their purchase, they got their name mutated in respect of suit land vide aforementioned mutation case and thereby they ceased to be co-sharer in respect of suit land since with the separation of holding from the joint holding and other co-sharer also being ceased to be co-sharer. On the other hand, A.M. Amin Uddin, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners (preemptor) denied the aforesaid argument and counter argued that it is to be as took into as to whether the notice of separation of holding was proceeding having been served on the co-sharer and mutation being effected behind their back and knowledge, there is no valid splitting up of jama and as such, the co-sharers have not lost their right of pre-emption under section 24 of Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. He further argued that the mutated khatian does not mean that there is the division of holding and by mutation khatian co-sharership does not extinguish the co-sharership and that in a proceeding under section 24 of Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, the petitioners ought to be co-sharer of the land transferred, not in the jama. He also argued that the ingredients of pre-emption under of section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act and those of section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act are different. The expression "holding" in section 96 is not to be found in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, He finally argued that the sub-division of holding without demarcation on the ground and not shown on the cadastral survey map is not a valid subdivision and the pre-emptee-opposite party failed to prove that after splitting jama, the land was demarcated on the ground by tri-angular pillars and that land was shown on the cadastral survey map. 

14. We have gone through the judgment passed by the learned Judge of the trial Court who observed in the following verbatim: - 
"It is admitted by the preemptor petitioner No.2 (P.W-1) himself that he mutated his name after his purchase of four decimals of land from Shyamal Pal. Though P. W.1 did not admit at the time of evidence that his father pre-emptor petitioner No.1 Kabir Ahmed Choudhury mutated his name vide mutation case No.92 of 1993-94, however the documents produced and exhibited by the opposite party No.1 such as certified copy of separation Khatian No.1664 in the name of Mrs. Shewly Chakrabarty, the predecessor of petitioner No.1 (Exhibit-Ga(1), Certified copy of order sheet of mutation case No.471 of 1988-89 instituted by Mrs. Shewly Chakrabarty (Exhibit- Gha(1) and Certificate copy of order for changing Mahal in the name Mrs. Shewly Chakrabarty (Exhibit- Uma) reveals the fact that Mrs. Shewly Chakrabarty, the predecessor in interest of petitioner No.1 Kabir Ahmed Choudhury, got her name mutated in pursuant of her purchase. Certified copy of separation Khatian No.1664 in the name of petitioner No.1 Kabir Ahmed Choudhury (Exhibit- Ga(2), Certified copy of order sheet of mutation case No.92 of 1993-94 instituted by of petitioner No.1 Kabir Ahmed Choudhury (Exhibit-Ga(3), and Certified copy of order for changing Mahal in the name Kabir Ahmed Choudhury (Exhibit-Uma(2), envisage that petitioner No.1 also got his name mutated and at the instance of petitioner No.1 jama has been separated. Certified copy of separation Khatian No.1686 in the name of petitioner No.2 Md. Yousuf Ahmed Choudhury (Babul) (Exhibit-Cha), Certified copy of order sheet of mutation case No.563/1988-89 instituted by petitioner No.2 Md. Yousuf Ahmed Choudhury (Babul) (Exhibit-Ja(1), Certified copy of petition for mutation on behalf of petitioner No.2 Md. Yousuf Ahmed Choudhury (Babul) (Exhibit-Ja(2), Certified copy of order for changing Mahal in the name petitioner No.2 Md. Yousuf Ahmed Choudhury (Babul) (Exhibit-ha), envisage that petitioner No.2 too got his name mutated and at the instance of petitioner No.2 jama has been separated. Certified copy of separation Khatian No.1687 in the name of Sree Bhupesh Datta, the predecessor of opposite party No.1 Sreemoti Sukladas Bhoumik (Exhibit-Ga), Certified copy of order sheet of mutation case No.702 of 1988-89 instituted by Sree Bhupesh Datta (Exhibit-Gha) and Certified copy of order for changing Mahal in the name Sree Bhupesh Datta (Exhibit-Uma(1) shows that the ancestor of opposite party No.1 after splitting his jama sold it to opposite party no. 1. It is evident from the earlier discussion that both the pre-emptor and the predecessor of the petitioner No.1 both separated the jama and mutated their name vide mutation case No.471 of 1988-89, 92 of 1993-94 and 563 of 1988-89 respectively. It is found that by Exhibit- "Uma" a separate Khatian has been prepared in the name of Mrs. Shevvly Chakrabarty (the predecessor of pre-emptor No.1) at a jama of taka 18 in mutation case No. 471 of 1988-89, by Exhibit-"Uma(2)" a separate Khatianhas been prepared in the name of Kabir Ahmed Choudhury (the pre-emptor No.1) at a jama of taka 20 in mutation case No.92 of 1993-1994 and by Exhibit "Jha" a separate Khatian has been prepared in the name of Md. Yousuf Ahmed Choudhury (Babul) (the pre-emptor No.2) in mutation case No.563 of 1988-1989. Since then the pre-emptors are paying rents as per their separation Khatians. It is also evident from the admission of P.W.1 and from the foregoing discussions that the jama in question was split up at the instance of both pre-emptors and opposite party No.1 in separate proceeding." 

15. The learned Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 submits that in respect of non-agricultural land on opening of separate khatians upon splitting up of the jama of land sought to be pre-empted in the name of the pre-emptors disentitled them from exercising right of pre-emption in respect of the land wherefrom he ceased to be a co-sharer because of splitting up of the jama and staring of a separate khatian in his name. In support of the aforesaid submission, he has referred to the observation made in the case of Alfazuddin Ahmed-Vs-Abdur Rahman and others reported in 8 MLR (AD) 2003 page 153 wherein it has been held as follows: 
"The question of ceasing of co-sharership in non-agricultural land upon partition by metes and bounds pursuant to a decree in partition suit and question of ceasing of co-sharership in the land on separation of jama and opening of khatian are two different aspects of ceasing of co-sharership. The two modes of ceasing of co-sharership are two distinct and different modes. The question of ceasing of co-sharership by metes and bounds pursuant to a deceee in partition suit is now a settled question. In the instant case here was ceasing of co-sharership twice-first because of decree in the partition suit filed by pre-emptor's father and second by separation of jama or splitting up of jama and opening of separate khatian by the pre-emptors." 

16. From the impugned judgment, the learned Judges of the Division Bench of the High Court Division held the view that the judgment and order is passed by trial Court a praiseworthy one wherein there has been vivid discussions and findings on the locus standi of the pre-emperors who tried to pre-empt the case land by dint of their alleged co-shareship in the case holding, but it is obvious to note from the papers on record that they have been ceased from co-shareship in the case holding and thereby they are not entitled to pre-empt the case land. 

17. In the background of the discussion made herein above, we are of the view that because of the opening separate khatian upon splitting up of the jama of the land sought to be pre-empted in the name of the pre-emptors disentitled them from exercising the right of pre-emption. If this is a fact then certainly the pre-emptors ceased to be co-sharers and debarred from claiming pre-emption. As such, the petitioners are not entitled to pre-empt the land in dispute. In the result, we hold the view that the trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal has decided the issue in hand rightly in favour of purchaser opposite party No.1 . In the instant case, we find that the learned Judges of the Division Bench of the High Court Division have made a threadbare discussion and left no stone unturned wherefrom it can be said that there is room for mis-appreciation or mis-reading or any scope for non-consideration of the evidence on record. 

18. Having considered those facts, circumstances, evidence and others materials on record, we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and accordingly, we find no merit in the petition and the same is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

19. Therefore, we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and accordingly, we find no merit in the petition. 

20. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order of the learned Judges of the Division Bench of the High Court Division is hereby affirmed. 

End.
