case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 13.01.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2807 of 2005)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 13.01.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2807 of 2005 discharging the Rule. 

2. The petitioner and respondent Nos.18- 24 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.57 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Rajnagar, Moulvibazar impleading respondent Nos.1-17 as defendants with the prayer for perpetual injunction. 

3. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Golok Nath who died leaving behind 5 (five) sons, namely, Lok Charan, Sundari Mohon, Romesh Chandra Nath, Shoshi Mohan Nath and Suresh Chandra Nath. The SA Khatian in respect of the suit land was correctly prepared in their names in equal share and by way of amicable partition, 3 (three) brothers, namely, Romesh Chandra Nath, Suresh Chandra Nath and Mohan Nath got the suit land. They offered to sell the suit land and one Yasin Ali, a predecessor of the plaintiffs, wanted to purchase the same. The talk of sale took place and the consideration was fixed at taka 20,000.00 and on 24.08.1972 an agreement of sale was executed by the said 3(three) brothers after receiving taka 16,000.00 and delivered the possession of the suit land in favour of Yasin Ali. After execution of the said Bainapatra, Yasin Ali died leaving behind his wife, plaintiff No.1, six sons, plaintiff Nos.2-7, two daughters, plaintiff Nos.8-9, who have been possessing the suit land. During Revisional Survey, the plaintiffs went to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Office, Rajnagar for mutation of the suit land in their names claiming title on adverse possession but the Mutation Case was rejected on 02.12.2000. After that, the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.3 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Moulvibazar praying for title on the basis of adverse possession and the said suit was decreed exparte on 01.07.2001 declaring the plaintiffs' title. While the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land peacefully, the defendants on 31.10.2001, in collusion with each other attempted to dispossess the plaintiffs by taking away ripe paddy from the suit land forcibly and as such, the plaintiffs were constrained to institute the instant suit for perpetual injunction. 

4. Defendant Nos.1-5 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegation made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit; that the suit was barred by limitation and that the suit being hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act was not maintainable in the present form. The defendants also con-tended that Md. Yasin Ali, predecessor of the plaintiffs, never purchased the suit land and the alleged deed of agreement is nothing but a false and forged document and the plaintiffs obtained the ex-parte decree dated 01.07.2001 in Title Suit No.3 of 2001 by practicing fraud upon the Court. The defendants further contended that the suit land belonged to Golok Chandra Nath, who died leaving behind 5(five) sons and the last SA Khatian was correctly prepared in their names. Three sons of Golok Chandra, namely, Lok Charan, Sundari Mohon Nath and Shoshi Mohon Nath got the entire suit land by way of amicable partition and they sold out the suit land in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by a registered deed dated 26.02.1982 and since then they have been possessing the suit land. Three sons of Golok Chandra Nath, namely, Romesh Chandra Nath, Suresh Chandra Nath and Shoshi Mohan Nath left this country before the liberation war and no notice of Title Suit No.3 of 2001 was served upon them and the plaintiffs obtained the ex-parte decree in Title Suit No.03 of 2001 by practicing fraud upon the Court. The plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. During the trial, the plaintiffs adduced six (6) witnesses as PWs and the defendants adduced seven witnesses as DWs and produced the documents to prove their respective case. The trial Court after consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit vide its judgment and decree dated 11.02.2004. 

6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the predecessor of respondent Nos.1-14 and respondent Nos.15-17 as the defendant-appellants filed Title Appeal No. 34 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Moulvibazar, who after considering the evidence on record allowed the appeal vide its judgment and decree dated 09.07.2004 and thereby set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 09.07.2004 passed by the appellate Court below, the plaintiff-petitioners have preferred Civil Revision No.2807 of 2005 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule and the stay order. Subsequently, the Rule was heard by the learned Judge of a Single Bench of the High Court Division who discharged the same through the judgment and order dated 09.07.2014. 

8. Being aggrieved by the said order of the High Court Division, respondent Nos.1-14 and 15 as petitioners filed two separate Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1672 of 2015 and 2522 of 2014 before the Appellate Division which were disposed of upon a direction to remand the Civil Revision for re-hearing before the High Court Division by its order dated 20.08.2015. Accordingly, the Rule of the Civil Revision was heard by the learned Judge of a Single Bench of the High Court Division who discharged the Rule by his judgment and order dated 13.01.2016.

9. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 13.01.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2807 of 2005, the petitioner preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.3151 of 2016 before this Division. 

10. Mr. Tabarak Hossain, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the suit was for a decree of perpetual injunction in which the question of possession was of utmost importance but the appellate Court dismissed the suit and thereby reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court without discussing the possession based on evidence on record and thereby committed an error of law resulting miscarriage of justice. He further submitted that the trial Court got the findings in his judgment to the effect that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land on the strength of a decree of Title suit No.3 of 2001 but the appellate Court reversed the decision of the trial Court and held that the decree of the earlier suit was obtained by the plaintiffs on practicing fraud although the said decree was not challenged by the defendant and thereby the appellate Court below has committed an error of law resulting miscarriage of justice. He also submits that the learned District Judge reversed the decree of the trial Court mainly upon discussing the decree of the earlier suit as if he was deciding the appeal in the earlier suit without considering that the earlier decree was not challenged and that decree stands valid till the date and that since the suit was for perpetual injunction, the Court has to decide the factum of possession only but the appellate Court decided the appeal as if he was deciding the title of the suit land and as such, the appellate Court below has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of jus-tice. He finally submits that the plaintiffs claimed the suit land based on the Bainapatra but the appellate Court while deciding the suit came to a conclusion that the said Bainapatra was false, as in his opinion the stamp paper was not purchased in the name of the father of the plaintiffs and his name was inserted afterward without considering that no such plea was taken by the defendant in the trial Court and as such, the aforesaid findings of the appellate Court below is not sustainable in law. 

11. Mr. Md. Zulfiqur Ahmed, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1-15, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

12. None appeared for respondent Nos.16- 24 to support the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

13. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides and perused the materials on record thoroughly. 

14. Admittedly, the suit land originally belongs to one Golok Nath who died leaving behind five sons namned Lok Charm, Sundari Mohon, Romesh Chandra Nath, Shoshi Mohon Nath and Suresh Chandra Nath and that SA Khatian in respect of land in suit was correctly prepared in their names to the extent of equal share. 

15. The plaintiffs as petitioners have come with an allegation that Ramesh Chandra Nath, Suresh Chandra Nath and Shoshi Mohon Nath acquired the entire land in suit by way of amicable arrangement and they offered to sell the same to one Yasin Ali and accordingly, an agreement was executed in between them on 24.08.1972 on fixing taka 20,000.00 as consideration. It has been further alleged that above noted three brothers executed such Bainapatra on receiving taka 16,000.00 as an advance and delivered possession therein. It has been also alleged that before registration of kabala on the basis such Bainapatra, Yasin Ali died leaving behind the present plaintiff-petitioners as his sole heirs. It has been further alleged that during revisional survey, the plaintiffs went to the office of the Thana/Upazila Assistant. Commissioner (Land) for mutating their names who refused to do so and as such, the plaintiffs were compelled to file Title Suit No.03 of 2001 in the Court of Sadar Moulvibazar and subsequently obtained an ex-parte decree on 01.07.2001. It has been also alleged that since such Bainapatra, the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land of more than twelve years and accordingly, they have acquired statutory right by way of adverse possession and on the event of resistance by the defendant, the plaintiff-petitioners were compelled to file the present suit for permanent injunction. 

16. On the other hand, the contesting defendant denied the aforesaid contention of the plaintiffs and counter claimed that the fact of execution of agreement of Bainanama is totally false and the plaintiffs have fabricated a forced Bainamapatra and also tried to grab the valuable suit property on the basis of such forced Bainapatra and subsequently obtained fraudulent ex-parte decree. The contesting defendant further contended that Ramesh Chandra Nath, Suresh Chandra Nath and Shoshi Mohon Nath left this country before the liberation movement and as such, no summons or any notice was ever served upon them and that the plaintiffs obtained the exparte decree by practicing fraud upon the Court It has been further contended that the heirs of Golok Nath sold out the suit land by a registered kabala dated 26.02. 986 in favour of these defendants and since then they have been possessing the suit land. 

17. It is the cardinal principal of law that the plaintiffs in order to succeed must establish their own case to obtain a decree and weakness of defendant's case is no ground for passing a decree in favour of the plaintiffs. Let us proceed to examine the evidence and other materials on record and see therefrom as to how far the plain-tiffs have been able to prove their case beyond reasonable shadow of doubt. 

18. The plaintiff-petitioners have filed this suit for granting an order of permanent injunction. The paramount consideration in a suit for permanent injunction is whether the plaintiffs have been successful in proving their exclusive possession. Question of title may be looked into incidentaly but decision on title in such a suit is not a guiding principle. 

19. On perusal of the materials on record, it revealed that the plaintiffs claim over the disputed land is based on a Bainapatra dated 24.08.1972 and subsequently, on the basis such Bainapatra, the plaintiffs had filed a suit for declaration of title on the ground of acquisition of statutory right of adverse possession and obtained an ex-parte decree dated 01.07.2001 as it appears from exhibit-2.

20. It is the positive case of the defence that the sons of Golok Chandra, namely, Ramesh Chandra, Surest. Chandra and Shoshi Chandra left this country before liberation movement and no summons or notice of Title Suit No.03 of 2001 was ever served upon them and the plaintiffs obtained the ex-parte decree in Title Suit No.03 of 2001 by way of practicing fraud upon the Court. On perusal of the certified copy of the judgment and decree of said ex-parte decree, it also appears that the defendants were not party in that suit although the contesting defendants purchased the suit land in the year 1986 long before the suit being Title Suit No.03 of 2001. Thus, it appears that there is illegality and infirmity in obtaining the aforesaid exparte decree. 

21. The trial Court found that since the decree of title in favour of the plaintiffs has not been challenged in any lawful forum and as such, it appears that the aforesaid decree bears the prima facie title of the plaintiffs in the suit land. Whereas the appellate Court being the last Court of fact observed that the Court below did not consider the ex-parte decree dated 01.07.2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Moulvibazar in Title Suit No.03 of 2001 is collusive one and he held that the same was obtained by practicing fraud upon the Court and that all the defendants of that Title Suit No. 03 of 2001 were the citizens of India and the defendant-appellants were not made party in the said suit although it has been asserted in the plaint of that Title Suit No.03 of 2001 (exhibit-2) that they went to the Office of Assistant Commissioner (Land), Rajnagar for mutation and they were refused. It has been further observed that according to provision of section 44 of the Evidence Act, legality of the impugned ex-parte decree can be called in question without instituting any separate suit. It is a matter of fact and law that when a judgment is set up by one party as a bar to the claim of the other, the first party will have to show that the same was delivered without jurisdiction or was obtained by fraud and that it is not necessary for him to have the judgment set aside by instituting a separate suit. 

22. The learned Advocate for the petitioner-plaintiffs has cited a decision enunciated in the case of Jahangir Alam (Md) Vs. Md. Shamsur Rahman Sarder reported in DLR 16 BLC (AD) page 22 wherein it has been held that:-
"When a judgment is given in evidence, the party against whom it is given in evidence may, in the proceeding in which it is given in evidence, show that the judgment was obtained by fraud or collusion, and a separate suit to have the said judgment set aside is not necessary. In view of the wide terms used in section 44 of the Evidence Act, it cannot be said that it is not open to a Court other than the Court from which the decree was passed, in cases fraud or collusion, to deal with the matter and decide whether the decree was obtained by fraud or collusion." 

23. Having considered those facts, circumstances and aforementioned enunciation, it appears that the appellate Court as well as the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division has rightly reversed the finding of the trial Court on holding that as per section 44 of the Evidence Act, legality of the impugned ex-parte decree can be called in question without instituting any separate suit to have the ex-parte decree set aside. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division further observed that there is no misreading, non-consideration and non-appreciation in the judgment of the appellate Court in holding that no title has been accrued on the basis of the said Bainapatra. In this regard, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff (petitioner) has cited a case law enunciated in the case of Shahidul Haque Vs Court of Settlement, reported in 69 DLR (AD) page 241 (para 31) where in it has been held that:-
"...It is now well settled that even without challenging a decree if it can be shown that any decree has been obtained by fraud a Court in a collateral proceeding can ignore such decree. A judgment obtained by fraud or collusion may be treated as nullity. Even the executing Court may refuse to execute a void decree without any formal proceedings to set aside the same if it can be shown that on the face of the decree, it has been obtained by fraud..." 

24. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of plaintiff-petitioner strenuously argued that the learned Assistant Judge evidently erred in law and mis-appreciated the scope of perpetual injunction. He next submitted that the learned Judge of the trial Court did not peruse the so-called Bainapatra dated 24.08.1972 which is the foundation of the claim of plaintiff-respondents. In such a context, the learned Advocate has drawn the attention of this Court on the said Bainapatra and submits that the name of the purchaser of the stamp and was subsequently manipulated removing the previous writing in respect of Bainapatra dated 24.08.1972, the appellate Court as the last Court of fact observed that the three brothers, namely, Ramesh Chandra Nath, Suresh Chandra Nath and Shoshi Mohon Nath alleged to have executed the same in favour of Yasin Ali (predecessor of plaintiffs) but the defence case is that since those three brothers left this country for India before liberation of Bangladesh and as such, it was not possible on their part to execute such Bainapatra in the year 1972. The learned Judge of the appellate Court as being the last Court of fact is of opinion that he has critically examined the Bainapatra and from the opposite pages of the same, it is found in naked eye that the stamps of the said Bainapatra were proved in the name of another person, whose name was removed by way and subsequently the name of Md. Yasin Ali predecessor was inserted. It has been held by the last Court of fact that the Bainapatra has been created by manipulating previous name which has been written in the opposite page of the same which appears to be tainted by fraudulent means. This view of the appellate Court has been concurred by the revisional Court. We find no scope to interfere in it. 

25. It is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceedings should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any Court of law whenever it is obtained by practicing fraud upon the Court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also well-established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceedings. Thus, the contravention of the provision of law cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand.

26. As regard possession, we find that the plaintiff-petitioners have inserted as many as four plots of land in the plaint schedule specifying the land in plot by mentioning the name of contiguous boundary men of each plot separately. The plaintiff-petitioners adduced as many as six witnesses as PWs with a view to prove their possession over the suit land. PW2, Abdul Jalil, came before the Court for proving the Bainapatra and the suit land is not known to him as it appears from his deposition. PW3, Modris Miah, deposed that he knew the suit land and that he has no land contiguous to the suit plot. In course of cross-examination, he deposed that there is land of one Sadik Miah on the northern side of a suit plot and one Nazirullah is being pos-sessed the land of southern side and one Abdul Khalek is being possessed the land contiguous to the West. PW4, Sundar Miah deposed that the defendant had been possessing the land contiguous to the suit land but plaint schedule shows otherwise. PWS, Abdul Khalek deposed that one Nazirullah possesses the land contiguous south of the suit plot and Abdul Mannan is being possessed the land eastern side of the suit plot which shows a blatant contradiction with the plaint schedule. He further deposed that the western side of the boundary of the plot number of item 3 to the plaint schedule is being possessed by one Abdul Mannan but the plaint schedule shows otherwise. PW6, Rashid Miah deposed that he is a landless co-villager and he denied the suggestion to the effect that he came to depose in lieu of money. On perusal of the aforesaid testimonies of the PWs, it appears that all the PWs have contradicted each other with a view to describe the names of boundary men and also contradicted with the boundary men as has been described in the plaint schedule. The appellate Court as being the last Court of fact observed in the following verbatim:- 
"The plaintiffs examined as many as 6 witnesses. Out of them, PW 1, Abdul Mannan is the plaintiff No.2, who admitted in his cross-examination that he filed Criminal Case No.855 of 2000, in respect of the case land and from such admission of the PW I, we can presume that the plaintiff has hopelessly failed to prove his undisturbed continuous possession for more than 12 years which is a free-condition to pass a decree on adverse possession. The most vital aspect of this case, namely, title by adverse possession, a few facts may not be lost sight of Adverse possession implies that it had commenced in wrong and is maintained against right. The plaintiff-respondents have claimed have their entry into the disputed land under a Bainapatra. So, the plaintiffs cannot claim in a decree on adverse possession as because their entry into the suit land was not wrongful." 

27. The learned Judge of the appellate Court observed that in the present case, the complicated question of title is involved and for that reason, the plaintiffs must establish their title by filing a suit for declaration of title with allied prayer. In this regard, the learned Advocate has cited and their decision enunciated in the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed-Vs-Mongla Barman and others reported in II BLD (AD) page 245, 247 (para 8) which runs as follows:- 
"In a simple suit for permanent injunction with regard to a disputed landed property, the relief is available to a person who is in possession. The Court may enquire incidentally into the respective claims of the parties to the suit for determining whether the plaintiff has got a prima facie case, i.e., whether he is in possession of the disputed property and entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. If the dispute involves complicated questions of title, the plaintiff must establish his little (title) by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. A simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing device for ascertainment of title. In this case, the plaintiff assails the presumption of the CS Khatian, a kind of exercise, the Court in a simple suit for permanent injunction should ordinarily avoid."(sic) 

28. Having considered all those facts, circumstances and evidence on record, we find that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division has made threadbare discussion in the impugned judgment and left no stone unturned in making the decision. 

29. In the light of the facts and circumstances discussed above, we do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division, which in our view does not call for any interference. 

30. Accordingly, we find no merit in the petition and the same is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 30th day of July, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos.3593 of 2004 With Civil Revision No.3670 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. These civil appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated the 30th day of July, 2009 passed by the High. Court Division in Civil Revision Nos.3593 of 2004 with Civil Revision No.3670 of 2004 discharging the Rules.

2. Three suits are disposed of together by the trial Court is Title Suit No.75 of 1996 was being filed by Nazrul Islam (herein called as plaintiffs) for declaration and partition. On the other hand, in Title Suit No.76 of 1996 filed by Bazlur Rahman Chawdhury herein this case called as defendant against Nazrul Islam and others for declaration that the Hiba-bil-ewaz deed dated 01.02.1984 is void, forged, collusive, operative and not binding upon the defendant. Title Suit No.78 of 1996 was filed by the defendant for recovery of khas possession over 5 square feet as described in the 3rd schedule of the plaint. All these three suits were tried analogously. 

3. The facts relevant for disposal of the case are that the predecessor-interest of appellant Nos.1-5 and appellant No.6 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.75 of 1996 in the First Court of the Assistant Judge, Chandina, Comilla for declaration that the judgment and order dated 06.01.1988 passed in Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case No.82 of 1985 was collusive, fraudulent, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs and also for partition stating, inter alia, that one Imam Ali was the owner of the land covering an area of 1.565 acres as described in the schedule of the plaint. Thereafter, the same was devolved upon one Delani, who sold the same to Dhirendra Nath Datta, Gobinda Chandra Saha, Zitendra Kumer Bhadra, Sunity Sudha Bhadra, Atindra Natrh Bhadra and others. Babu Dhirendra Nath Datta and others instituted Partition Suit No.64 of 1950 in the First. Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Comilla and got decree. They got saham in respect of the land described in schedule-2 to the plaint which is the subject matter of Title Suit No.75 of 1996. Zatindra Mohon and Sunity Sudha Bhadra sold .1150 acre land to defendant No.1, Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury and one Mominul Hoque. Mominul Hogue gifted his share to his father-in-law, Rowshan Ali on 15.04.1981. Rowshan Ali gifted the same to plaintiff No.1 by a deed dated 01.02.1984. Plaintiff No.1, while possessing .08 acre land, transferred .04 acre land to his wife, plaintiff No.2 by a Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed dated 11.03.1984. By this way, the plaintiffs acquired title in .0575 acre of land. They came to know that defendant No.1 had managed to get an order of pre-emption in Preemption Case No.82 of 1985 on the basis of solenama which was fraudulent one. The plaintiffs requested the defendants to effect partition of the land of the disputed Khatian but in vain; hence the suit. 

4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit con-tending, inter alia, that he instituted Miscellaneous Case No.82 of 1985 for preemption against the deed executed by Mominul Hoque in favour of Rowshan Ali. Ultimately, the said miscellaneous case for preemption was ended on compromise and this contesting defendant got the entire land of Plot No.1268 in terms of compromise. The plaintiffs have had no title and possession in the suit land. 

5. Defendant No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.76 of 1996 for declaration that the Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed dated 01.02.1984 executed by Rowshan Ali in favour of plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 was void, fraudulent, inoperative and by the said deed, he had no acquired any title in the land described in the schedule to the deed. Plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 contested Title Suit No.76 of 1996 as defendant No.1 contending that the impugned deed was genuine one. In the written statement, he narrated the story of the plaint case of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and prayed for dismissal of this suit. He also prayed for recovery of khas possession in Title Suit No.78 of 1996 in respect of third scheduled land. 

6. The learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 31.07.2002 decreed Title Suit No. 75 of 1996 and allotted saham of .0575 acre land in preliminary form and declared that the solenama dated 06.01.1988 made in Preemption Miscellaneous Case No.82 of 1985 was not binding upon the plaintiff. The learned Assistant Judge dismissed Title Suit No.76 of 1996. He also dismissed Title Suit No.76 of 1996 and Title Suit No.78 of 1996. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, defendant No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and the plaintiff of Title Suit No.76 of 1996 and Title Suit No.78of 1996 preferred Title Appeal Nos.189 of 2002 and 190 of 2002 respectively. The learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla allowed Title Appeal No.189 of 2002 upon setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.75 of 1996. The appellate Court below dismissed Title Appeal No.190 of 2002. 

8. Against the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court, the appellants (plaintiffs) filed Civil Revision Nos.3593 of 2004 and 3670 of 2004 in the High Court Division. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dis-charged both the Rules. 

9. Against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the appellants (plaintiffs) filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.2521 and 2522 of 2009 and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners: 
"Mr. Abdul Quaym, learned Senior Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the appellate Court and revisional Court misread the material evidence, particularly, the transfer deeds dated 14.01.1996, 15.04.1981 and 01.02.1984 and wrongly held that the transfer deed dated 01.02.1984 did not cover the suit land and there was no reason for the respondents to file Title Suit No.76 of 1996 for declaration against that deed. He further submits that' appellate Court and revisional Court have failed to consider that according to the admission of the defendant-respondents in solenama, the plaintiff-petitioners got .02¾  ± .04¼ = .07 acre land, for which, they were entitled to get decree for partition." 

10. Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the appellate Court and the revisional Court misread the material evidence, particularly, the transfer deeds dated 14.01.1966, 15.04.1981 and 01.02.1984 and wrongly held that the transfer deed dated 01.02.1984 did not cover the suit land and there was no reason for the respondents to file Title Suit No.76 of 1996 for declaration against the deed. He further submits that the appellate Court and the revisional Court have failed to consider that according to the admission of the defendant-respondents in sole-nama, the appellants (plaintiffs) got 
.02¾  ± .04¼ = .07 acre land, for which, they were entitled to get decree for partition. He further submits that the High Court Division manifestly erred in law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in misreading the evidence on record and failed to consider the legal and admitted facts and in basing decision on mere surmise and conjecture, since the trial Court comparing the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali as appears in the disputed solenama found that the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali does not tally with other admitted signatures of Md. Rowshan Ali and accordingly having decreed Title Suit No.75 of 1996, the appellate Court without comparing with the signature committed error in allowing the appeal, considering the certified copies of the applicants and Haziras filed by Md. Rowshan Ali in Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and holding that if the solenama, Haziras and the applications filed in the said case are genuine, the solenama cannot be a forged one without comparing the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali. He further submits that the High Court Division has misread, misconstrued and misunderstood the materials on record and consequently failed to comprehend the facts of the case and misapplied the law, since the written statement of Bazlur Rahman in Title Suit No.75 of 1996 to the effect that he got constructed of the wall in between the boundary of the land of the plaintiff and the defendant having some partition out of 1½ decimals land, he got by disputed compromise, it demonstrates that the said compromise was not acted upon and the appellate Court committed error in allowing the appeal without considering this aspect of the case. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances of the case in its true perspective, as a result of which, there has been serious miscarriage of justice, since after making the gift by Md. Rowshan Ali had no locus standi or authority to compromise the pre-emption case and the trial Court having considered this aspect of the case, rightly decreed the suit, but the appellate Court illegally held that the said gift dated 01.02.1984 has not been acted upon. He further submits that the High Court Division overlooked that the appellate Court committed error of law in allowing the appeal without considering that the defendant admitted that he got .01½ acre land by solenama and by amicable partition out of .0575 acre land and the plain-tiff got the rest of the suit land and is in possession of the same by constructing dwelling house thereon and Title Suit No.76 of 1996 filed by the defendant, Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury for recovery of khas possession also provided that the solenama was not acted upon. He further submits that the High Court Division filed to consider that the appellate Court committed error of law in holding that Md. Rowshan Ali executed the solenama and relinquished his right, title and interest over Suit Plot No. 1268 without considering that Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case No.82 of 1985 was filed by the petitioner as a 2nd class co-sharer against another 2nd class co-sharer, long after the period of limitation without making party to the present plaintiff who got the suit land by way of gift long before filing of the said pre-emption case. He finally submits that the High Court Division failed to reflect that the appellate Court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in finding that the plaintiff could not prove his possession without discussing of the evidence and materials on record, particularly, the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land. 

11. Mr. M. Qumrul Hoque Siddique, learned Counsel, appearing for respondent Nos.1(Ka)-1(Uma) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He contends that the appellants' predecessor admitted through compromise petition that their predecessor, Md. Rowshan Ali, got 20 decimals land from Plot No.1268 which has been separated from, the land of Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury by boundary wall and the appellants herein are totally stopped to claim any land out of 20 decimals land from Plot No.1268. He further contends that the appellate Court below and the High Court Division considered all the materials on record in their true perspective and as such, the instant appeals are liable to be dismissed. He further contends that the appellate Court below clearly found and observed that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 miserably failed to prove that the compromise petition was fraudulent and product of forgery. He lastly contends that as the plaintiff-appellants admitted the right, title, interest and possession of Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury through compromise petition in preemption case and as such, the claim of the appellants is barred by estoppels and acquiescence. 

12. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. 

13. It is admitted by the parties that one Bazlur Rahman and Mominul Haque acquired .11½  acre land from Zatindra Kumar Bhadra and Sunity Sudha Bhadra by a kabala dated 15.01.1964. 

14. The plaintiff-appellants have come with an allegation that their predecessor, Md. Rowshan Ali acquired the suit land from Mominul Haque by a deed of gift dated 15.04.1981. Defendant-respondent No.1 filed a pre-emption case being No.82 of 1985 against aforesaid Md. Rawson Ali treating the deed of gift as a kabala deed. 

15. The defendant-respondents have denied the claim of the plaintiff- appellants and counter claimed that aforesaid Md. Rowshan Ali executed a solenama in favour of defendant No.1 and as a result of which, the preemption case has been allowed in favour of defendant No.1 who claimed the entire land of Plot No.1268. But present plaintiff-appellants instituted a title suit being No.82 of 1958 seeking a declaration to the effect that the aforesaid solenama is forged, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon them and also prayed for cancellation of pre-emption order and also for effecting partition. 

16. Now, the issue that falls for determination is whether the aforementioned solenama was forged, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff-appellants. 

17. The plaintiff (in Title Suit No. 75 of 1996), Mohammed Nazrul Islam while deposing as PW 1 stated that his father, Md. Rowshan Ali never executed such solenama and the same is forged, fraudulent and collusive which has been created by using his father's name. He also deposed that his father, Md. Rawson All gifted out the suit land in his favour on 01.02.1984 and thereafter, it is not possible on his part to execute solenama in the year 1985 in pre-emption case being No.82 of 1985. PW2, Abu Tahir also corroborated PW 1 , on deposing that Md. Rowshan Ali gifted out the suit land in favour of his son, Nazrul Islam. 

18. One the other hand, DW1, Bazrul Rahman Chowdhury deposed that the father of plaintiff-appellant, Md. Rowshan Ali entered in appearance in pre-emption case being No.82 of 1985 through Advocate Younus Khan. But the pre-emption case being No.82 of 1985 has been disposed of exparte earlier against which Md. Rowshan Ali filed a Misc. case under Order IX, rule 13 wherein Md. Rowshan Ali filed a solenama and the basis of the such solenama, the Misc. Case (under Order IX, rule 13 C.P.C) has been allowed and the said Misc. case has been restored to its file and number and thereafter, the pre-emption case has been allowed in terms of the solenarna. He finally deposed that Md. Rowshan Ali himself appeared through his learned Advocate and there is no scope to declare such sole degree as being fraudulent collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff-appellants. We have called for lower Court record and the record of the Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case No.82 of 1985 from Comilla Judge Court. We have compared the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali put on the solenama and the signatures put on his written objection, signatures put on the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code as well as signature on Vokalatnama. We have performed a comparative study in between those signatures of Md. Rowahan Ali. It revealed that the signature put on solenama and that have been put on all other papers as stated above are not identical and same. Section 73 of the Evidence Act empowers the Court to compare the disputed signature of a person with signature which have been admitted or proved to the satisfaction of the Court to have been made by the signatory. A Court may rely upon its own comparison of the signature unaided by expert evidence. A reference may be made from a decision enunciated in the case of Kutubuddin Vs. Aftab Ali in 13 BLC page 782 wherein it has been held that:-
"On a careful examination of those signatures side by side it appears that the admitted signatures of defendant No.1 as contained in the Exhibit 'Ka' and that in the deposition sheet if be compared with those as containing in Exhibits 5 and 6 series those signatures of Exhibits 5 and 6 series appear to be not the product of the handwriting of defendant No.1. In view of the above, it is held that Exhibits 5 and 6 series were not executed by the defendant No. 1." 

19. We find that the aforesaid case law is identical with our present one. 

20. It further reveals from the order sheets of the record of Misc. Preemption Case No.82 of 1985 that on 02.02.1988 the Court fixed a date on 02.02.1988 for hearing a petition filed on 31.12.1987 and on 03.01.1988 the parties filed joint petition for shifting back the date of the case and on that day, the pre-emption case has been allowed on the basis of solename after making an order of shifting back the date. On perusal of the order, it appears that the Court was on hurry in passing such order sheet of this order which appears to be unusual and very much suspicious. It is true that a revision was pending before the High Court Division at the time of passing aforesaid order. The trial Court on perusal of this record has arrived at a decision on the following verbatim:  
“ইহা স্বীকৃত যে, এ সময়ে রোশন আলী অসুস্থ্য ছিলেন। উক্ত ছোলেনামার মাত্র ১৫ দিনের মাথায় রোশন আলী মারা যায়। এমতাবস্থায় উক্ত ছোলেনামা দাখিলের জন্য বা আদেশ তাড়াতাড়ী হওয়ার জন্য তাড়াহুড়া করার কোন যৌক্তিকতা আত্রাদালতে দেখিতে পায় নাই। যেহেতু উক্ত pre-emption মোকদ্দমা নিয়া মহামান্য হাইকোর্টে রিভিশন হওয়ার পর হঠাৎ করিয়া কারো পক্ষে এইরূপ ছোলেনামা দাখিলের ত্র্রে সন্দেহের অবকাশ রহিয়াছে কেননা ছোলেনামা দাখিলী স্বার ও অন্যান্য স্থানে প্রদত্ত স্বাক্ষর এক নহে মর্মে খালি চোখেই দৃশ্যমান। date না থাকা স্বত্বেও এগিয়ে নিয়ে এসে ০৬/০১/১৯৮৮ ই তাং ছণালেনামা দাখিল হয় এবং আংশিক ছোলেনামা প্রদত্ত হয়। তাহাতে ৩(তিন) শতক ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমার ১নং বিবাদী ও রোশন আলী । ২(দুই) শতকের একটু বেশী প্রাপ্ত হয়। ১নং বিবাদী জেরায় স্বীকার করেন যে, ৩(তিন) শতক পাইলেও .০১ ১/২ শতকে দখল নেন। জেরায় তিনি আরণে বলেন যে, ১৯৬৯ সনে সীমানা দেওয়াল করেন। তাহা হইলে প্রশ্ন উঠা স্বাভাবিক যে, প্রিয়েমশান মূলে .০১ ১/২ শতকের দখল কিভাবে নিলেন স্বাস্থ্য পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, কবির উদ্দন সাহেব ও ওয়াহেদ কমিশনায় সাহেব ৩/৪ দিন যাবৎ পরিমাপ করিয়া দেন এবং সীমানা দেওয়াল বহাল আছে মর্মে রিপোর্ট দেন। ইহার অর্থ ১নং বিবাদী পূর্বেই ১ ১/২ শতক দখল নিয়াছিল। ১নং বিবাদী দাবী করেন যে, বাদী উক্ত .০১ ১/২ শতক বাদ দিয়া বন্টনের ডিক্রী পাইতে পারে। ৭৬/১৯৯৬ ইং মোকদ্দমায় বাদী তথা ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমার ১নং বিবাদী নিঃস্বতৃবান তৃতীয় ব্যক্তি হিসাবে ০১/০২/১৯৮৪ইং তারিখের দলিলের বৈধতা Challenge করিয়াছেন যাহা ইতিপূর্বে বিস্তারিত আলোকপাত করিয়াছি। এমতাবস্থায় ৭৬/১৯৯৬নং সিদ্ধান্ত হইল ।”

21. On performing a comparative studz in between the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali on solenama and his actual signature put on vokalatnama, W/O etc, we found a glaring inconsistency in between the two signatures. We also find from that record that Md. Rowshan Ali was sick at the time of putting such signature on solenama. It is also evident that Md. Rowshan Ali had died soon after 15 days after submission of such solenama. When any document like solenama is executed by an age old and sick person burden lies on the person who claims benefit under the document to establish that the document was executed by him on his own accord. Independent advice in case of execution of such document by such type of old and sick person is insisted when the document stands in a fiduciary relationship with such person. It appears that the beneficiary of the sole-decree is the defendant who has adduced only one witness. Thus, it stands that the there is no corroborating witness so as to prove the fact that there was disinterested Adviser for Md. Rawson Ali understand the contents of solenama. Thus, the defendant-respondents failed to prove that they complied all the formalities with a view to obtain fair and legal sole-decree. Hence, we find that there are ingredients of fraudulent activity in obtaining such sole-decree. 

22. The High Court Division over looked that the appellate Court committed error of law in allowing the appeal without considering that the defendant admitted that the he got .011/2 acre land by solenama and by amicable partition out of .0575 acre' land and the plaintiff got the rest of the suit land and is in possession of the same by constructing dwelling house thereon and Title suit No.78 of 1996 was filed by defendant, Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury for recovery of khas possession also proved that the solenama was not acted upon. The learned Judge of the High Court Division committed a grave error of law occasioning failure of justice in not finding that the trial Court, on consideration of the evidence and materials on record, having decreed the suit in Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and dismissed Title Suit No.76 of 1996 and Title Suit No.78 of 1996. The learned appellate Court committed error in law in allowing the appeal without reversing all the findings of the trial Court. 

23. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court failed to properly weigh and assess the finding of the learned trial which runs as follows: - 
“প্রোক্ত আলোচনা পর্যালোচনার ধারাবাহিকতায় বলা যায়। যে। যেহেতু ৭৫/১৯৯৬ ইং মোকদ্বমার বাদীপ মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা তাহার মোকদ্দমা বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে রনীয় মর্মে প্রমান করিতে পারিয়াছে সেহেতু বাদীপক্ষ তাহার প্রার্থীত মতে প্রতিকার পাইতে আইনগতঃ ও ন্যায়তঃ হকদার বটে। এবং যেহেতু ০৬/০১/১৯৮৮ইং বাদীপক্ষ তাহার উপর বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে ঘোষনা মূলক ডিত্রীর প্রার্থনা করিয়াছেন এবং ১নং বিবাদী উক্ত ছোলেনাম সাঠিক মর্মে মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা যথাযথ আছে প্রমান করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছেন সেহেতু বাদীপ তাহার প্রার্থীত মতে প্রতিকার পাইতে পারেন মর্মে আমি মনে করি। অপর দিকে ৭৬/১৯৯৬ইং ও ৭৮/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমায় বাদী পক্ষ তথা ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং মণাকদ্দমার ১নং বিবাদী তাহার দায়েরকৃত মোকদ্দমায় মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা প্রমান করতে সম হন নাই বিধায় আইনতঃ ও ন্যায়তঃ কোন প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার নহেন। এমতাবস্থায় সকল বিচার্য বিষয় গুলি ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদী পরে অনুকূলে এবং ৭৬/১৯৯৬ইং ও ৭৮/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমায় বাদী পরে প্রতিকুলে নিস্পত্তি করা হইল। ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদী পরে মোকদ্দমা আইনত ও ন্যায়তঃ রনীয় ৭৬/১৯৯৬ইং ও ৭৮/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমার বর্তমান আকার ও প্রকারে রক্ষনীয় নহে, এমতাবস্থায় ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমার বাদীপ তাহার প্রার্থীত মতে প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে । ৭৫/১৯৯৬ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদী পক্ষের মোকদ্মা প্রমাণিত ।”

24. We have observed that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division failed to consider that the appellate Court committed error of law in holding that Md. Rowshan Ali executed the solenama and relinquished his right, title and interest over Suit Plot No. 1268 without considering that Misc. Pre-emption Case No. 82 of 1985 was filed by the defendant-respondents as a second class co-sharer against another second class co-sharer long after the period of limitation without making party to the present plaintiff-appellants who got the suit land by way of gift long before filing the said pre-emption case. Thus, it appears that the pre-emption case being No.82 of 1985 was not only barred by limitation but also not binding upon the present plaintiff-appellant. Over and above, the learned Judge of the High Court Division failed to consider that after executing the deed of gift by Md. Rowshan Ali in favour of Nazral Islam, Md. Rowshan Ali has no locus standi stand or authority to compromise the pre-emption case. Rather the trial Court having considered this aspect of the case rightly decreed this suit. On the other hand, the appellate Court abruptly opined that the said gift deed dated 01.02.1984 has not been acted upon which is mere mis-appreciation and non-reading of the evidence on record. Not only that, the plaintiff-appellant has been able to prove his pre-emption case over the suit land. We find no cogent, corroborated and unimpeachable evidence from the defence corner (respondent) so as to hold that the Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed dated 01.02.1984 in favour of the plaintiff executed by Rowshan Ali was void, fraudulent and inoperative. Thus, the Title Suit being No.76 of 1996 is liable to be dismissed. 

25. We hold the view that the finding of the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court below are shockingly perverse and those are vitiated by non-reading of the material evidence and misconstruction of any evidence on record affecting the merit of the cases. Thus, it appears that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division without assessing the evidence on record arrived at a wrong decision and thereby affirmed the finding of the appellate Court below which is liable to be set aside. 

26. Accordingly, we find merit in the appeal. Thus, the appeal is allowed with-out any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and order delivered by the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division as well as the judgment of the appellate Court below are set aside and the judgment and order passed by the trial Court is restored. 

End.
