case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated the 30th day of May, 2018 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4520 of 2016)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated the 30th day of May, 2018 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4520 of 2016 making the Rule absolute. 

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the petitioner and others as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.58 of 2012 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bancharampur, Brahmanbaria for permanent injunction stating, inter alia, that one Gazi Mamud sold out 15 decimals land out of 31 decimals land of CS Plot No.846 to one Kamar Uddin, father of Abdul Awal before 40 years. After two years, said Abdul Awal sold out that land to one Yusuf Ali and others and handed over the possession, but no registered deed was executed between them. Subsequently, afore-said Gazi Marnud, Abdul Awal, Dhanu Miah, Yusuf Ali and Momen Miah died leaving behind their respective heirs. The plaintiffs as heirs of Yusuf Ali are in possession in the suit land. The defendants had no title and possession over the suit land. Subsequently, the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from the heirs of Gazi Mamud vide three separate registered deeds being No.2304, 2305, 2306 dated 03.04.2012 respectively. On 20.04.2012, Defendant Nos.3-7 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land; hence the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos.1-2 and 4 contested the suit by 'filing a written statement denying all allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Gazi Mamud, who sold out 15 decimals land out of 31 decimals land to Abdul Awal, father of defendant Nos.1 and 2 and grandfather of defendant No.4 vide registered deed No.1431 dated 12.02.1969. Thereafter, Abdul Awal died leaving behind his heirs defendant Nos.1 and 2 and one daughter, Sufia Khatun who got the possession of the suit land by way of amicable partition. Subsequently, defendant Nos.1 and 2 extended their homestead by way of cutting earth from the suit land. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession over the suit land as such, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. The learned trial Court framed three issues for disposal of the suit. The plaintiffs side adduced 6(six) witnesses as PWs and the defendants side adduced 3(three) witnesses as DWs. 

5. After concluding trial, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bancharampur, Brahmanbaria decreed the suit by his judgment and decree on 30.10.2014. 6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 30.10.2014, the defendants as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.56 of 2015 before the learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria who dismissed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 05.10.2016. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 05.10.2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria, the defendants as petitioners moved before the High Court Division and the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. Hence, plaintiffs as present-petitioners filed this civil petition for leave to appeal. 

8. Mr. Md. Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and order dated 30.05.2018 passed by the High Court Division is bad in law and fact. He further submits that the findings and decision taken by the High Court Division in passing the impugned judgment and order is based on surmises, conjectures and extraneous circumstances for which the said findings are liable to be struck down. He further submits that the learned Judge of Single Bench of the High Court Division committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in making the Rule absolute and setting aside the impugned judgments and decrees of the Courts below based on concurrent findings of fact. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division failed to appreciate that a revisional Court acts beyond its jurisdiction in setting aside the concurrent findings of facts, when there is no misreading and mis-appreciation of the evidence on record. He further submits that the High Court Division miserably failed to consider the cogent and categorical findings of both the trial Court and the appellate Court below. He finally submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in not taking into consideration the fact that the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction cannot enter into the question of fact or otherwise of the reliance on the evidence of the witnesses by the Courts below, if it is found that the Courts below duly considered and analyzed the evidence adduced by the parties.

9. Mr. SK. Md. Morshed, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent Nos.1-2 and 6 supported the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division, but none appeared for other respondents. He further submits that the petitioner plaintiff has got no prima facie and arguable case to obtain an order of permanent injunction and as such the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division is very much justified in making the rule absolute. 

10. We have heard the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused the materials on record. 

11. Admittedly, the suit land originally belongs to one Gazi Mahamud. 

12. The plaintiffs have come with an allegation that one Abdul Awal purchased the land from Gazi Mahamud and thereafter their predecessor Yusuf Ali, Dhanu Miah and Momin Miah purchased such land from Abdul Awal but there is no registered kabala for such purchase. It has been also claimed that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land exclusively since their acquisition and as such, they prayed for an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant so that they can-not disturb their exclusive possession. 

13. On the other hand, contesting-defendant Nos.1, 2 and 4 denied the aforesaid contention of the plaintiffs and counter claim that Gazi Mahamud sold out .15 acre land to Abdul Awal who died leaving behind two sons, defendant Nos.1 and 2 and one daughter named Sufia Khatoon and aforesaid heirs of Abdul Awal have been possessing the suit land since acquisition and extended their homestead by way of cutting earth from the suit land. It has been further alleged that their predecessor, Abdul Awal never sold the suit land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs and there is no registered instrument of such transfer and as such, the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession over the suit land as alleged and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

14. The crux of the case is whether there was any fransfer by Abdul Awal in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. In this respect, plaintiff Shafiqul Islam while deposing as PW1 clearly stated that there is no registered deed of transfer by Abdul Awal in favour of their predecessor and that it was an oral transfer. In course of cross examination, he stated that at the time of such transfer, he was a student of class seven. He further deposed that Gazi Mahmud transferred the suit land in the year 1969. He further deposed that he is now 54 years old. Thus, it stands that he was born in the year 1959 and on calculation, it appears that he was a boy of 10 years at the time of such oral transfer. It also appears to us that a boy of 10 years cannot be a student of class seven. Hence, there are intrinsic weaknesses and inherent infirmity in his evidence. Excepting PW1, the plaintiff-petitioner adduced no other witness with a view to prove the alleged fact of oral transfer. Over and above, as per provision of section 54 of Transfer of Property Act, an oral transfer cannot be a valid mode of transfer of land. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that the alleged transfer was not effected by registered instrument because the valuation of the suit land is less than 100/- taka. In this respect the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent has cited a decision in the case of Gulshan-Vs- Ameer Ali reported in PLD 1997 (Kar) page 292 wherein it has been held that: "Mere agreement to sell would not confer any right, title or ownership inasmuch as any transaction of sale in respect of immovable property worth Taka 100 or upward was required to be compulsorily registered-Suit on basis of title, therefore, was not maintainable." 

15. The plaintiffs further have come with an allegation that they have purchased the suit land from the heirs of Gazi Mahamud by dint of three kabalas. But it is admitted by the plaintiffs that Gazi Mahamud sold the suit land to one Kamar Uddin 40 years back who died leaving behind only son in Abdul Awal. It is admitted by both the parties that Gazi Mahamud sold the suit land to the predecessor of the defendants. Thus, we find that the heirs of Gazi Mahamud or his heirs had no saleable interest at the time of creation of three kabalas in favour of the plaintiffs. Thus, those three kabalas appear to be paper transaction which created no title in favour of the plaintiffs. Having considered the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, we find that the plaintiff-petitioner has no prima facie title and arguable case with a view to obtain an order of perpetual injunction.

16. This is a suit for permanent injunction. In such suit, the Court may enquire incidentally into the respective claims of the fact for determining whether the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property and entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. It is now well established by the consistent decisions of our apex Court that a suit for permanent injunction is maintainable where the plaintiff has been able to prove his exclusive possession in the suit property even though he may not have prima-facie title thereto. 

17. Let us proceed to examine the evidence of record and see therefrom as to how far the petitioner-plaintiff has been able to prove the exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property. 

18. PW1 Shafiqul Islam deposed that the predecessor of the plaintiffs got possession of the suit land in the year 1975. But he cannot say as to what was the actual date and month of getting such possession. He also admits that their predecessor never paid any rent for such land. PW2 deposed that he never went to the suit land. PW3 Abdul Mazid deposed that he is a man of 65 (sixty-five) years and he saw the predecessor of the plaintiffs to grow tobacco in the suit land at his age of 10/12 years. On calculation of his age, it appears to us that PW3 was born in the year 1948 and he saw the predecessor of the plain-tiffs to grow tobacco from the year 1958/1960. Whereas PW I deposed that their predecessor was inducted into possession of the suit land in the year 1975. PW4 Dhanesh Miah deposed that he knew the suit land but he never saw anybody to grow tobacco in the same. PW5 Sudhan Miah has contradicted with plaint in respect of naming the boundary men as has been described in the plaint. Thus, we find that the testimonies of the PWs are impeachable and full of contradictions. The facts and circumstances and evidence on record lead us to hold that the plaintiffs hopelessly failed to prove their exclusive possession over the suit land. Thus, the learned Judge of the High Court Division rightly appreciated the evidence on record and thereby set aside the concurrent findings of facts since there is apparent non- consideration and mis-appreciation of the evidence on record. 

19. On the other hand, DWI Alauddin deposed that their predecessor Abdul Awal acquired the suit land measuring .15 acre by dint of a kabala and as owner in possession of such land he died leaving behind defendant Nos.1 and 2 and a daughter Sufia and that they have been possessing the land peacefully since their acquisition. DW2 Shaheen corroborated DW1 in respect of their possession. We find that those statements of the DWs were not shaken during the course of their cross-examination. Thus, they are able to earn the confidence of the court. In such a state of affairs, we find that the balance of convenience and in convenience is in favour of the defendants. 

20. It is well settled that a plaintiff even though has no prima facie title may maintain a suit for permanent injunction if he can prove his exclusive possession over the suit property. In the instant case, the main question before us is whether the plaintiff-petitioner has succeeded in proving the plaintiffs' exclusive possession over the suit land. It appears that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division has entered into the factual aspect of the case regarding possession and after thorough consideration of the same, came to the finding that the plaintiffs have not succeeded in proving their exclusive possession and disagreed with the finding of the Courts below. We have already seen that in a simple suit for permanent injunction with regard to a disputed landed property, the relief is available to a person who is in possession. 

21. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondents further cited a decision enunciated in the case of Aktar Hossain and others-Vs-Shamsuddin Moulvi and other reported in 8BLC (AD) page 72 wherein it has been held that :-
"The suit for permanent injunction is essentially a suit for possession. Though the title may be incidentally gone into but in a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed question of title except the extent, as it would help in finding which of the parties has possession. Plaintiff has failed to bring home their possession in the suit land for a decree for a permanent injunction." 

22. From the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record, it appears that the plaintiff-petitioner was neither able to prove prima facie title nor the plaintiffs' possession. 

23. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division was very much justified in making the Rule absolute and thereby set aside the concurrent decision of the Courts below since there is misreading of evidence on record and non-consideration of material evidence affecting the merit of the case. 

24. Thus, we do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and accordingly, we find no merit in the petition and the same is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.541 of 2018
lawyer:
Mr Md. Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
For the Respondents -------- None represented
parties:
Md. Atiar Rahman and another ------- Petitioners
-Vs-
Most. Rabeya Khatun and others ------- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 18th day of July, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.858 of 2015)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated the 18th day of July, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.858 of 2015 discharging the Rule. 

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the respondents herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No.131 of 2001 in the Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Kushtia for declaration of title in the disputed property stating, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to Mouza-Mozompur under S.A. Khatian No.259 corresponding to Plot No.369 comprising an area of .37 acre land originally belonged to defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, in two annas share and defendant No.1, Atiar Rahman in 14 annas share. Defendant No.1 was the minor son of defendant No.2 and for his welfare, for want of money defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, herself and as natural guardian, mother of the minor son, defendant No.1 on 30.06.1969 A.D. transferred .0825 acre land in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor by a sub-kabala deed dated 30.06.1969 being No.8077. The possession of the transferred land was handed over by the vendor in favour of the purchaser and after purchase, the predecessor of the plaintiffs possessed that land and paid rent after mutation for more than 12 (twelve) years. The predecessor of the plaintiff, Sarwar Hossain's name has been correctly recorded against the suit land in the present RS record. In RS Plot No.4132, the suit land measuring .0831 acre was recorded primarily in the name of Sarwar Hossain, but subsequently defendant No.1 filed Other Class Suit No.69 of 1987 against Sarwar Hossain and others in respect of the entire land of suit of S.A. Khatian challenging the transfer deed in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor, Sarwar Hossain, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kushtia. The suit was dismissed on contest and against that dis-missal decree, defendant No.1 filed an Other Appeal No.219 of 1987 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia. After hearing, the appeal was dismissed affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and in this manner, the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs to the suit land remained intact. The further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant Nos.1 and 2 in collusion with the settlement officials including the suit land measuring .0825 acre along with .37 acre in SA Plot No.369 with other lands pre-pared a collusive RS Khatian in the name of defendant No. 1. On the basis of that wrong collusive RS record, the defendants on 26.01.2001 denied the title of the plain-tiffs' which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for declaration of their title. 

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant No.1 is that defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, for the welfare of her minor son, defendant No.1, did not execute and register any transfer deed in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs on 30.06.1969 in respect of the suit land measuring .0825 acre. The further case of the defendants is that the deed in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor in respect of the suit land is without consideration, collusive, forged and not acted upon. On the basis of that sub-kabala deed, neither the predecessor of the plaintiffs nor the plain-tiffs acquired any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs' suit is barred by limitation and on the basis of false allegations, they have filed the instant suit. 

4. The trial Court during trial of the suit after examining two witnesses from the side of the plaintiffs and two witnesses from the side of the defendants dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 19.05.2013. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.52 of 2013 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia which was transmitted to the 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Kushtia who after hearing the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 18.01.2015 allowed the same. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below, the defendant-petitioners filed Civil Revision No.858 of 2015 before the Court Division and the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division discharged the Rule. 

7. Against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the defendant-petitioners filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal seeking leave before this Division. 

8. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the plaintiffs claimed that defendant No.1 was the minor and during his minority, his land was sold by his mother, defendant No.2. He adds that mother is a de facto guardian, so the transfer made by de facto guardian is void. He further submits that defendant Nos.1 and 2 have been in possession over the suit land and the SA record was correctly prepared in their names on the basis of the possession, so the instant suit for mere declaration of title cannot be maintainable with-out seeking for recovery of possession. But the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division without discussing this vital issue decreed the suit and thereby committed error of law. He further submits that the plaintiff claimed 0.0831 acre land out of 0.037 acre which is unspecified and indefinite. In a suit for declaration of title without specifying the suit land is not maintainable and as such, the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit. He finally submits that the plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree, but in the instant case, the plaintiff failed to prove his case. 9. No one appeared on behalf of the respondents to support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

10. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners and perused the materials on record. 

11. It is admitted by the parties that the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint originally belongs to defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa to the extent of 2 annas share and defendant No.1, Ataiar Rahman to the extent of 14 annas share. The respondents as plaintiffs have come with allegation that defendant No.1, Atiar Rahman, was a minor son of defendant No.2 who as natural guarding-mother of the minor son for want of money had transfer .0825 acre land in favour of plaintiff-predecessor by Sub-Kabala dated 30.06.1969 being No. 8077 and since then the plaintiff-predecessor has been possessing the same for more than 12 years. It has been further alleged that the suit land was recorded primarily in the name of predecessor of plaintiff, namely, Sarowar Hossain, but subsequently defendant No.1 filed Title Suit No.69 of 1987 against Sarowar Hossain and others challenging the transfer deed in Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kushtia and the suit was dismissed on contest and thereafter, the plaintiff of that suit (defendant No.1) filed Title Appeal No.219 of 1987 which was dismissed subsequently and as a result of which the right title interest of the present plaintiff remained intact. Finally, the plaintiff alleged that defendant Nos.1 and 2 in collusion with the settlement official were able to record their names fraudulently and on the basis of such wrong record, they denied the title of the plaintiff. 

12. On the other hand, the contesting defendant denied the aforesaid contention of the respondent-plaintiff and counter claimed that the deed in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor in respect of suit land is without consideration, collusive, forged and not-acted upon and on the basis of which neither the plaintiff nor his predecessor acquired any right, title, interest and possession of the suit land and that the suit is barred by limitation. 

13. At the very outset, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner-defendant assailed the plaintiffs predecessor kabala dated 30.06.1969 on arguing that a mother is a delacto guardian who has no authority to sell out any property of the minor without obtaining any permission from the District Judge and as such, this type of transfer is void in the eye of law. In this respect, a decision may be mentioned which has been enunciated in the case of Kashem Mollah-Vs-Fajel Shek and others reported in 3DLR page 306 wherein it has been held as follows: 
"A minor, whose property has been sold by his mother during his minority need not aside the sale which is void, but he can institute a suit for possession within 12 years from the date of the sale or within three years from the date of his attainment of majority whichever may be the later date. If the suit is not so instituted his title in the property would be extinguished under section 28 of the Limitation Act and the subsequent suit would be barred by limitation". 

14. From the aforementioned enunciation, it appears that the present suit is barred by the provision of article 28 of the Limitation Act. 

15. Apart from that we find, in respect of the suit of the property, Title Suit No.69 of 1987 was instituted by the defendant-respondents claiming his right, title, interest and possession. In respect of that suit, there is a certified copy of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.69 of 1987 which has been marked as Exhibit-8 by the trial Court. That suit was filed by the defendant-respondents in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kushtia and after holding trial, the learned trial Court dismissed the suit on finding that there is no right, title, interest and possession of the present respondent-defendants in the suit property. A Title Appeal being No.219 of 1987 was preferred against that judgment and decree of dismissal from the side of the present defendant-respondent-petitioners as it appears from Exhibit-9. That appeal was heard and disposed of by the then Sub-ordinate Judge who disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and dis-missal decree passed by the trial Court. After disposal of such appeal, none challenged such judgment and decree in the High Court Division in a revisional forum. The learned appellate Court below in the instant case, has rightly held that the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal being No. 219 of 1987 have got its every binding force upon the parties concerned. 

16. In this respect, plaintiff No.9 while deposing as PW1 stated that the suit land appertaining to Mouza Mozampur under S.A Khatian No.259 originally belong to defendant Nos.1 and 2 and defendant No.2 is the minor son of defendant No.1 who for the purpose of maintaining his minor son (defendant No.2) sold out the suit property measuring .0825 acre in favour of his father on 30.06.1969. He further depoed that soon after such transfer, his father got possession in such land and paid rent after mutating his name in suit Khatian. PW1 further stated that Title Suit being No.69 of 1987 was filed against their predecessor's title document, i.e. Kabala deed No.8077 dated 30.06.1969 by the defendant, but they lost the same up to Appellate Court. During his course of examination, plaintiff No.9 produced their deed dated 30.06.1969, copy of R.S. Khatian No.330, rent receipt showing payment of rent, the DCR, copy of math porcha, copy of S.A Khatian No.259 along with the certified copy of judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.69 of 1987 and Title Appeal No.219 of 1987. All those documents were produced and being marked as exhibits in course of his examination. Waliur Rahman, PW2, deposed that he is the contagious land holder of the suit property and the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property for long term by erecting boundary wall. During his course of cross examination the aforementioned testimonies of the PWs were not shaken in any manner. On perusal of those evidence on record, we find that there is no intrinsic weakness and inherent infirmity in those testimonies. Thus, we are not in a position to disbelieve them. 

17. On the other hand, defendant No.2 as DW1 admitted in his cross examination that after the second marriage of his mother, they went to the house of his step father in the village-Bhadali which is 8 kilometers away from the suit land and used to live there permanently. In course of his cross-examination, he failed to identify the suit land properly. Al Mamun Biswas, DW2, also deposed that he cannot say as to whether the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land since 1969. Thus, it cannot be said that the testimonies of the DWs are unimpeachable. 

18. The revisional Court after appreciating the evidence and other materials on record have come to a concurred decision with the Appellate Court below who is the last and final Court of fact in the following verbatim: 
"The principle of law as spelt out earlier makes it clear that the appellate court below during disposal of her appeal committed no such illegality or infirmity by dint of which it can be held that there has been any misreading or non-reading of evidence or that there was non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with". 

19. Having gone through the aforementioned state of affairs, we are also inclined to hold that the learned Judge of the Appellate Court below as final court of fact on preponderance of the evidence on record arrived at a conclusive decision that the present respondent (plaintiff) has got right title interest and possession over the suit land. 

20. It is settled principle that a court of revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure can interfere with the finding of fact, as a final Court of facts, only in exceptional circumstances when the findings are shockingly perverse or those are vitiated by non-reading of the material evidence or misconstruction of any important documents affecting the merit of the suit. But in the instant case, we find that the Appellate Court below has made a threadbare discussion and left no stone unturned where from it can be said that there are rooms for mis-appreciation or misreading or any scope to non-consider the material evidence on record. 

21. In view of the above discussion and finding of the Courts below, we find no illegality and infirmity in those judgments. 

22. Accordingly, we find no merit in this civil petition and as such, the same is dis-missed. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 3137-3139 of 2013
lawyer:
Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, Advocate instructed by Mr Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioners (In all the cases) 
Mr Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate with Mr Probir Neogi, Advocate instructed by Mr Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Respondents (In all the cases)
parties:
Md. Harun-Ur-Rashid and others ------ Petitioners (in all the cases)
-Vs-
Md. Sirajul Islam and others ------ Respondents (In all the cases)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 10.07.2013 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1216 of 1999 along with Civil Revision Nos.1217 of 1999 and 1218 of 1999.)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J. All these 3(three) Civil Petitions) for Leave to Appeal have been directed against the same analogous judgment and order dated 10.07.2013 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1216 of 1999 along with Civil Revision Nos.1217 of 1999 and 1218 of 1999 and as such all these 3(three) Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal have been heard analogously and this single judgment will dispose of all these 3(three) Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal. 

2. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of these Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal, in short, are as follows; 

3. The respondent Md. Sirajul Islam in these 3 Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal, as plaintiff, filed Title Suit No.134 of 1996 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.9.9 of 1997 in the Court of, the Assistant Judge, Nababgonj against the present leave-petitioners Md. Harun-Ur-Rashid and others and also the defendant-respondent Nos.2- 5 herein for permanent injunction. The leave-petitioners Md. Heron-Ur-Rashid and others also, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit Nos.100 of 1997 and 101 of 1997 against Md. Sirajul Islam (the plaintiff of Title Suit No.99 of 1997). The Title Suit No.100 of 1997 was for declaration of title and the Title Suit No.101 of 1.997 was for a declaration that the judgment and decree dated 21.10.1995 passed in Title Suit No.254 of 1994 was fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

4. The case of the plaintiff of Title Suit No.99 of 1997 (present-respondent No.1, Md. Sirajul Islam), in short, was that the suit land originally belonged to Khoda Boksha in 8 annas share and Sheikh Kalu and Sheikh Malu in 4 annas share each. Sheikh Malu died leaving behind 2 sons, Newazuddin and Mainuddin and 2 daughters Guljan and Nazibun Nessa. Thereafter, Newazuddin died leaving behind only son Romizuddin and a wife Keti Bibi. On 08.12.1966 Nazibun Nessa sold her 1.75 acres of land in favour of Keti Bibi. Thus: Keti Bibi and Romizuddin, by inheritance and by purchase, acquired 1.51 -acres of land from plot No.2721 and 2.31 acres of land from plot No.2792 and possessed that land exclusively by amicable partition. Romizuddin and Keti Bibi sold .8250 acre of land from plot No.2721 in favour of Zayeda Begum by kabala dated 19.02.1968 and since purchase, Zayeda Begum had been possessing the said land by paying rents. Keti Bibi died leaving behind only son Romizuddin. Romizuddin transferred 1.4550 acres of land in favour of the plaintiff by a kabala dated 06.12.1993. The plaintiff purchased .8250 acre of land also from Zayeda Begum by a registered kabala dated 08.10.1993. The plaintiff got possession of his purchased land and constructed 2 tin-shed huts on a portion of that purchased land and has been possessing the rest land by cultivation. That Romizuddin and Mainuddin threatened the plaintiff with dispossession in the year 1994 and as such the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.254 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and that suit was decreed on 04.10.1995. On 14.06.1996 the defendants Md. Harun-Ur-Rashid and others tried to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land and hence the suit. 

5. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit Nos.100 of 1997 and 101 of 1997 (the present leave-petitioners), in short, was that the suit plot No.2721 comprising 10.90 acres of land along with other lands originally belonged to Khoda Boksha in 8 annas share and Sheikh Kalu and Sheikh Malu in 4 annas share each. That Sheikh Malu died leaving behind 2 sons Mainuddin and Newazuddin and 2 daughters Guljan Bibi and Nazibun Nessa. Thereafter, Newazuddin died leaving behind a wife Keti Bibi and one son Romizuddin. That Mainuddin, Guljan Bibi, Nazibun Nessa, Romizuddin and Keti Bibi amicably partitioned their share in plot No.2721 and in S.A. Khatian their share comprising an area of 2.51 acres of land from plot No.2721 was duly record-ed. Romizuddin sold out .31 acre of land in favour of Mainuddin by a registered kabala dated 12.04.1966 and Mainuddin purchased another .1550 acre of land from said Romizuddin by a registered kabala dated 15.06.1966. Thus Mainuddin acquired 1.57 acres of land. Mamuddin sold out .33 acre of land to the plaintiffs by 3 separate registered kabalas dated 05.02.1987 and 09.02.1987. The plaintiffs got possession of their purchased land and they had been possessing the same peace-fully for more than 12 years. But suddenly on 06.05.1994 the defendants Md. Sirajul Islam and others threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession; that it was then disclosed that the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No.254 of 1994 against Romizuddin and others and managed a collusive and fraudulent decree and on the basis of that decree the defendant has threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession and hence the suits. 

6. All the above 3 Title Suit Nos.9-9 of 1997, 100 of 1997 and 101 of 1997 were tried analogously by the learned Assistant Judge, Nababgonj (Sadar), Dhaka. The trial court, or consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties, decreed Title Suit No.99 of 1997 for permanent injunction and dismissed both Title Suit Nos.100 of 1997 and 101 of 1997. As against this analogous judgment and decree of the trial court the present leave petitioners filed Title Appeal Nos. 354 of 1997, 355 of 1997 and 356 of 1997 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. All those 3 title appeals were heard analogously by the learned.
 
7. Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka and by the analogous judgment and order dated 23.02.1999 the appellate court below dismissed all those 3 title appeals and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. These leave-petitioners then preferred the above mentioned 3(three) Civil Revision Nos.1216 of 1999, 1217 of 1999 and 1218 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained rules. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order, discharged all those rules making observations to the effect that the suit land i.e. .33 acre of land of suit plot No-2721 mentioned in the schedule to the plaint of Title Suit No.100 of 1997 is not specific and identifiable and it had also not been proved that this suit land of Title Suit No.100 of1997 is included in .82½ acre of suit land of Title Suit No.254 of 1994, that it was also not proved that .33 acre of-land as described in the schedule to the plaint of Title Suit No.101 of 1997 is they same land as described in the kabala of the plaintiff of that suit-the exhbits-UmaUma(2) and that the decree passed in Title Suit Nos:254 of 1994 still subsists and that Md. Sirajul Islam-the plaintiff of Title Suit No.99 of 1997 has been able to prove his title and possession in the suit land and that it was not proved al8o that .33 acre of land as claimed by the plaintiff of Title. Suit No.100 of 1997 is part of .824 acre of land as claimed by the plaintiff in Title Suit No.99 of 1997. 

8. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioners has made submissions to the effect that the leave-petitioners Md. Harun-Ur-Rashid and others undisputedly, purchased .33 acre of land of the suit plot No.2721 from its rightful owner long before the purchase of the claimed land of the respondent Md. Sirajul Islam and in the circumstances the courts below committed wrong-and also injustice in dismissing the suit of the leave-petitioners for declaration of their title in their purchased .33 acre of land on a wrong finding that this suit land has not been well specified. The learned Advocate has argued also that there is no clash in between the leave- petitioners and the respondent Md. Sirajul Islam as regards title in their respective claimed land and in the circumstances the courts below ought to have decreed the suit of these leave-petitioners for declaration of their title in their claimed .33 acre of land. 

9. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Senior Advocate for the respondents has made submissions to the effect that in a suit for declaration of title the plaintiff requires to specify the suit land clearly, but in this suit all the courts below found that the claimed .33 acre of land of the plaintiffs Md. Harun-Ur-Rashid and others has not been well specified in the plaint and that the demarcation of this suit land which has been given in the plaint did not tally with the demarcation mentioned in the purchase deeds of the plaintiffs. The learned Senior Advocate has argued that in the circumstance the courts below rightly dismissed the suits filed by these leave-petitioners. 

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the impugned judgment and order of the-High Court Division and also those of the appellate court below and the trial court. 

11. It appears that all the 3 courts have found that in Title Suit No.100 of 1997 filed by these present leave-petitioners the suit land was not well demarcated and that the specification of this suit land which the plaintiffs mentioned in their plaint did not tally with the specification of the land mentioned in their purchase deed. 

12. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioners could not controvert these concurrent findings of the courts below. In the circumstances we find no merit in these Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal. 

13. However, the leave-petitioners Md. Harun-Ur-Rashid and others being purchasers of .33 acre of land from its rightful owner can seek proper remedy through a suit for partition. 

14. All these Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal be dismissed. 

End.

case_source: [২০০৩ সালের ৭৫৪৭ নম্বর রীট পিটিশন মামলায় ১৫ই জুলাই, ২০০৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত রায় ও আদেশ হতে উদ্ভুত]
full_judgment:
বিচারপতি মোহাম্মদ ইমান আলী: এই সিভিল আপগীলটি (যা লিভ টু আপীল এর মাধ্যম গৃহীত) হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের ইংরেজি ১৫/০৭/২০০৮ তারিখের ৭৫৪৭/২০০৩ নং রীট মামলার রায় ও আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে আনীত একটি আপীল । যে আদেশের মাধ্যমে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ পূর্বে ইস্যুকৃত রুল খারিজ করেছেন।

২. মামলার বিবরণ সংক্ষেপে এই যে, মুলসীগঞ্জ জেলার শ্রীনগর উপজেলার মাইপাড়া মৌজার এস.এ. ১২২ নং খতিয়ানের সি,এস. ও এস.এ. ৫৮৭, ৫৮৮, ৫৮৯, ৫৯৭, ৫৯৮, ৬০০ ও ৬০১ নং দাগের ১.২২ একর ভূমিতে রেকর্ডীয় মালিক ছিলেন দেবেন্দ্র কুমার সাহা। আবেদনকারীর বক্তব্য মতে, তিনি দেশত্যাগ করে ভারত চলে যাওয়ায় উক্ত ভূমি ভি.পি. ৩০৪/১৯৭৫ নং কেসের মাধ্যমে অর্পিত সম্পত্তি হিসেবে শ্রী হয় এবং প্রথমে জনৈক সুবল দাস ও পরে আব্দুল কাদির ঢালীর নিকট ও পরবর্তীতে ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলামের এর নিকট লীজ দেয়া হয় যিনি উক্ত ভূমিতে কর্তৃপক্ষের অনুমতি ব্যতীত একটি টিনসেড ঘর উত্তোলন করেন, অবৈধভাবে সাব-লীজ প্রদান করেন, উক্ত অর্পিত সম্পত্তিতে অবস্থিত মূল্যবান গাছপালা কর্তন করেন ও গাছ বিক্রির টাকা আত্মসাৎ করেন । ফলশ্রুতিতে বন্দোবস্ত দলিলের শর্ত ভঙ্গ করার জন্য ৪নং প্রতিপক্ষ উক্ত লীজ বাতিল করেন ও বিরোধীয় ভূমি থেকে ৬৪ শতাংশ ভূমি ১ নং রিট পিটিশন কারীর নিকট বাংলা ১৪০৬ সনের জন্য বন্দোবস্ত প্রদান করেন। তিনি ০৮/০২/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখে ০৫৫৫০৭১ নং ডিসিআর- এর মাধ্যমে সেলামীর টাকা জমা দেন এবং পরবর্তীতে ১৪০৬-১৪০৭ বাংলা সনের জন্য বন্দোবস্ত নবায়ন করা হয়।

৩. ১ ও ২নং আশীলকারী পুনরায় বিরোধীয় এস.এ. ১২২ খতিয়ানের ৬০০ ও ৬০১ নং দাগ থেকে ৩৩ শতাংশ ভূমিতে বন্দোবস্ত প্রাপ্ত হন এবং ২৯/০৬/২০০০ খিঃ তারিখের ০২৮২৮৬৫ নং ডি.সি.আর. এর মাধ্যমে সেলামীর টাকা প্রদান করেন। আবেদনকারীগণের বন্দোবস্তের বিরুদ্ধে ১ নং প্রতিবাদী, প্রাক্তন বন্দোবস্ত গ্রহীতা হিসেবে অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক, মুলসীগঞ্জ এর বরাবর ভিপি আপীল নং ৮/১৯৮৮ রুজু করেন যা ০৭/০৭/১৯৯৯ খ্রিঃ তারিখে তদ্বীরের অভাবে খারিজ হয়। ১ নং প্রতিপক্ষ পুনরায় অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার (৬নং প্রতিবাদী) বরাবর ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/১৯৯৯ দায়ের করেন যিনি ২৯/১০/২০০০ খ্রিঃ তারিখে উক্ত আপীল মঞ্জুর করেন এবং রীট আবেদনকারীদের বন্দোবস্ত বাতিল করেন । উক্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে রীট আবেদনকারীগণ ভূমি আগীল বোর্ড বরাবর ৩৫৬/২০০২ নং আপীল দায়ের করেন যা ০৭/০৯/২০০৩ খিঃ তারিখে নামঞ্জুর করা হয়।

৪. ১নং প্রতিবাদী জবাব দিয়ে প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করেন। তার জবাবের মূল বক্তব্য এই যে, তিনি ৩০৪/১৯৭৪ নং ভি.পি. কেসের মাধ্যমে দেবেন্দ্র কুমার সাহার যে সম্পত্তি ভি.পি. শ্রেণীভূক্ত করা হয় তার প্রথম বন্দোবস্ত গ্রহীতা । মূল হিন্দু মালিকের কর্মচারী হিসেবে তিনি ১৯৭৪ খাদে বন্দোবস্ত প্রাপ্ত হন এবং ১৯৯৮ খ্রিষ্টাব্দে পর্যন্ত প্রতি বছর বন্দোবস্ত নবায়ন করেন। ১৯৯৮ খ্রিষ্টাব্দে আবেদনকারীরা উক্ত অর্পিত সম্পত্তি বন্দোবস্তপাওয়ার জন্য অতিঃ জেলা প্রশাসক রোজন্ব), মুন্সীগঞ্জ বরাবর আবেদন করিলে উক্ত অতিঃ জেলা প্রশাসক সম্পূর্ণ বে-আইনীভাবে সহকারী কমিশনার (ভূমি), শ্রীনগর, মুন্সীগঞ্জকে মৌখিকভাবে ১নং প্রতিবাদীর বন্দোবস্ত বাতিল করে এবং একই ভূমি দরখাস্তকারীদের বরাবর বন্দোবস্ত দেয়ার নির্দেশ দেন। পরবর্তীতে তিনি ঢাকার অতিরিক্ত বিভাগীয় কমিশনার(৬নং প্রতিবাদী) বরাবর ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/১৯৯৯ দায়ের করেন যিনি অত্র মামলার আবেদনকারীর বন্দোবস্ত বাতিল করে আপীল মঞ্জুর করেন। পরবর্তীতে আবেদনকারীগণ ভূমি আপীল বোর্ড বরাবর ৩-৫৬/ ২০০২ নং আপীল করলে তা ০৭/০৯/২০০৩ খ্রিঃ তারিখে খারিজ হয়। উক্ত খারিজাদেশের বিরুদ্ধে আবেদনকারীগণ হাইকোর্টে রীট পিটিশন দায়ের করলে হাইকোর্ট রুল জারী করে ও শুনানীঅন্তে বিরোধীয় আদেশ ও রায় দ্বারা উক্ত রুল খারিজ করেন।

৫. এর ফলশ্রুতিতে আপীলকারীগণ ৮৪/২০০৯ নং লীভ টু আপীলের প্রার্থনা করেন যা নিয্নবর্ণত উপস্থাপনের ভিত্তিতে গৃহীত হয়:
১. হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ (এ বিষয়টি) বিবেচনা করতে ব্যর্থ হয়েছে যে ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ অতিঃ কমিশনার, ঢাকা কর্তৃক বিচারযোগ্য ছিল না কারণ উক্ত আপীল টি ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলাম কর্তৃক আনয়ন করা হয় যিনি কিনা তর্কিত বন্দোবস্তের কোন পক্ষ ছিলেন না। সুতরাং অতিঃ কমিশনার, ঢাকা কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ভিপি, আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ এর ২৯/১০/২০০০ খিঃ তারিখের আদেশ রক্ষণীয় নয় ও আইনত অবৈধ এবং এর ফলে ন্যয়বিচার ব্যাহত হয়েছে।
২. হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ আরও বিবেচনা করতে ব্যর্থ হয়েছে যে, ভি.পি. মোকদ্দমা ৩০৪/১৯৭৫ থেকে উদ্ভুত ভি.পি. আপীল নং ৮/১৯৯৯ অতিঃ জেলা প্রশাসক, মুন্সীগঞ্জ কর্তৃক তদ্বীরের অভাবে খারিজ হয়। উক্ত খারিজাদেশের বিরন্নদ্ধে কোন প্রতিকার গ্রহণ না করে ভি পি আগীল ১৩/২০০০ দায়ের করিলে অতিঃ কমিশনার, ঢাকা উক্ত আপীলের এর রক্ষনীয়তা বিবেচনা না করেই তা মঞ্জুর করেন যা সম্পূর্ণ আইন বহির্ভূত হয়েছে।
৩. হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত রীট পিটিশন নং ৭৫৪৭/২০০৩ এর ১৫.০৭.২০০৮ তারিখের বিরোধীয় আদেশ স্ববিরোধী কারণ উক্ত রায়ের শেষাংশে লেখা রয়েছে- “১০২ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী অত্র আদালতের আপীল আদালত হিসেবে পক্ষদ্বয়ের দাবীর বৈধতা বিচার করার কোন খতিয়ার নেই ”।

৬. আপীলকারীগণের পক্ষে বিজ্ঞ এডভোকেট জনাব মোহাম্মদ হোসেন-এর যে সকল উপস্থাপনের ভিত্তিতে লীভ মঞ্জুর করা হয়েছে সেসব বিষয়ের উপর বক্তব্য উপস্থাপনের পাশাপাশি আরো বলেন যে একই সাথে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করেন যে- “অত্র আদালত ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ নং আপীল ও ভূমি আপীল এবং রিভিউ মঞ্জুরের ক্ষেত্রে ৪-৬ নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষের কোন অবৈধতা খুজে পাননি । সুতরাং এই রুলের কোন ভিত্তি নেই ও আইনত খারিজযোগ্য |” তার অর্থ এই যে, যেখানে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করে যে ১০২ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী অত্র আদালতের আপীল আদালত হিসেবে পক্ষদ্বয়ের দাবীর বৈধতা নির্ণয়ে মেরিটে প্রবেশ করার কোন এখতিয়ার নেই সেখানে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ দোষ-গুণ বিচারের ভিত্তিতে রুলটি খারিজ করেন।

৭. তিনি আরো বলেন যে অতিঃ কমিশনার, ঢাকা কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ এর ২৯/১০/২০০০ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশ রক্ষণীয় নয় ও আইনত অবৈধ কারণ ভি.পি. মোকন্দমা ৩০৪/১৯৭৫ এর দ্বারা উদ্ভূত ভি.পি. আপীল নং ৮/১৯৯৯ অতিঃ জেলা প্রশাসক, মুন্সীগঞ্জ কর্তৃক তদ্বীরের অভাবে ০৭/০৭/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখে খারিজ হয়। উক্ত খারিজাদেশের বিরুদ্ধে কোন আপীল করা হয়নি। তিনি আরো বলেন যে, অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব) এর আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে অতিরিক্ত বিভাগীয় কমিশনার এর নিকট দায়েরকৃত আপীলটি রক্ষণীয় নয় । সুতরাং অতিরিক্ত বিভাগীয় কমিশনারের আদেশটি কর্তৃত্ব বহির্ভূত ।

৮. ১ নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষে জনাব আব্দুল ওয়াদুদ ভূঁইয়া বিজ্ঞ সিনিয়র এডভোকেট এবং ২-৮ নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষে এডভোকেট অন রেকর্ড জনাব হরিদাস পাল হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের বিরোধীয় রায় ও আদেশের পক্ষে বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন। তারা বলেন যে, বিভাগীয় কমিশনার কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ১৫/১০/২০০০ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশে সঠিকভাবে বলা হয়:
“ভি, পি. মিস কেইস ৮/৯৮ বিজ্ঞ অতিঃ জেলা প্রশাসক রোজস্ব)র নিকট বিচারাধীন থাকা অবস্থায় থানা নিবহী অফিসার লীজ বাতিল করেছেন এবং প্রতিপক্ষকে লীজ প্রদান করেছেন৷ আরো উলে-খ্য প্রতিপক্ষকে লীজ প্রদানের এক মাসের মধ্যেই ঘর তোলার অনুমতি দেওয়া হয়েছে, পক্ষান্তরে আগীলকারীর ঘর মেরামতের বক্তব্য গ্রহণ করা হয় নাই। ইহার প্রেক্ষিতে জেলা প্রশাসক প্রচ্ছন্ন ইংগিতে কিংবা তার মৌখিক নির্দেশে অযৌক্তিকভাবে বিনা অনুমতিতে ঘর উঠাবার অযুহাতে লীজ বাতিল করা হইয়াছে এবং প্রত���পক্ষের অনুকূল অনিয়মে লীজ প্রদান করা হয়েছে। আদেশে আরো উলে-খ করা হয়েছে, সার্বিক পর্যালোচনান্তে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, জেলা প্রশাসকের হস্তক্ষেপের কারণেই ন্যায়বিচার পদদলিত করে আগীলকারীর লীজ বাতিল করা হয়েছে এবং প্রতিপক্ষকে অন্যায়ভাবে লীজ প্রদান করা হয়েছে।”

৯. বিজ্ঞ এডভোকেট আরও বলেন যে ভূমি আপীল বোর্ডের ০৭/০৯/২০০৩ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশে স্পষ্ট বলা হয়..
“সুদীর্ঘ ২৪ বছর যাবৎ ভোগ দখলে থাকা অবস্থায় কেবল ঘর মেরামতের কারণ দেখিয়ে প্রতিপক্ষের লীজ বাতিল করণ সঠিক নয়, উপরন্ত লীজের অন্য কোন শর্ত লংঘিত হয়েছিল বলে প্রতীয়মান হয় না”।

১০. এছাড়াও ভূমি আপীল বোর্ডের পূর্ণ বোর্ড কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ২৯/১১/২০০৩ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশে বলা হয়...
“উভয় পক্ষের বক্তব্যের প্রেক্ষিতে নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার এবং বিজ্ঞ সদস্য সার্বিক বিষয়টি বিচার বিশে-ষণ করে প্রতিপক্ষের ইজারা দেয়া বহাল রেখেছেন। অত্র বোর্ড মনে করে যে, তাদের প্রদত্ত আদেশ যথাযথ হয়েছে। এ কারণে এ আবেদনটি পুনঃ বিচারের অবকাশ নেই। এমতাবস্থায় আবেদনটি নাকচ করা হল”।

১১. প্রতিবাদী পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ এডভোকেটগণ আরও দাবী করেন যে, হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ রুলটি খারিজ করে কোন আইনগত ভূল করেননি এবং ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ এর আপীল এবং রিভিউ মঞ্জ্ররের ক্ষেত্রে ৬-৮ নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষের কোন অবৈধতা নেই ফলে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ এ রুলের কোন বৈধতা খুজে পাননি তাই রুলটি খারিজ করেছেন। সুতরাং অত্র সিভিল আপীলটি খারিজযোগ্য ৷

১২. আপীলকারীগণের পক্ষ থেকে বলা হয়েছে যে ভিপি আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ অতিঃ কমিশনার, ঢাকা কর্তৃক বিচারযোগ্য ছিল না এ বিষয়টি হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ বিবেচনা করতে ব্যর্থ হয়েছে কারণ উক্ত আপীলটি ১নং প্রতিবাদীর ভাই নুরুল ইসলাম কর্তৃক আনয়ন করা হয় যিনি কিনা তর্কিত বন্দোবস্তের কোন পক্ষ ছিলেন না। সুতরাং অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার, ঢাকা কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ এর ২৯/১০/২০০০ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশ বরক্ষণীয় নয় ও আইনত অবৈধ এবং এর ফলে ন্যয়বিচার ব্যাহত হয়েছে। প্রকৃতপক্ষে ১ নং প্রতিবাদী বিরোধীয় ভূমির প্রথম বন্দোবস্ত গ্রহীতা । সুতরাং আপীলটি খারিজযোগ্য ।

১৩. উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ কৌসুলীর বক্তব্য ও হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ কর্তৃক প্রদেয় তর্কিত রায় ও আদেশ এবং অন্যান্য কাগজপত্র পর্যালোচনা করে দেখা যায় যে, বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির মূল মালিক দেবেন্দ্র কুমার সাহা ভারতে চলে যাওয়ার পর ১ নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলাম ১.২২ একর সম্পত্তির ইজারা গ্রহণের জন্য সরকারের নিকট আবেদন করেন। উক্ত বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তিটি নজরুল ইসলাম এরই দখলে ছিল। ইংরেজি ০৭/১১/১৯৭৪ সালের ভি.পি, ৩০৪/১৯৭৪ নম্বর মামলার ০৭/১১/১৯৭৪ খ্রিঃ তারিখেরে আদেশ বলে নজরুল ইসলামের ইজারা আবেদন গৃহীত হয়। এই লীজ এক বছরের জন্য মঞ্জুর করা হয়েছিল এবং পরবতীতে সরকারি বিধি অনুসারে ভাড়া বৃদ্ধির মাধ্যমে বার্ষিক ভিত্তিতে নবায়ন করা হয়।

১৪. ভি. পি. মামলার অর্ডার শীট থেকে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, গত ৩১/০৫/১৯৯৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখে বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির কিছু অংশ বসতবাড়ি এবং কিছু অংশ পুকুর হিসেবে শ্রেণিভূক্ত করে এবং নিলামের মাধ্যমে ইজারা দেয়ার নির্দেশ দেয়া হয় কিন্তু দেখা যায় যে নির্ধারিত নিলামে অংশগ্রহণ করার জন্য কেউ উপস্থিত ছিল না। প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলাম সংশি-ষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষকে অবগত করেছেন যে সম্পত্তিটি প্রকৃতপক্ষে পুকুর নয় বরং এটা কৃষিজমি যাহা স্থানীয় তদন্তের মাধ্যমে নির্ধারণ করা যেতে পারে।

১৫. আরও দেখা যায় যে, ইতিমধ্যে বর্তমান আবেদনকারী মাসুদুর রহমান এই সম্পত্তির ইজারা পাওয়ার জন্য আবেদন করেন যার প্রেক্ষিতে উভয় পক্ষের উপস্থিতিতে বিগত ১৬/০৮/১৯৯৮ খিঃ তারিখে শুনানি হয়। একই দিনে বিদ্যমান লীজ গ্রহীতা বর্তমান বছরের সেলামীর টাকা প্রদান করার ইচ্ছা প্রকাশ করেন এবং পরবর্তী বছরের ইজারা পাওয়ার জন্য আবেদন করেন । উভয় পক্ষের যৌথ আবেদন এর ভিত্তিতে বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তিতে অননুমোদিত বাড়ি নির্মাণের বিষয়টি তদন্ত করার জন্য আদেশ হয়। বিগত ২৪/০৯/১৯৯৮খ্রিঃ তারিখের ৪১ নম্বর আদেশ অনুসারে প্রদেয় রিপোর্টে দেখা যায় যে লিজ গ্রহীতা অনুমতি ছাড়া একটি টিনশেড বাড়ি নির্মাণ করেছেন এবং একই আদেশে লিজ গ্রহীতাকে বাড়ি নির্মাণের ব্যাখ্যা দেয়ার জন্য নোটিশ জারি করার নির্দেশ দেয়া হয়।

১৬. ২১/১০/১৯৯৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশ হতে দেখা যায় যে ইজারা গ্রহীতা তার বাড়ি নির্মাণের ব্যাখ্যা হিসেবে বলেন বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তিতে ইজারা গ্রহণের পূর্বেই তিনি তিনটি ঘর নির্মাণ করেছিলেন এবং ১৯৯৮ সালের বন্যার পরে তিনটি ঘরের একটি ঘর মেরামত করতে হয়েছিল। লীজ গ্রহীতার এই ব্যাখ্যাটি সন্তোষজনক নয় বিবেচনায় তৎকালীন টি.এন.ও অর্থাৎ থানা নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে ইজারা গ্রহীতাকে নোটিশ প্রাপ্তির তিন দিনের মধ্যে বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তিটি খালি করার নির্দেশ দেন। সম্পত্তির দখল ফেরতের এই নোটিশটি বিগত ৯/১২/১৯৯৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখে প্রদান করা হয়। এই নোটিশ এর কার্যকারিতা চ্যালেঞ্জ করে ১নং প্রতিবাদী ইজারা গ্রহীতা, ২৩/১২/১৯৯৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখে অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব), মুন্সিগঞ্জ বরাবর ভি.পি. মামলা নং ৮/৯৮ দীয়ের করেন।

১৭. অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব) এর ২৩/১২/১৯৯৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখের আদেশবলে একটি বিবিধ মামলা (মিস কেস) শুরু হয় এবং সহকারী কমিশনার (ভূমি) এর রিপোর্ট সমেত নথি তলব করা হয়। তবে আবেদনকারী থানা নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা (টি.এন.ও) বরাবর চলমান মামলার পরবর্তী কার্যক্রম স্থগিত চাইলেও অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব) এ মর্মে কোন স্থগিতাদেশ প্রদান করেন নি; শুধুমাত্র নথি তলব করেছেন । থানা নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা (টি.এন.ও) এর ১০/০২/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখের ৪৯নং আদেশ শুট দেখা যায় ২৬/০১/১৯৯৯ ও ২৭/০১/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখে অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব) কর্তৃক রিপোর্ট সমেত নথি তলব চাওয়া হলেও মে, ১৯৯৯ এর আগে তা পাঠানো হয় নি। ইতোমধ্যে আপীলকারী মাসুদুর রহমান ও মাহবুবুর রহমান ১৮/০১/১৯৯৯ খ্রিঃ তারিখে ইজারা বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির মধ্যে ৬৪ শতাংশ ভূমি পাওয়ার আবেদন করেন । থানা নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা (টি.এন.ও) এর ৪৭ নং আদেশ থেকে প্রতীয়মান হয় জেলা প্রশাসক, মুন্সীগঞ্জ উক্ত আবেদনকারীদের একই দিনে অর্থাৎ ১৮/০১/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখে ইজারা প্রদানের জন্য মৌখিকভাবে আদেশ দেন। তাতেই প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব), মুন্সীগঞ্জ কর্তৃক ২৬/০১/১৯৯৯ ও ২৭/০১/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখে নথি তলব চাওয়া স্বত্তেও পূর্বের লীজগ্রহীতাকে উচ্ছেদ করা হয়। আরও দেখা যায় যে নতুন লীজগ্রহীতা কর্তৃক ১০/০২/১৯৯৯ খ্রিঃ তারিখে আনীত গৃহনির্মাণের দরখাস্তটি ১৫/০২/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখে মঞ্জুর করা হয়। তাতেই স্পষ্টতই দেখা যায় যে, প্রকৃত লীজগ্রহীতা নজরুল ইসলামের লীজটি জেলা প্রশাসক, মুলগীগঞ্জ এর অন্যায় আদেশে বাতিল করা হয় এমন এক সময় যখন বিষয়টি অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব),  বরাবর বিচারাধীন ছিল ।

১৮. লীজের জমিতে অননুমোদিত গৃহ্নির্মাণের জন্য লীজগ্রহীতার কাছে ব্যাখ্যা চাওয়া হলে তিনি ব্যাখ্যা প্রদান করেন যা থানা নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা (টি.এন.ও) এর কাছে সন্তোষজনক মনে না হওয়ায় তিনি তিন দিনের মধ্যে জমি খালি করার নোটিশ প্রদান করেন। উক্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে পরবর্তী উর্ধতন কর্মকর্তা অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব), বরাবর আপীল করা হয়। এ আপীলের বিষয়টি বিচারাধীন থাকা অবস্থায় নিয়মতান্ত্রিক পদ্ধতির বাইরে গিয়ে জেলা প্রশাসকের মৌখিক আদেশের ভিত্তিতে নতুন লীজগ্রহীতার কাছে লীজ দেয়া হয় যারা শর্তভঙ্গের বিষয়টি আবিষ্কৃত হওয়ার পূর্ব থেকেই সুযোগের অপেক্ষায় ছিল এ���ং টিএনও তড়িঘড়ি করে জেলা প্রশাসকের মৌখিক আদেশের ভিত্তিতে প্রাক্তন লিজগ্রহীতার লিজ বাতিল করেন এবং তিন দিনের মধ্যে ভূমি খালি করার নির্দেশ দেন।

১৯. যেহেতু পূর্বেই বলা হয়েছে যথাযথ কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আপীল চলাকালীন সময়ে পূর্বের লীজগ্রহীতার লীজ বাতিলকরণ প্রক্রিয়া সম্পূর্ণ বেআইনী ও ভয়েড আযাব ইনিশিও (void ab initio) সুতরাং এ বিষয়ে পরবর্তী যা কিছু সিদ্ধান্ত বা আদেশ হয়েছে সব কিছুই বেআইনী । এ বিবেচনায় এটা বলা বেআইনি হবে না যে নজরুল ইসলাম নামীয় লীজ বাতিল এবং তাকে উচ্ছেদ করা সম্পূর্ণ বেআইনী ও অবৈধ। সম্পত্তি হস্তান্তর আইনের অন্যতম একটা মূলনীতি হলো-- “Pendente lite nihil innovature” অর্থাৎ মামলা চলাকালীন মামলার বিষয়বস্তুতে নতুন কোন রাইট, ইন্টারেস্ট সৃষ্টি না করা। সুতরাং অত্র মামলায় ভিত্তিহীন, বেআইনী মৌখিক আদেশের ভিত্তিতে নতুন লীজগ্রহীতার অনুকূলে বেআইনিভাবে প্রদেয় লীজ পূর্বের লীজ গ্রহীতার কোন অধিকারকে ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ করবেনা ।

২০. আরো দেখা যায় যে, অতিরিক্ত জেলা প্রশাসক (রাজস্ব), বরাবর বিবিধ মামলাটি চলমান থাকা অবস্থায়ই ১৩/০১/১৯৯৯ খিঃ তারিখের আদেশকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করে পূর্বের লীজগ্রহীতা অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার বরাবর ভি.পি. আপীল নং ১৩/৯৯ দায়ের করেন। প্রকৃতপক্ষে এ আদেশটি দিয়েছিল থানা নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা (টি.এন.ও), যার বিরুদ্ধে আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষ হবে জেলা প্রশাসক । এ বিষয়ে অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার তার ২৯/১০/২০০০ তারিখের আদেশে মতামত প্রদান করে বলেন যে অননুমোদিত গৃহনির্মাণের দায়ে লীজ বাতিল করা এবং নতুন করে লীজ দেয়া সবই হয়েছিল জেলা প্রশাসকের নির্দেশে সুতরাং তার নিকট আপীল করে কোন ফলাফল পাওয়া যেত না। তা স্বত্বেও আমরা/এই আদালত বলতে বাধ্য হচ্ছি যে, আপীল কর্তৃপক্ষকে এভাবে পাশ কাটিয়ে যাওয়া কোনভাবেই সমর্থন করা যায় না। আইনের নির্ধারিত বিধি বিধান ও প্রক্রিয়াসমূহ অবশ্য পালনীয়।

২১. এ বিষয়ে ন্যাচাবান জাস্টিস এর একটি মূলনীতি উলে-খ করা যেতে পারে । যেখানে বলা আছে যে, Nemo Judex in causa sua or Rule against bias. অর্থাৎ কোন ব্যক্তি তার নিজের পক্ষের বিচারক হইবেনা । অত্র মামলার ১নং প্রতিবাদী টি. এন. ও. এর আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে জেলা প্রশাসক বরাবর আপীল করার কথা ছিলো । কিন্তু নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলামের লীজ বাতিল করতঃ আবেদনকারীগণের অনুকূলে লীজ প্রদান করার জন্য টি.এন.ও. কে জেলা প্রশাসক মৌখিকভাবে আদেশ দেন। জেলা প্রশাসকের মৌখিক এই আদেশ থেকে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলামের অনুকুলে লীজ বাতিলের আদেশটি পরোক্ষভাবে জেলা প্রশাসকেরই আদেশ ছিলো | এই আদেশের বিরুদ্ধেই ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলাম যথাযথ কর্তৃপক্ষ অর্থাৎ জেলা প্রশাসক বরাবর আপিল না করে অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার বরাবর আপিল করেন। যেখানে জেলা প্রশাসক নিজেই পরোক্ষভাবে আদেশ প্রদান করেছেন সেখানে উক্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে জেলা প্রশাসকের আগীলেট কর্তৃপক্ষ হওয়ার আইনগত কোন সুযোগ নেই। সুতরাং ১নং প্রতিবাদী অতিঃ বিভাগীয় কমিশনার বরাবর ভিপি আগীল নং ১৩/৯৯ দায়ের করে মামলার পদ্ধতিগত সৌন্দর্য নষ্ট করেছেন বলে প্রতীয়মান হয়না ।

২২. আপীলকারীগণের পক্ষে বিজ্ঞ এডভোকেট দাবী করেন যে ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলাম লীজ গ্রহীতা না হয়েও তার ভাই নুরুল ইসলামের পক্ষে অতিঃ কমিশনার, ঢাকা বরাবর ভিপি আপীল নং ১৩/২০০০ দায়ের করেন যাহা আইনগতভাবে রক্ষণীয় নয় । কিন্তু নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় ১নং প্রতিবাদী নজরুল ইসলামই প্রর্কত লীজ গ্রহীতা এবং অনাইনুগভাবে তার নামেই লীজ বাতিল করা হয়। সুতরাং ১নং প্রতিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে আবেদনকারীগণের আনিত এই অভিযোগটিও ভিত্তিহীন ।

২৩. ২৩/১০/২০০৩ তারিখে টিএনও-এর আদেশ থেকে আমরা লক্ষ্য করছি যে মূল লীজ গ্রহীতা জোর করে ০৯/০৯/২০০৩ তারিখে লীজকৃত সম্পত্তির বাড়িতে প্রবেশ করে এবং স্থানীয় তদন্ত প্রতিবেদন থেকে জানা যায় যে নজরুল ইসলামের স্ত্রী এবং মোঃ ফারুকের স্ত্রী এই সম্পত্তিতে বসবাসরত থাকাবস্থায় তাদের বাড়ি থেকে উচ্ছেদ করার সুপারিশ করা হয়েছে। যাহোক, মূল লীজ গ্রহীতা সফলভাবে ভূমি আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল পর্যন্ত তার ইজারা রক্ষা করতে সক্ষম হয় এবং বর্তমান আপীলকারীগণ হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ থেকে কোন আদেশ পেতে ব্যর্থ হয়, ফলে ০১.০১.২০০৪ তারিখে মূল লীজ গ্রহীতার কাছ থেকে লিজের টাকা নেয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত হয়।

২৪. উপর্যুক্ত পর্যালোচনার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে অযৌক্তিক অযুহাতে ১নং প্রতিবাদীর ভোগদখলকৃত ইজারা বাতিল করে আপীলকারীগণের অনুকূলে ইজারা প্রদান করার সিদ্ধান্ত সম্পূর্ণ বেআইনি এবং ভিত্তিহীন। এমতাবস্থায় আপীলকারীগণের আনীত আগীলটি সম্পূর্ণ ভিত্তিহীন ঘোষণা করা হইলো ।

২৫. সুতরাং খরচা ব্যতিরেকে অত্র আগীলটি খারিজ করা হইলো ।

শেষ।

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 6-1-2008, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 276 of 1998).
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J : This Civil Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 6-1-2008 passed by a single Bench of the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 276 of 1998 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10-5-1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal No.287 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Noakhali in Title suit No. 696 of 1974 dismissing the suit for declaration of title. 

2. Facts necessary for disposal of this Civil Appeal, in brief, are: 
That the present respondent Nos.1-3 and two others instituted Title suit No. 696 of 1974 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Noakhali, against the government and others for declaration of title in 10.26 acres' of land described in the schedule to the plaint. As the land of the appellants and others were included in the schedule to the plaint, they got themselves added as defendant Nos.5-11 in the suit on their application under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

3. The plaintiff's case, in short, inter-alia, is that Fazlu Miah was the recorded owner of 10.26 acres of land, in PS Khatian No.1041 under Mouja Char Jublee within Police Station Sadar, District Noakhali. After his death his only son, Hossain Ahamed Kazi inherited the same and mortgaged the same to Mohammad Miah, predecessor of defendant Nos. 2 to 4, at Taka 130 by a conditional sale deed executed and registered on 20th Chaitra 1341 BS for a period of 8 years on condition, to repay the aforesaid money within 20th Chaitra 1349 BS and get back the said land. But Hossain Ahamed Kazi did not redeem it. While Mohammad Hossain Miah was owner in possession of the said land, none paid the government taxes and, as such, the suit land was put into auction and the government purchased the same on 1-10-1936 in Certificate Case No. 201 of 1933-34 which was confirmed on 4-12-1936. Thus, the Government became the owner of the said land. The said Mohammad Hossain Miah then took settlement of said land in Revenue Settlement Case No.650 of 1936-37 from the Government and accordingly, SA Khatian No. 2594 was opened in his name and since then he had been enjoying the suit land. Subsequently, the land was correctly recorded in his name in Diara Khatian No. 2336. After the death of Mohammad Hossain Miah his heirs, defendant Nos. 2-4 sold the suit land to the plaintiffs by four kabalas all dated 25-3-1974 and delivered possession of the same to the transferees. But subsequently, the suit land was wrongly recorded in Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government and, as such, the local Tahsilder on 4-11-1974 refused to accept the rent from the plaintiffs. Thus, they were constrained to institute the suit. 

4. The defendant No.1, defendant Nos.5-11 and 12-17 filed three sets of separate written statements to contest the suit. The defendant No.1 in its written statement stated inter (ilia that, the suit land was diluviated in 1344 BS and was under the water for more than 20 years. As a result the right, title and interest of Mohammad Hossain Miah or Hossain Ahamed Kazi was extinguished in consequence of the provisions of President Order No. 135 of 1972 and the same vested in Government without any encumbrance. During the last survey, the land was correctly recorded in the name of the Government. The S.A. record, prepared in the name of Mohammad Hossain Miah, the predecessor of defendants Nos. 2-4, was without any basis. The plaintiffs did not acquire any right, title or interest by the purchase deed from defendant Nos. 2-4 over the suit land as the said defendants had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. The written statement filed by defendant Nos.5-11 and 12-17 are identical and, as such, the same does not require to be narrated elaborately.

5. In the written statement, fendant Nos. 5 to. 11 denied the entire plaint case of the plaintiffs. Their substantive cases are that Hossain Ahmed Kazi mortgaged 8 annas measuring 5.10 acres out of scheduled land of the plaint to Mohammad Hossain Miah which he redeemed. The suit land was diluviated from the possession of Hossain Ahmed Kazi, and government could not take possession as it was diluviated land at that time. After alleviation Hossain Ahmed Kazi took possession of the suit land. After the death of Hossain Ahmed Kazi his heirs added defendant Nos. 5 to 11 have been possessing the suit land by cultivating the same. It is stated that, the defendants denied the so called settlement of Mohammad Hossain Miah from government and they asserted that suit land was under water at the time of so-called auction by government. After alluvian, these defendants prayed for restoration of the holding in their names as the heirs of original owner and accordingly, the government restored the original holding in the name of these defendants vide restoration Miscellaneous Case No. 369 of 1972-73 and they paid dues and arrear rents to government. These defendants denied the right, title and interest of Mohammad Hossain Miah, his heirs and plaintiffs in the suit land and, as such, challenged the so-called deeds of the plaintiffs as claimed in the plaint. On the basis of the aforesaid assertion, the defendant Nos. 5 to 11 prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

6. Subsequently, the defendant Nos. 5 to 11 filed an additional written statement, contending, inter alia that they have their homesteads, tanks in some portion of the suit land where they have been living with their family members and that they have been possessing the rest land by cultivation. 

7. In the written statement, defendant Nos. 12 to 17 asserted in the similar way as has been stated by the defendant Nos. 5 to 11 in their written statement and, as such, the same does not require to be stated again. In the written statement, the defendant Nos. 12 to 17 claim 2.25 acres out of the suit land as the heirs of the original owner, Hossain Ahmed Kazi and prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

8. The trial court, after hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31-8-1987. Against which the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 287 of 1987 before the learned District Judge, Noakhali. Subsequently, the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Noakhali who dismissed the same by his judgment and decree dated 10-5-1997. The plaintiffs then filed Civil Revision No.276 of 1998 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which ultimately has been made absolute by judgment and order dated 3-1-2008. 

9. Hence the present appellants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 846 of 2008 and obtained leave giving rise to this appeal. 

10. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant appellant submits that the High Court Division committed error in making the Rule absolute without reversing the concurrent findings of both Courts below in as much as the plaintiffs could not prove their title and possession in the suit land, whereas the defendant proved the same. He submits that the High Court Division failed to consider the printed Kabuliyat dated 6-2-1937 (Exhibit 4) filed by the plaintiffs claiming that, to be the title document of their predecessor in its own perspective when on the face of the same it clearly appears to have been printed on 26-2-1954 from one Lucky Press, Chaumuhani, Noakhali and, as such, the basic document of the plaintiffs' predecessor being a false and ante dated document the same has not created any valid title of the plaintiffs or on their predecessor. Hence, all subsequent deeds filed by the plaintiffs having not created any legal right the same are forged and fabricated which has been rightly pointed out by the trial Court and affirmed by the Court of appeal below in its judgment. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that Mohammad Hossain Miah, predecessor of the plaintiffs' vendor, instituted Title Suit No. 70 of 1969 for declaration of his title for the self same land, but ultimately withdrew the same on 29-3-1974 without obtaining permission from the court to sue afresh and thus, filing of the instant suit by the plaintiffs in 1974 upon creating the alleged kabuliyat, the title deed of the predecessor of their vendors (defendants Nos. 2 to 4) suppressing the fact of filing and withdrawing the said suit clearly proves that they practiced fraud upon the Court which the Court of appeal, below rightly found that the instant suit is hit by Order XXIII, rule 3 of the Code. Mr. Chowdhury also submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as they did not pray for any consequential relief and also for non consideration of the material evidences on record. Lastly, he submits that the High Court Division made the Rule absolute against all the defendant opposite parties amongst whom defendant-opposite party Nos. 7, 8 and 13 died in the meantime during the pendency of .the Rule and, as such, the impugned judgment and order making the Rule absolute against the dead persons is a nullity. 

11. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on Record appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 submits that both the Courts below without applying their judicial mind and upon non reading and misreading the materials on record came to an erroneous decision and thereby, dismissed the suit which the High Court Division upon full consideration of the materials on record set aside by the impugned judgment and order. According to him, PW 1 proved the Kabuliat submitted by the Government as Exhibit 4 showing that the plaintiffs got the settlement of the suit land from the Government, and they are possessing and enjoying the same without any hindrance. All the PWs, according to him, categorically proved the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land during the SA settlement and their names have been rightly prepared and published in the SA Khatian as Exhibit 1(ICa). He submits that the defendant No.1, the Government, claimed that the suit land was diluvion land which was under the water for long time and, as such, the plaintiffs' predecessor lost his title and possession over the suit land as no claim was ever made within the specific period. Such finding of the Courts below was totally misreading of materials on record inasmuch as had it been so the SA Khatian would never have been prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. He submits that no evidence has been led by the defendants to prove that the suit land was under water and, as such, the submissions of the defendants are totally wrong. He submits that the Courts below failed to consider that PW 1 proved the rent receipt (Exhibit 5) produced by the plaintiffs and also failed to consider and determine the possession of the plaintiffs although all the PWs categorically proved the same and the documents exhibited by the plaintiffs in support of their title and possession clearly proves their title and possession in the suit land by constructing houses and living there. Hence the findings of the courts below were erroneous. In support of his submission he relied on the case of Md. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, reported in 17 BLD (AD) 91 = 2 BLC (AD) 56; and thereby submitted that since construction of document is a mixed question of law and fact and the same having not properly been construed by the Courts below, the High Court Division was very much within its competence to reverse the said finding of fact arrived at by the Courts below giving cogent reason. He submits that the courts below failed to take into consideration Exhibit 1(Ka), S.A Khatian, Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) and the rent receipt (Exhibit 5) which obviously proved the plaintiffs' right, title and possession in the suit land. The High Court Division having considered those documents found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land and made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment. Lastly relying on the decision in the case of Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury vs Mr. Nurul Amin, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162; Mr. Bhuiyan submits that when there is misreading of evidence and non consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case. Thus the High Court Division has rightly made the Rule absolute which does not call for any interference by this Court. 

12. From the facts and circumstances and the submissions of the learned advocates of both the sides as stated above, it appears that the whole crux of the case is the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) which is the title document of Mohammad Hossain Miah the predecessor of the plaintiffs' vendors. On perusal of the said Exhibit it appears that it has been printed from one "Lucky Press", Chaumuhani, Noakhali on 26-2-1954. From, the contents of the said exhibit it appears that the same has been executed on 6-2-1937 by the collector of Noakhali on behalf of the Governor of Bango Prodesh as one part and Mohammad Hossain Miah, predecessor of the plaintiffs' vendors as the other part and the same appears to have been given effect from 1344 BS in respect of 10.26 acres of land. After taking such settlement by the said Kabuliyat, the said Mohammad Hossain Mia died leaving behind defendants Nos. 2 to 4 as his heirs who, according to the plaintiffs, transferred the said land (suit land) to them. 

13. It further appears that the trial Court on examination of the materials on record held that, only question for determination is whether the plaintiffs could prove that Mohammad Hossain Mia got the settlement through RS Case No. 650/36-37. On analyzing the materials on record it found that the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) has been executed on 6.2.1937 and has been accepted on 15-3-1950 and the form on which the said Kabuliat has been prepared appears to have been printed from one "Lucky Press", Chaumuhani, Noakhali on 26-2-1954 and thus the trial Court held that; how a Kabuliat claimed to have been executed on 6-2-1937 and accepted 15-3-1950 can be shown to have been executed in a form printed on 26-2-1954 from Lucky Press, Chaumuhani. It also held that the date of comparing the deed and printing of the Kabuliyat and the date of execution are not the same. Thus the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) is not a reliable document and no title and possession can be passed on the basis of such unacceptable document. From the materials on record the trial Court also found that the Government vide Certificate Case No. 201/33-34 auction purchased the suit land on 1-10-1936 which was confirmed on 4-12-1936 and RS Case No. 650/36-37 appears to have been filed and Kabuliyat appears to have been executed on 6-2-1937. So the chronology of dates also show that, after confirmation of auction sale within two months the RS case has been filed which clearly proves that within a year (actually two months) of getting the auction sale confirmed in favour of the Government, Mohammad Hossain Miah created the settlement by the said Kabuliyat. 

14. On the other hand upon scanning Exhibit 6 it appears that the restoration case No. 369/72- 73 does not show that any holding was opened or restored in the name of the defendant Nos. 2 to 4. 

15. Considering Exhibits 4 and 6 and the evidence on record the trial Court held that the claim of the plaintiffs that Mohammad Hossain Miah or his heirs, defendant Nos. 2 to 4 obtained right, title and possession in the suit land is not proved. All these findings have been affirmed by the court of appeal below who also held that Mohammad Miah, the predecessor of the defendants. Nos. 2 to 4 from whom the plaintiffs purchased the suit property also filed Title Suit No. 70 of 1969 against the Government on the same plea and the said suit was permitted to be withdrawn by Order No. 55 dated 23-3-1974 on payment of cost of Taka 15 to the defendant. The plaintiffs under such circumstances filed the instant suit without disclosing anything about filing of the earlier suit by Mohammad Hossain Miah and since there is no permission to sue afresh, the present suit filed by the plaintiffs claiming through the heirs of Mohammad Miah is hit by Order XXIII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thus the suit is not maintainable as filing of the subsequent suit, i.e. the instant suit on the self same cause of action, by the plaintiffs, is barred by law since the plaintiffs could not produce any paper that he took permission to sue afresh at the time of withdrawal of the earlier suit. 

16. From the aforesaid facts and circumstances it is clear that Mohammad Hossain Miah and/or his heirs (defendants Nos. 2 to 4), the vendor of the plaintiffs had no title and possession in the suit land. Moreover it appears that the auction purchase of the government has been confirmed on 4-12-1936 and within two months of confirmation Mohammad Hossain Miah obtained Kabuliyat in his favour which is not at all practicable. Apart from this it also appears that Title Suit. No. 70 of 1.969 filed by Mohammad Hossain Miah against the government for declaration of his title in respect of the self same property has been withdrawn on 23-3-1974 of course without permission to sue afresh, and interestingly the plaintiffs claim that the defendants Nos. 2 to 4 have sold the same to them by four. Kabala deeds on 25-3-1974 i.e. within two days of such withdrawal of the earlier suit and immediately after purchase the plaintiffs instituted the present suit in 1974. Thus the whole transaction appears to be concocted on the basis of some forged documents. 

17. Thus the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case and, as such, they are not entitled to get any relief and rather the defendants case that the suit land was under river for more than 20 (twenty) years and, as such, the title and possession has vested, in the Government, appears to be correct. 

18. On perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the High Court Division did not consider all these aspects of the case and erroneously made the Rule absolute. 

19. From the discussions made hereinabove we are of the view that the High Court Division committed serious error of law in making the Rule absolute and thereby the judgment and order of the High Court Division, is liable to be set aside. 

Accordingly, we find merit in this appeal and thus the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs and the judgment and order impugned herein, passed by the High Court Division is set aside. 

End.

None Represented—Respondent Nos. 2-56.
