case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 9-7-2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.714 of 1998).
full_judgment:
Borhanuddin, J: This appeal by leave has been filed against the judgment and order dated 9-7-2002 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.714 of 1998 making the Rule absolute against the judgment and order dated 18-9-1997 passed by the Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Laxmipur, in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Appeal No.38 of 1996 affirming the judgment and order dated 24-9-1996 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Laxmipur, dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.47 of 1993 filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.
2. Relevant facts for disposal of the appeal are that the respondent No.1 herein as pre-emptor-petitioner filed the miscellaneous case on 5-7-1993 stating inter alia that one Boli Mia @ Boli Mohammad was the original owner of the case land who died leaving behind one son Suja Mia and the said Suja Mia died leaving behind pre-emptor Nurul Amin @ Abu Taher, Vendor-opposite party Sekandar Mia and opposite party Nos. 3-5 as heirs; Suja Mia transferred 43 acres of land to the pre-emptor-petitioner by heba deed dated 18-2-1982 and thus the pre-emptor became a co-sharer of the holding by inheritance as well as on the basis of the heba deed; The pre-emptor had been serving in the Saudi Arabia since before the disputed transfer; Vendor-opposite party No.2 Sekandar Mia is the full brother of the pre-emptor-petitioner; Dispute relating to land exists between the brothers; The vendor opposite party No.2 transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 without serving statutory notice to the co-sharers; After returning home from Saudi Arabia, the pre-emptor came to know from his brother-in-law Noor Nabi on 12-5-1993 that the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 disclosed to him that he has purchased the case land from the vendor-opposite party No.2; Knowing about the said transfer, the pre-emptor on search procured certified copy of the kabala deed from the Maizdi Sub-register Office though the case land situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Laxmipur Sub-register Office; Getting definite information, the pre-emptor filed application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption affirming that the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 is a stranger to the case land and the pre-emptor has got less than 60 bighas of land. By amending plaint of the case it is further stated that the subsequent transfer dated 21-6-1992 by the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 infavour of the opposite party No.6 (predecessor of the appellants herein) is collusive and sham transaction.
3. That the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 contested the case by filing written objection contending inter cilia that the application for pre-emption is not maintainable, barred by limitation and also barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. His specific case in brief is that the vendor-opposite party No.2 sold the case land to him in consultation with the pre-emptor and his karjokarok Noor Nabi; The vendor sold the land for sending the pre-emptor to Saudi Arabia; The vendor by executing and registering kabala deed transferred the land to the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1; Thereafter, for necessity of money the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 transferred the land to the opposite party No.6 Abdur Rashid on 21-6-1992 who is a co-sharer of the holding and, as such, the application for pre-emption is liable to be rejected.
4. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record held that the application for pre-emption is not time barred and transfer by the vendor to the pre-emptee was beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor-petitioner. But the trial Court held that since the case land had been transferred by the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 to the opposite party No.6, a co-sharer of the holding, the application for pre-emption is not maintainable.
5. Being aggrieved, the pre-emptor-petitioner as appellant preferred miscellaneous appeal in the Court of the learned District Judge, Laxmipur, which was on transfer ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Laxmipur, who after hearing the parties affirmed the judgment of the trial Court that pre-emption is not tenable against a co-sharer.
5. Feeling aggrieved, the pre-emptor-appellant as petitioner moved before the High Court Division by filing revisional application and obtained Rule. After hearing the parties and perusing evidence on record, a Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute by setting aside the judgment and order of the Courts below.
7. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, successors of the co-sharer opposite party No.6 (who expired during pendency of the case before the trial Court) preferred instant civil petition for leave to appeal.
8. Leave was granted on the ground that prior to the filing of miscellaneous case on 5-7-1993 the pre-emptee transferred the case land to the co-sharer of the holding opposite party No.6 (in the miscellaneous case) on 21-6-1992 and, as such, no right of pre-emption was in existence on the date of filing of the miscellaneous case seeking pre-emption against the pre-emptee-opposite party and also on the ground that the High Court Division failed to consider the question of maintainability of the case on the background of the fact that when the miscellaneous case was filed against the pre-emptee he had no subsisting interest in the land sought to be pre-empted.
9. Mr Md Abdun Nur, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submits that prior to the filing of the miscellaneous case on 5-7-1993 the pre-emptee transferred the case land to the opposite party No.6 (in the miscellaneous case) on 21-6-1992 who was undeniably a co-sharer in the holding and, as such, no right of pre-emption was available on the date of filing of the miscellaneous case seeking pre-emption against the pre-emptee-opposite party and thus the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that the miscellaneous case is not tenable in the eye of law. Relying on the decision passed in the case of Hafiz Ahmed vs Ahmedur Rahman & others, reported in 48 DLR 170, learned Advocate also submits that 'the vendor and the vendee are permitted to avoid accrual of the right of pre-emption by all lawful means and the vendee may sell the property to a rival pre-emptor with preferential or equal right to defeat the right for pre-emption of another co-sharer. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate referred to the case of Shaft Khan vs Mannujan Hossain, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 225 and the case of Hafiz Ahmed vs Ahmedur Rahman and others, reported in 48 DLR 170.
10. On the other hand, Mr Khair Ezaz Masud learned senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 submits that the subsequent transfer is subject to right available against the original transfer whether the transfer was made before or after filing of the pre-emption application and, as such, pre-emptor's application for pre-emption merits success, although the vendee-opposite party. No.1 transferred the case land to his father opposite party No.6 Abdur Rashid who was a co-sharer in the holding by purchase, before the filing of the application for pre-emption. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate referred to the case of Hajera Bibi vs Noor Jahan Begum and others, reported in 35 DLR 238 and the case of Girija Nath Kundu vs Ahamad Ali Sardar and others reported in 50 CWN 806.
11. Heard the learned Advocates, perused the evidence on record as well as the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the parties. It appears that the trial Court though arrived at a finding that the pre-emptor had no knowledge about the disputed transfer and the case is not barred by limitation but dismissed the case holding that the opposite party No.6 was a co-sharer in the case land since before the transfer on 21-6-1992 as such prayer for pre-emption is not tenable.
12. The Appellate Court below affirmed the judgment of the trial Court that the miscellaneous case for pre-emption is not maintainable against a co-sharer inasmuch as opposite party No.6 admittedly was a co-sharer in the holding.
13. We have meticulously gone through the judgment passed by the High Court Division. The High Court Division in disposing of the civil revision decided two points of law.
14. The first one is whether the application for pre-emption is barred by limitation or not. The High Court Division after thorough discussions arrived at a finding that the miscellaneous case was filed within the time inasmuch as no statutory notice was served upon the pre-emptor-co-sharer and the pre-emptee disclosed about the transfer to the brother-in-law of the pre-emptor on 25-5-1993 and thereafter the pre-emptor on search procured certified copy of the deed from the Maizdi Sub-register Office on 27-5-1993 though the case land is situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Laxmipur, Sub-register Office.
15. The 2nd point which is vital and relevant to decide the controversy in the present case as to whether after transfer by pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 to co-sharer opposite party No.6 the pre-emptory right of the pre-emptor exists or not. The High Court Division after discussing the case reported in 48 DLR 170 and the case reported in 50 CWN page 806 and also the case reported in 35 DLR 238 concurred with the views taken by their lordships in the case of Hajera Bibi vs Noor Jahan Begum and others, reported in 35 DLR 238 and thus made the Rule absolute by setting aside the judgment and order passed by the Courts below.
16. On perusal of proviso to Sub-section (1) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it appears that the right of pre-emption is not available to a co-sharer tenant or tenants holding land contiguous to the land transferred unless he is a person to whom transfer of the holding or the portion or share thereof, as the case may be, can be made under section 90. Again, Sub-section (10) of section 96 provides that right of the pre-emption is not available in the following cases:
(a) a transfer to a co-sharer in the tenancy whose interest has accrued otherwise than by purchase; or
(b) a transfer by exchange or partition; or
© a transfer by bequest or gift (including Heba but excluding Heba-bil-Ewaj for any pecuniary consideration) in favour of the husband or wife or the testator or donor, or of any relation by consanguinity within three degrees of the testator or donor; or
(d) a simple or complete usufructuary mortgage, or, until a decree or order absolute for foreclosure is made, a mortgage by conditional sale; or
(e) a Waqf in accordance with the provisions of the Muhammadan Law; or
(f) a dedication for religious or charitable purposes without any reservation of pecuniary benefit for any individual. 17. Apart from this, our apex court denied right of pre-emption in the case when the vendee retransferred the land to the vendor and the right is barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence.
18. We have also gone through the judgment and order passed in the cited cases. In the case of Shafi Khan vs Mannujan Hossain reported in 35 DLR (AD) 225 referred by the learned Advocate for the appellants is a case of reconveyance wherein the land under pre-emption was sold by one Abdul Bari Khan to his nephew Ayesh Khan and the said Ayesh Khan retransferred the land to said Abdul Bari Khan one month before filing of the application for pre-emption as such this Division allowed the appeal by setting aside the orders allowing. pre-emption. In that case, this Division observed that:
"In the instant case, the learned Judges of the High Court Division placed reliance mainly on the decisions in the case of Girija Nath Kundu vs Ahamad Ali Sardar & others and Sic Lokman Ali vs Abdul Motalib & another, both reported in 50 CWN, the former at page 806 and the latter at page 807, decided by two different single Benches of the Calcutta High Court. But it is found that in neither of these two cases there was any reconveyance or re-sale to the original vendor, but the lands were retransferred to different persons other than the original vendor."
19. So it is clear that the Apex Court distinguished between the circumstance `reconveyance and re-sale to the original vendor' and `retransfer to different persons other than the original vendor'. Provisions relating to pre-emption in the case of `reconveyance and re-sale to the original vendor' and `retransfer to different person other than the vendor' are not same. On perusal of the case of Hajera Bibi vs Noor Jahan Begum and others reported in 35 DLR 238 it appears that the petitioner Hajera Bibi was a co-sharer in the holding and opposite party No.3 Abdul Khaleque transferred the case land by registered kabala to opposite party No.2 Syed Habibur Rahman and by another registered kabala opposite party No.3 Abdul Khaleque transferred a portion of land under khatian No.165 to opposite party Syed Mohibur Rahman. Opposite party No.3 Abdul Khaleque was also a co-sharer of the holding. Opposite party No.2 Syed Habibur Rahman was a stranger who transferred his purchased land to opposite party No.1 Noor Jahan Begum (opposite party No.10 in the said pre-emption case) on 26-8-1972. Thereafter, on 17-9-1973 the petitioner filed application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption depositing consideration money. In that case the contention of the opposite party No.1 Noor Jahan Begum was that since Syed Habibur Rahman already transferred his interest to Noor Milan Begum before filing of the application for pre-emption by the petitioner Hajera Bibi and, as such, the application for pre-emption was not maintainable and barred by limitation. The trial Court dismissed the case on the ground of limitation and the Appellate Court below held that since Syed Habibur Rahman sold the Case land to Noor Jahan Begum before filing of the application for pre-emption the Miscellaneous case is not maintainable. In deciding the case a Single Bench of the High Court Division referring the judgment of Civil Appeal No.50 of 1982 (Shay Khan vs Mannujan Hossain) observed that:
"In the judgment, the appellate Division has referred to the cases of Girija Nath Kundu and Sheikh Lokman Ali referred to earlier and has distinguished the facts of the case before it from the facts of those two cases on the ground that in neither of the cases there was any `reconveyance or re-sale' to the original vendor but the lands were 're-transferred' to different persons other than the original vendor. In the instant case before me also there was no 'reconveyance or re-sale' of the lands sought to be pre-empted to the original vendor but the lands were transferred to another stranger Nurjahan Begum. The Appellate Division has not disapproved the decisions of Girija Nath Kundu and Sheikh Lokman Ali and has made a distinction between these two cases and the case before it. I, with respect, agree with the principle of law laid down in those two reported cases. Following decision of Shiekh Lokman Ali in which case also the second transfer was made before an application for pre-emption was made, I hold that the petitioner Hajera Bibi's right to pre-empt subsists even though the second transfer was made before her filing of the application for pre-emption. In this view of the matter, I agree with the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr Khondakar Mahbubuddin Ahmed that the Courts below have taken an erroneous view of law and there has been an error of law apparent of the face of the record."
20. In the instant case before us the Appellate Court below placed reliance in the case reported in 48 DLR 170, wherein it is observed that: "The vendor and the vendee are, therefore, permitted to avoid accrual of the right of pre-emption by lawful means. The vendee may defeat the right by selling the property to a rival pre-emptor with preferential or equal right."
21. In the 48 DLR case one Nazamat Ali gifted the case land to his daughter-in-law Najuma by a deed of gift dated 31-1-1980 who gifted the same to her husband by another deed of gift dated 07-4-1980. Thereafter, the pre-emptor Ahmedur Rahman filed application for pre-emption on 30-3-1981 claiming himself as a co-sharer. It appears that his lordship in passing the judgment reported in 48 DLR 170 quoted the aforementioned portion from the case of Bishan Singh, reported in AIR 1958 (SC) 838. In deciding the case reported in 48 DLR 170 his lordship refused the prayer for pre-emption mainly on the ground that the impugned deed was deed of gift and the same was not pre-emptable. In the case of Girija Nath Kundu vs Ahamad Ali Sardar, reported in 50 CWN 806, his lordship observed:
"As soon as a transfer of a share in a holding is effected a right to pre-empt immediately accrues to the co-sharer tenants and any subsequent transferee of the property must take it subject to that right. If at any time after an application for pre-emption has been made it comes to the notice of the co-sharer applicants for pre-emption that the property has been again transferred there is nothing in the section as it stands, to prevent the subsequent transferee from being made a party to the proceedings, as was done in the case with which we are now dealing, and it seems to me that section 26F(5) of the Act was expressly framed to provide that in certain suitable cases the money which had been deposited might be paid to a subsequent transferee."
<u>22. In deciding the case reported in 35 DLR 238 his lordship taking into consideration of the above cited decision and an unreported case of Shaft Khan vs Mannujan Hossain (Civil Appeal No.50 of 1982), subsequently reported in 35 DLR (AD) 225, observed as under:</u>
<u>"The petitioner Hajera Bibi's right to pre-empt subsists even though the second transfer was made before her filling of the application for pre-emption."</u>
<u>23. In the present case the vendor-opposite party Sekandar Mia sold the case land to pre-emptee-opposite party Feroj Mia who was a stranger in the case land and said Feroj Mia transferred the land to opposite party No.6 Abdur Rashid, predecessor of the present appellants, on 21-6-1992 who was a co-sharer in the holding as such considering the view taken by their lordship in the case of 50 CWN 806 as well as 35 DLR 238 and also distinguishing the facts of 35 DLR (AD) 225, We have no hesitation to hold that even after subsequent transfer by the stranger pre-emptee to another co-sharer of the holding, the pre-emptory right of a co-sharer pre-emptor will not be defeated as because the subsequent transfer is subject to the right available against the original transfer and the subsequent transferee would be impleaded as party in the pre-emption proceeding and he would be entitled to get the consideration and compensation money as deposited by the pre-emptor.</u>
24. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, we are of the view that the High Court Division rightly and legally passed the impugned judgment and order dated 9-7-2002 in Civil Revision No.714 of 1998.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
However, without any order as to costs.
End.

full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J : This appeal at the instance of the defendant No.3-Eastern Food (Pvt.) Limited has been preferred against the judgment and decree dated 4-2-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 decreeing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract on compromise. 

2. The present appeal was sent to this court by the Hon'ble Chief Justice by order dated 15-7-2018 to be heard and disposed of by the Division Bench presided over by AKM Abdul Hakim, J. 

3. The respondent No. 1 MNH Bulu as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka on 7-2-2008 seeking a decree for Specific Perfor-mance of Contract impleading the respondent No. 2 Mrs. Hosn-e-Ara and respondent No. 3 Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK), Dhaka as defendants. 

4. The plaint case, in short, is that the suit plot morefully described in the schedule of the plaint belonged to Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) now Rajuk; that Late Abu Ahmed Shah, husband of Hosn-e-Ara, defendant No. I got allotment of 15 khatas, 14 chattak land of plot No. CWN (B) 28 of Gulshan Model Town from DIT by allotment letter contained in memo No. 2725 dated 7-4-1962, subsequently on the prayer of the original allotee, Dhaka Improvement Trust DIT allowed the prayer accordingly Lease Agreement was executed between the defendant No. 1 and DIT by registered Lease Deed No. 8832 dated 22-9-1964; that after obtaining approval of construction plan by the DIT, defendant No.1 constructed a one-storied building upon the said plot taking loan from the East Pakistan House Building Finance Corporation by mortgaging the plot and had been residing thereon; that after libration war said plot was enlisted in the `kha' list of the abandoned property under President Order No. 16 of 1972 (PO 16 of 1972); that the defendant No. 1 filed Settlement Case No. 360 of 1995 in the Court of Settlement releasing the said property from the list of abandoned property. After hearing, the case was allowed and the government was directed to release her property from the list of abandoned property by judgment and order dated 29-6-1996. Against the order of the court of settlement, the government filed Writ Petition No. 710 of 2002 in the Hon'ble High Court Division, after hearing the said writ petition was discharged and judgment of the court of settlement was upheld; that the defendant No. 1 expressed her desire to sell the suit plot due to necessity and plaintiff agreed to purchase the same, after discussions between them, defendant No. 1 entered into an Bainanama Agreement for sale of the suit land and building at .a total consideration of Taka 4 core and out of total consideration money, defendant No. 1 received Taka 3 core 90 lac as earnest money (Baina Money) from the plaintiff and executed a registered Bainanama Agreement being No. 6359 dated 3-4-2006. That further case of the plaintiff is that an application was filed on 4-12-2001 for publication of Gazette Notification for release of the suit property from the `kha' list of Abandoned Property. Ultimately gazette notification was published on 6-9-2007 after much effort and great contribution and .help made by the plaintiff. That the plaintiff after publication of the gazette notification on 6-9-2007, the plaintiff repeatedly requested the defendant No. 1 to execute and register the sale deed on receipt of the balance consideration money Taka 10 lac; that inspite of repeated demand by the plaintiff, the defendant No. I did not execute and register the kabala. Finally on 23-10-2007, the plaintiff requested the defendant No. 1 to execute and register the kabala deed but defendant No. 1 informed that if the plaintiff did not increase the price of the suit plot in addition to balance consideration money she will not execute and register the sale deed. Hence the suit. 

5. At the, time of filing of the suit on 7-2-2008, plaintiff by firisty filed two documents namely (i) Photocopy of the certified copy of the registered Bainanama No. 6359 dated 6-4-2006 (ii) Original Bangladesh Bank Chalan No. 8308 dated 6-2-2008 showing payment of balance consideration money Taka 10 lac. 

6. Defendant No. 1, Mrs. Hosn-e-Ara entered appeared in the suit on 10-3-2008 but did not contest the suit by filing any written statement. 

7. Defendant No. 2 RAJUK entered into appearance and contested the suit by filing written statement dated 28-3-2011 and better statement on 9-2-2015 stating that the suit is not maintainable in the present form, suit filed without giving statutory notice under the. Town Improvement Act, 1983 barred under estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and also under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The positive case of the defendant No.2, in brief, is that the suit property was allotted by. the DIT in favour of Hosn-erAra; that on 15-3-2005 she requested the RAJUK to attorn Ms. Nazma Khan as her constituted attorney in respect of her CWN (B) Plot No.28 Gulshan Residential Area; that it appears from the Memo issued by the Ministry of Housing and Works dated 22-10-2006 that said plot was released from the `kha' list of the abandoned property; that Nazma Khan filed some documents to transfer the said plot to Eastern Foods (Pvt.) PW 1, was cross-examined by the defendant No.2 RAJUK on 13-11-2014 and 27-11-2014. That PW1 in his examination-in-chief stated that "আমি এই মামলার বাদী পক্ষে নিযুক্ত আমমোক্তার”. But he did not file any power-of-attorney in the present suit. In cross-examination he stated that— In cross-examination he further stated that—

“আমি বাদীর কর্মচারী। বাদীদের পক্ষে সাক্ষ্য দিতেছি। আমি বাদীর আমমোক্তার । আমি আমমোক্তার নামা আদালতে দাখিল করেছি। নালিশী জমির মূল মালিক, পাজউক |” In cross-examination he further_stated that “এই প্লট পাই এই বাদী এবং আদালতে আরো একটি মামলা করেছে। পরে বলে জানিনা | ঐ মামলাটি অত্রাদালতে করেছে কিনা জানিনা । দেঃ ৩৯৮/২০০৩ মামলাটি খারিজ হইয়াছে, কিনা আমি জানিনা । আমরা মামলার পূর্বে রাজউককে আমরা নোটিশ দিয়েছি। আরজিতে নোটিশ সম্পর্কে উল্লেখ আছে কিনা বলতে পারবো না। সত্য নয় যে, নোটিশ সম্পর্কে আরজিতে উল্লেখ নাই। নোটিশের কপি আমার কাছে আছে। কোর্টে দাখিল করি নাই । নালিশী জমি রাজউকের অধীন্যস্ত। আমরা রাজউকের অনুমতি নেই নাই কারণ বায়না করতে রাজউকের অনুমতি লাগে না। হোসনে আরা বোনের সাথে বায়না করেছি হোসনে আরা পাকিস্তানি কিনা জানি না। সে বাঙ্গালি হোসনে আরা দাখিলী ছবি ও আমার দাখিলী হোসনে আরার ছবির সাথে মিল নাই মর্মে রাজউক পত্র দিয়াছেন কিনা জানিনা ৷ সত্য নহে আমাদেরকে হাজির হতে বলিলে আমরা হাজির হই নাই । হোসনে আরা বাঙ্গালি মর্মে সনদ আনতে বলেছিল কিনা আমার মনে নাই। সত্য নয় যে, আমার বায়নাপত্র ভুয়া। সত্য নয় যে, এই কারণে নালিশী জমি পরিত্যক্ত সম্পত্তি হইয়াছিল ।............... সত্য নয় যে, হোসনে আরা বলতে কেউ নাই, আমাকে দিয়ে বাদী মিথ্যা স্বাক্ষী দিয়েছেন ।”

31. In the suit one Md. Tarikul Islam depose on behalf of RAJUK as DW 1 on 4-5-2015 and 25-1-2016. DW I in his examination-in-chief stated that—
“আমি রাজউকের পক্ষে ক্ষমতাপত্র মূলে সাক্ষ্য দিচ্ছি। এই সেই ক্ষমতাপত্রে দাখিল করিলাম, প্রদঃ-“ক’ CW(B) নং-১৮ প্লট এর জমির পরিমাণ ১৫ কাঠা ১২ছটাক। ------ PO মূলে (১৬/৭২) পরিত্যক্ত হয়।----- এরপর একাধিক ব্যক্তি এই প্লট হোসনে আরা পক্ষে দাবী করছে। এই দাবীকারীগণের মধ্যে-------, ইন্টার্ণ ফুডস লিঃ আজিম উদ্দিন চৌধুরী এবং MNH বুলু গং । এই কারণে Writ Petition No.710 of 2002, ৫৮৪৫/২০০৯, ডিক্রী জারী মামলা-২০৯/২০০৯, দেওয়ানী-৫৪৪/২০০৯, দেওয়ানী ৪২৩/২০১৩, Writ Petition No- 995 of 2013 Petition No-995 of 2013 মামলা গুলো চলমান। প্লটটি এখনও রাজউকের দখলে আছে। পরিত্যক্ত তালিকাভুক্ত আছে। সত্য নয় যে, বাদী আমাদের নিকট হস্তান্তরের অনুমতি চেয়েছে । মামলা খারিজ হবে । " In cross-examination he-further stated that ”………….. হোসনে আরা এই বাদীর সাথে বায়না চুক্তি করেছে এমন রাজউকের জানা নাই ।............. সত্য নয় যে, বাদীর নিকট হতে হোসনে আরার বৈধ পনের মাধমে চুক্তি হয়েছে তা রাজউক জানে হেতু আমরা জবাবে তার নাম উল্লেখ করেছি কিংবা বাদীর চুক্তি বৈধ । বাদীর চুক্তির বিষয়ে রাজউক অবহিত নয় ”

32. Upon consideration of the evidence of PW I and DW I it is crystal clear that the RAJUK being Lessor is not aware about the disputed Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 and Defendant No. I Lessee obtained any permission from the Lessor RAJUK before executing the alleged Bainanama for transferring the suit property in favour of plaintiff. 33. Subsequently, on 6-9-2015 defendant No.1 and plaintiff filed a joint compromise petition. But it is very surprising that Solenama was not filed under the signature of the plaintiff and he was not depose in the suit and the PW 1. who depose on behalf of the plaintiff did not tile any power-of-attorney, which clearly proved that the Solenama was not executed by the plaintiff and he did not appear in the court to prove the said Solenama. Thus the plaintiff miserably failed to prove the registered Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 and compromise petition dated 6-9-2015 and same were not marked as exhibits in the suit. 

34. On scrutiny of the case record, it appears that no list of exhibited documents were available in the record and the plaintiff to prove the case did not file the Original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006. It is apparent from the order sheet that the defendant No. 1 and plaintiff deposed on 6-9-2015 to prove the Solenama filed by the plaintiff and defendant No.1 but did not file the original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 on 6-9-2015 but the trial cowl decreed the suit on compromise on 4-2-2016 as per Solemnama dated 6-9-2015 and. accordingly decree was prepared on 11-2-2016. 35. Thus it is crystal clear that without filing the original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 suit was compromised on 6-9-2015 but later on 9-11-2015 the original bainama was filed which is evident from Order No. 58 dated 9-11-2015 and surprisingly no documents including the original Bainanama was exhibited in the suit. Although there was a serious dispute with regard to the genuineness of the Bainanama and the signature appearing in the said Bainanama. So far execution of the Bainanama by the defendant No.1 in favour of the plaintiff, the defendant No.2 and defendant No.3 claimed that the said agreement was forged agreement created for the purpose of grabbing of suit land by the plaintiff. From the materials on record.it appears that although the defendant No.3 filed an application for verifying the signature of the defendant No.1 in the baina and to get expert opinion. 

36. Section 107(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure has empowered the appellate court for a comparison by itself when necessary under Section 73 of the Evidence Act. In view of the said authority, we have examined and compared the signature of the defendant No. 1 appearing in the Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 with the admitted signature appearing in the documents mentioned namely—1) Vokalatnama filed by defendant No.1 in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008, 2) compromise petition dated 6-9-2015 filed by the plaintiff and defendant No.1, 3) deposition sheet of Hosn-e-Ara as DW I in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 dated 6-9-2015. 4) signature of the original lease agreement dated 22-9-1964 between DIT and Hosn-e-Ara and thumb impression appear therein, and 5) signature in mortgaged-deed dated 27-8-. 1970. between defendant No. 1 and The East Pakistan House Building Finance Corporation. After comparison, it is evident that the signature appearing in the above documents do not appear to be identical/similar with the signature appearing in the Bainanama in question dated 3-4-2006 (Exhibit-4) as such the case of the plaintiff regarding the Exhibit-4 is not proved. 

37. It appears that at the time of filing of the compromise petition on 6-9-2015, the defendant No.1 filed fresh power again through his Advocate Liaquat Ali, whose power was cancelled earlier by the court on 29-11-2006 in Title Suit No. 398 of 2006, subsequently renumbered Title Suit No. 5972 of 2008 which will be heard analogously with present Title Suit No. 682 of 2008. It also appears that defendant No.3 filed an application in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 on 9-11-2015 praying for rejection of the compromise petition filed by the defendant No. l. but the learned Joint District Judge by order dated 9-11-2015 kept the same with the record stating that the same will be considered at the time of final adjudication of the suit. From those evidences is creates a series of doubt about the genuineness and bonafide of the agreement in question and inspired us to believe that the case of alleged contract on sale of the suit property and the case of reducing the contract into an agreement have been founded 'upon bundles of false hood. 

38. It is apparent on the face of the record that none of the documents upon the strength of which suit has been decreed on compromise, have been legally tendered in evidence. Not a single document bears endorsement which is required under Order XIII, rule 4 and 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The trial judge has failed to comply with the most material requirement of the-Code of Civil Procedure. Had it been necessary for us to deal with the evidence it would have been impossible to do so upon present record as hardly a single document has been admitted in accordance with the provisions of Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Joint District Judge must strictly comply with the provisions of Order, XII, rules 4 and 5 of the Civil Procedure Code.

39. In view of the above we are constrained to hold that the learned Joint District Judge without considering the material evidence on record and erroneously considered the Solenama dated 6-9-2015 and the registered Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 decreed the suit illegally. The plaintiff and the defendant No.1 have hopelessly failed to prove the Solenama upon which the compromise decreed was passed on the basis of the Bainanama agreement. 

40. This matter was heard by this Bench on good number of days and on the last three occasions Mr AKM Faiz, the learned Advocate appeared with Mr Shishir Kanti Majumder, Advocate for the respondent No.1 and when asked by this court, whether it will be possible on the part of the respondent No. 1 to produce Hosn-e-Ara before this court for proper adjudication and final settlement of the case. In reply, Mr AKM Faiz, learned Advocate on earlier two occasions submits that it will be possible to produce Hosn-e-Ara before This court after her return from Chennai, where she is now staying for her medical treatment. Since the respondent No. 1 took adjournments, accordingly the date of delivery of judgment was adjourned till 10-12-2018. On that date on the prayer of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 delivery of the judgment of the appeal was deferred till today. Today (14-1-2019) Mr Shishir Karti Majumder, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 without producing Hosn-e-Ara, submitted her original passport being No. 0442656 issued on 3-1-2019 along with a NID card being No. 2695-0469-48339 which was issued by the respective authorities on 29-4-2008 showing her address Holding No. 3/3(1) Chand Mia Housing, post Office Mohammadpur, 1207, Dhaka City Corporation and also filed photocopy of her earlier passport No. 095540 issued on 21-4-014. 

41. In this connection it is very important to note that the trial court by Order No. 57 dated 21-10-2015 fixed Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 for hearing Joint compromise application filed by the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and also for appearance of the original plaintiff, MNH Bulu. The defendant No. l submitted photocopy of her NID card and copy of passport those documents were be kept with the record. Plaintiff MNH Bulu his constituted attorney, Anowarul Kabir and defendant No.1 appeared in person in court and submitted their respective signature before the court and learned Joint District Judge passed order dispensing the personal appearance of plaintiff and defendant No.1 and prayer of defendant No.3 is allowed. But surprisingly enough those documents are not available in the case record. Moreover, plaintiff did not give any explanation why he appointed Anowarul Kabir as his constituted attorney. Later on 9-11-2015 plaintiff filed original Bainanama No. 6359 dated 3-4-2006 by filing firisty on that date. In the judgment the trial court failed to take notice of the fact that the plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 429 of 2006 on 2-11-2006 for Specific Performance of Contract impleading the present defendant No.1, Hosn-e-Ara and defendant No.2 RAJUK as defendants. In the said suit present plaintiff showed last cause of action on 10-10-2006 but did not deposit balance consideration money of Taka 10 lac at the time of filing of the plaint, which is a pre-condition in filing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract for sale of any immovable property. Since the plaintiff did not file: the balance consideration money in accordance with the amended provision of Specific Relief Act, the trial court rejected the plaint as the suit is barred under Section 21A Sub-clause (b) of the Specific Relief Act. 

42. It further appears that the plaintiff filed the present suit on 7-2-2008 showing the last cause of action on 23-10-2007 which is clearly barred by limitation under the principle of res-judicata. The trial court should have also considered that the Title Suit No. 398 of 2006 subsequently renumbered as 5972 of 2008 which was filed by the present plaintiff for permanent injunction. Later on, in the present suit learned Joint District Judge passed an order on 22-10-2008 that the present suit will be heard analogously with Title Suit No. 398 of 2006. Subsequently, on the prayer of the plaintiff Title Suit No. 5972 of 2016 was withdrawn by order dated 4-2-2016. 

43. Admittedly registered Bainanama was executed on 2-4-206 and same was registered in the Sub-registrar Office, Gulshan on 3-4-2006 being Deed No. 6359. We have gone through the computer typed Bainanama but in the last page of Bainanama the date was put by hand. Further the said Bainanama was not registered complying the rule 20 of the Bangladesh Registration Rules 1973, clause (J) of the said Rule clearly provide that photographs of both the parties should have been pasted in the instrument and the parties have put their respective signatures and left thumb impressions across their photographs in the instruments (Section 22A(2). But in the present case Bainanama was registered without following the said provision of law. It further appears that the Bainanama was written on a stamp paper of denomination of Taka 150 and affidavit was affirmed upon stamp of Taka 50 only. But proper stamp duty of instrument of Agreement is fixed at Taka 300 under Article 5 of schedule (1) and Affidavit is required to be stamped at Taka 200 under Article 4 of schedule (I) of the Stamp Act, 1899. 

44. It further appears from the NID card of Hosn-e-Ara which was filed today before this court along with the original passport and photocopy of earlier passport the signature appearing in the NID card does not tally with the signature of Hosn-e-Ara Defendant No.1. In the NID card the signature of Hosn-e-Ara is in Bengali but the documents mentioned above the signature of Hosn- e-Ara appears in English. Further it is apparent from the Bainanama that the  address of the present defendant No. 1 is Plot No.28, House No. 119 Block-CWN(B) Gulshan Road, Dhaka but in the NID card filed in court today, her address was shown holding No. 3/3(1) Chand Mia Housing, Post Office Mohammadpur, 1207, Dhaka City Corporation. 

45. It is by now settled that relief under Specific Relief Act, 1877 for enforcement of contract is discretionary with the court and that if any fraud practice is found to have been made in any contract there remains no scope for enforcement of the contract from a court of law. In this respect we can profitably referred the decision reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 51 wherein it has been held that: 
"Specific performance is an equitable relief but equity is not available to a person whose intention is not honest, rather who, by raising a false claim attempted to practice fraud and cause total deprivation to the proposed vendor." 

46. Referring to the case of Jogesh Chandra Das and others vs Farida Hasan, 1983 BLD (AD) 225 where it was observed that-
"under Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act a decree for Specific Performance of Contract is discretionary and the court is not bound to grant such relief merely because it is lawful to do so. Specific Performance of Contract is not to be granted as a matter of course." 

47. For the reasons, we are of the view that the learned Joint District Judge erroneously considered the documents and believed the Bainanama which was not proved and marked Exhibit in the suit but the Joint District Judge illegally decreed the suit on compromise. When the plaintiff totally failed to prove the existence of Bainanama and the signature as contained in the Bainanama is not the signature of the defendant no-1 as appeared from the admitted documents kept in the record.. Moreover, it is evident that defendant No.1 did not obtain any sale permission from the Lessor-RAJUK-defendant No.2 before executing the Bainanama for transferring the suit property in favour of the plaintiff. Thus the impugned judgment and decree are not sustainable in law. 

48. In the result the appeal is allowed and the connected Rile being Civil Rule No. 119(F) of 2016 is disposed of. The judgment and decree dated 4-2-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 are set-aside. The suit is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

Send down the lower court record along with a copy of this judgment at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Mohammad Arshadur Rouf, Advocate-For the petitioners.
Prahlad Debnathe, A4G with Shovana Banu, AAG, with Faruk Hossain, Advocate-For the defendant-OP. No. 1.

Shamsul Haq (Md) and another ……… Plaintiffs-Respondents-Petitioners
vs
Chairman, No. 2, Chapair Union Parishad and others ……… Defendants- Appellants-Opposite-Parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015, passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No. 56 of 2015, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008, passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 120 of 2004, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, are that, one Sharnsul Haque and Md Nazrul Islam, had filed Title Suit No. 120 of 2004, before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur, against the Chairman, No. 2, Chapair Union Parishad, Kaliakoir, Gazipur, and 44 others, seeking partition in respect of the suit property by way of allotting [5467/100] decimals of land out of 350 decimals, described in the schedule to the plaint. The pleadings of the plaintiffs need not be repeated, since these are maintained in the LCR and I have gone though the same.

3. Only the defendant No. 1, i.e. the Chairman of No. 2, Chapair Union Parishad, had contested in the suit by filing written statements on 25-8-2005, whereby it has denied the case of the plaintiffs and stated its own case at paragraph No. 10 of the written statements. The ease of the defendant No. 1 need not be repeated, since, the same is maintained in the LCR and I have gone through the same.

4. It appears that, the plaintiffs has produced 6 witnesses namely, PWs 1-6 and also produced certain documents which have been marked as Exhibit 1 to 5, 5, 5(Ka), 6, 6(Ka), 7, 7(Ka), 8, 8(Ka), 9, 9(Ka). The certified copy of CS khatian No. 69 (Exhibit), 3 original title deeds (exhibit 2-4) and the certified Copy of the SA and RS khatian (Exhibit 5 and 6 series), respectively. Besides, Exhibit 7 is also an original deed No. 1767 dated 4-4-1994, Exhibit 7(Ka) to 9(Ka) are the signatures of the PWs No. 3 to 5, who are the deed writers. Having examined the order sheet of the trial court, I find that, the defendant, did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence.

5. After perusing the documents and evidence on record, the trial curt decreed the suit ex-parte on 7-4-2008. Thereafter, the trial court has appointed an Advocate Commissioner vide order dated 3-11-2008 for the purpose of measurement and demarcation of the suit property claimed by the plaintiff and also for the purpose of allotment of Saham. The Advocate Commissioner submitted a report on 10-5-2009, which was accepted by the trial court on 14-6-2009 and preliminary decree dated 10-4-208 has been made final i.e. the Court has passed the final decree on 10-11-2009 and ordered that, the Advocate Commissioner's report dated 10-4-2009, Field Book, Chitta, Map etc. do form part of the final decree. Thereafter, the decree-holder filed an Execution Case No. 1 of 2011 and from the order dated 6-5-2013 of the said execution case, it appears that the judgment-debtor i.e. the defendant No. 1 Union Parishad has appeared in the executing court by filing Vokalatnama and prayed for time for filing written objection against the warrant of possession. It further appears from the order dated 15-10-2014 of the executing court that, the judgment-debtor took time on 17 dates, from 6-5-2013 to 15-10-2014, but the defendant No. 1 did not file any written objection before the court and the executing court has recorded that,
“এমতাবস্থায় মোকদ্দমাটি অযথা আপত্তি দাখিলের নামে সময় অতিবাহিত করা আদালতে কাছে যুক্তি যুক্ত প্রতিয়মান না হওয়ায় দখলী কার্যক্রম সন্তোষজনক হওয়���য় মোকদ্দমাটি নিম্পত্তিযোগ্য। অতএব,
আদেশ হয় যে,
অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি পূর্ণ সন্তোষ্টিতে নিষ্পত্তি করা হইল।”

6. Then, after expiry of 1,896 days delay, the judgment-debtor-defendant No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 56 of 2013 along with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, for condonation of delay and it appears that, the appellate court has condoned this inordinate delay and had admitted the appeal. Thereafter, by the impugned judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015 (decree signed on 14-10-2015, the appellate court has decided to remand the case to the trial court for ends of justice so that. the contesting defendant No. 1 get an opportunity to adduce evidence in support of it's claim and accordingly by the judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015, it has set-aside the judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008 of the trial court, passed in Title Suit No. 120 of 2004 and sent back the case on remand for allowing opportunity to the defendant No. 1 to adduce oral and documentary evidences. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015 of the appellate court, the plaintiffs-respondents have filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and obtained the present Rule.

8. Learned Advocate Mr Md Arshadur Rouf appeared on behalf of the petitioners. He having place the revisional application submits that, the defendant No. 1-appellant-petitioners appeared in the suit and had filed written statements and hearing of the suit continued on several dates and the plaintiffs had adduced as many as 6 witnesses and had proved all relevant documents, which were marked as Exhibit 1-9 series. He also submits that, the trial court, having considered oral and documentary evidences, was satisfied that the plaintiffs have proved the case and accordingly it had passed the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008. He next submits that, there was no error of law, nor the trial court has committed any error in passing the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008 and the same did not occasion any failure of justice. He proceeds on that, as per provision of  law, the plaintiffs has applied for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for making measurement and inspection of the suit property and as per prayer of the plaintiffs an Advocate Commissioner was appointed and he had submitted his report on 10-5-2009. But, the defendant did not file any objection against the said report of the Advocate Commissioner and the trial court had accepted the said report dated 10-5-2009 along with the field book, chitta, map etcetera filed by the Advocate Commissioner with his report, and passed the final decree on 10-11-2009. The learned Advocate further submits that, all these steps were taken by the plaintiffs and the final decree was passed in accordance with law. He proceeds on that, thereafter, the plaintiffs has filed Execution Case No. 1 of 2011 in the proper forum for warrant of delivery of possession in the suit property, as per their respective shares or saham. In the said Execution case No. I of 2011, the defendant No. 1 i.e. the Union Parishad had appeared by filing Vokalatnama and had prayed for time against warrant of delivery of possession, and their petition for time was allowed and, even after taking adjournments on 17 dates, the defendant No. 1 did not file any objection, nor it had filed any petition under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, against the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008 and, as such there was a delay of 1896 days and the said delay was condoned by the appellate court, as if it were routine, and it had allowed the appeal only on the ground that, the defendant No. 1-appellant could not adduce any oral and documentary evidence before the trial court, hence, for ends of justice, it should be given an opportunity to adduce oral and documentary evidence before the trial court and sent back the suit on remand, accordingly. The learned Advocate further submits that, the judgment and order of the appellate court is contrary to the provisions of law in as much as a case could not be sent back on remand to give any opportunity to either of the parties to improve its case. He also submits that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court was contrary to the decision reported in 1 MLR (AD) 1996 page 430 = 49 DLR (AD) 77: Feroz Alam and others vs Zobaida Nahar @ Zharna and others, which he read out. Besides, he proceeds on that, the appellate court has not at all record any circumstance that had prevented the defendant-appellant from adducing the oral and documentary evidence before the trial court in support of their case, inspite of filing written statement and he had asserted the fact that, the defendant-judgment-debtor had took time on 17 dates for filing written objection against the warrant to deliver possession, as recorded in the order dated 15-10-2014, whereby the execution case has been finally disposed of, vide the certified copy, annexed to the application for revision. He also submits that, the plea that the previous Chairman of the defendant No. 1 did not inform about Title Suit No. 120 of 2004 is a lame excuse and is totally false, unprecedented and unreasonable in as much as an Union Parishad is a local authority and has its permanent establishment to manage it's affairs. Therefore, the plea that the earlier Union Parishad Chairman was busy in his election, hence, he could not take any step in the suit or in the execution case are all simply absurd and not cogent grounds in as much as an election is a matter of personal interest of that Chairman candidate and it has nothing to do with the business of the Union Parishad. He further submits that, considering the matter in its totality and in view of the law laid down by the Appellate Division, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute.

8. On the contrary, Mr Prahlad Debnath, AAG with Mrs. Shovana Banu, AAG and Mr Faruk Hossain, Advocate have appeared on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite party No. 1, Their main contention is that, the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners did not challenge the order of condonation of delay and that, the impugned judgment and decree was passed by the appellate court to protect the public interest in as much as the property of an Union Parishad was included the property of the plaintiffs. Besides, the learned Advocates also submit that, the court of Senior Assistant Judge did not at all discuss the oral and documentary evidence in the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008. They also submits that, in the schedule to the plaint corresponding RS and DS plot number has not been mentioned which is a vital defect and the trial Court did not notice the same. Hence, the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court, whereby it has set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008 of the trial court, is lawful and the appellate court has committed no error of law, nor it has resulted in any error in the decision, nor the same has occasioned any failure of justice in as much as both the parties will have an opportunity to adduce oral and documentary evidences in Support of their respective cases before the trial court, if the matter is heard afresh. In support of their contention, they have relied upon the decision reported in 40 DLR (AD) 101: Jobeda Khatun and others vs Md Hamid Ali being dead his heirs Taherun Nessa and others where in it has been held that,
"Remand to the trial court to decide the respective saham of all co-sharers in the partition suit upon examination of documents and witness afresh"

9. The learned Advocates also relied upon another decision reported in 68 DLR 399: between Moniruddin (Md) vs Md Salauddin Sarker and others wherein it has been held that,
"Mere mistake in the schedule to the plaint a party should not suffer and should not be deprived of getting relief as prayed for"
They conclude that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged.

10. I have heard the learned Advocates appeared for the parties, perused the revisional application, the supplementary-affidavit and the evidence, oral and documentary as well as the L.C.R.

11. I find that, the defendant No. 1-appellant-petitioners appeared in the suit and have filed written statements and hearing of the suit was continuing on several dates and the Plaintiffs have adduced as many as 6 witnesses and proved all relevant documents, which have been marked as Exhibit 1-9 series. I also find that, the trial court, having considered oral and documentary evidences and being satisfied that the plaintiffs have proved their case, it has passed the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008. Hence, as per provision of law, the plaintiffs have applied for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for making measurement and inspection of the suit property and, as per prayer of the plaintiffs, an Advocate Commissioner was appointed and he had submitted his report on 10-5-2009. But, the defendant did not file any objection against the said report of the Advocate Commissioner and the trial court has accepted the said report dated 10-5-2009, along with the field book, chitta, map etcetera, filed by the Advocate Commissioner along with his report, and passed the final decree on 10-11-2009.

12. All these steps were taken by the plaintiffs and the final decree was passed in accordance with law. Thereafter, the plaintiffs have filed Execution Case No. 1 of 2011 in the proper forum, for warrant of delivery of possession of the suit property. In the said Execution case No. 1 of 2011, the defendant No. 1 i.e. the Union Parishad, has appeared by filing Vokalatnama and prayed for time to file objection against warrant of delivery of possession. Their prayer for time was allowed by the executing court. But, even after taking adjournment on 17 dates, the defendant No. 1 did not file any objection, nor it has filed any petition under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, against the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008 and, as such, there was a delay of 1,896 days and the said delay was condoned by appellate court and it had also allowed the appeal only on the ground that, the defendant No. 1-appellant could not adduce any oral and documentary evidence before the trial court, i.e. to improve its eases.

13. However, the appellate court has set-aside the ex-parte decree of the trial court, on the plea of ends of justice and the suit was sent back on remand.

14. In view of the series of decisions of the Apex Court and the trend of law declared by it, I am constrained to hold that the judgment and decree of the appellate court is contrary to law in as much as a case cannot be sent back on remand to give an opportunity to the defendant Union Parishad, to improve its case when it is evidently guilty of gross neglect of duty and also for abusing the process of the court. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court was contrary to the decision laid down in 1 MLR (AD) 1996 page 430 = 49 DLR (AD) 77: Feroz Alam and others vs Zobaida Nahar@Zharnaand others, wherein it has been held that,
"Order for remand of a case for retrial cannot be made when the petitioner was found extremely negligent and was pursuing the proceeding with vexatious conduct. The discretion in the name of ends of justice must not be exercised capriciously or as sweet. will of a court without having justified ground."

15. Besides, the appellate court has not at all recorded any circumstance, to justify its order of remand, that bad prevented the defendant-appellant from adducing its oral and documentary evidence before the trial court in support of their case inspite of filing written statement. It is axiomatic that, the plea that the previous Chairman of the defendant No. 1 did not inform about Title Suit No. 120 of 2004 is totally false, unprecedented and unreasonable in as much as an Union Parishad is a local authority and it has permanent office and establishment to look after all its affairs and cases etcetera. Besides, the candidacy of the previous Chairman is matter of his personal interest and not of the public interest.

16. Considering the matter in its totality and in view of the law declared by the Appellate Division, I am of the considered opinion that, the case reported in 1 MLR (AD) 1996 page 430 = 49 DLR (AD) 77, squarely applies in the facts and circumstances of this case.

17. In view of the judgment of the Appellate Division, reported in 1 MLR (AD) 430 = 49 DLR (AD) 77, the appellate court has committed grave error of law in sending back the case on remand and the same is liable to be set-aside on this ground alone, since it fails in all the tests laid down in section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

18. Besides, the appellate court has not recorded any reason to show that, the defendant-Union Parishad had adducing any oral and documentary evidence before the trial court inspite of taking any honest effort or being diligent in any manner. The appellate court even did not consider that the defendant-Union Parishad even does not file any written objection, before the executing court, against the warrant to deliver of possession, even after taking time on 17 dates, hence, the executing court has disposed of the execution case, for the reasons stated in it's order dated 15-10-2014.

19. In such circumstances, ends of justice is not to be considered only for the defendant-appellant alone, but ends of justice will be considered in respect of the plaintiffs as well, which the appellate court has failed to appreciate, perhaps being an one eyed court.

20. Moreover, there are specific provisions of law namely, Order 41, rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, regarding the remand. Rule 23 empowers the appellate court to send back the case on remand, if suit were disposed of on preliminary point. But, this was not the case here. Hence, Rule 23 of Order 41 was not applicable in this case. On The contrary, Rule 24 of Order 41, requires the appellate court to pronounce judgment, where the document is available to pronounce the judgment and the Rule applied in the instant case, but the appellate court, instead of following the specific provisions laid down in Rule 24 of Order 41, had resorted to shortcut exist by through section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, which in fact and substance, amounts to dereliction of judicial duty by the appellate court and, in view of the specific provisions laid down under Order 41, to deal with the appeal preferred, the act of resorting to section 151 by the appellate court, was not permissible in this case.

21. I have considered the evidence on record, oral and documentary, adduced by the plaintiffs and find that, the evidence on record were sufficient for the appellate court to pronounce the judgment as regards the legality and illegality or infirmity (if any) in the judgment and order of the trial court, passed ex-parte, on 7-4-2008 and if the appellate Court had found that it would take additional evidence or should frame further issues as authorized by Rule 25 of Order 41, then it could have trained some additional issues, if necessary, for the purpose of pronouncement of judgment as well as it could have taken additional evidence as per clause (b) of sub-Rule (1) of Rule 27 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, because, the clause (a) of sub-Rule (1) of Rule 27 was not available to the appellants since there was no case of refusal to admit evidence proposed to be placed by the defendant before the trial court.

22. On the other hand, I have also looked into the judgment relied upon by the learned AAG the learned Advocate for the Union Parishad (the opposite party Nos. 1-4), that has been reported in 40 DLR (AD) 101, wherein the Appellate Division has sent the case on remand in a partition suit on the ground that the parties affected i.e. the heirs of the deceased-plaintiff were widow and minors and they lacked proper legal advices. But, the facts and circumstances of the instant case is totally different in the case of 40 DLR (AD) 101, hence, liable to be distinguished.

23. Besides, the judgment reported in 68 DLR 399, although have some factual similarity that the plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and the defendant examined none in the case reported in 68 DLR 399, however, that case is regarding permanent injunction and the issues in that case and the present one are totally different. Hence, this case is also liable to be distinguished.

24. I have given emphasis to the submission of the learned Advocates for the opposite party that, the plaintiffs ought to have given reference to RS and BS plot number in their plaint, but I find that, the plaintiffs have submitted the certified copy of the CS, SA and RS khatinas, respectively marked as Exhibit 1, 5 and 6 series. The defendant did not appear even to cross-examine the plaintiff's witnesses on the oral evidence or documentary evidences to prove that the boundary or description of the suit property was not correct or that any property of the Union Parishad were lying within the suit property described in the schedule to the plaint. Therefore, this objection is not sustainable in view of the fact and these khatians were available to ascertain if the suit property, at all included any property of the Union Parishad and as to whether any saham was claimed in respect of any property owed by the Union Parishad. Even, the defendant did not put any written objection, inspite of taking 17 adjournments against the warrant of delivery of possession. As such, the executing court has rightly disposed of the execution case by order No. 49 dated 15-10-2015, as has been annexed to the revisional application.

25. In view of the above, I find that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree by the appellate court, it has committed error of law, resulting in error in the decision impugned, and that has occasioned failure of justice in as much as, it has remanded the case to the trial court in clear violation of the specific provisions of Rule 24, 25 and clause (b) of Sub-Rule (1) of Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, as well as the law declared in 1 MLR (AD) 430 = 49 DLR (AD) 77.

26. Before parting of, I must record that the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008 of the trial court also shows a shocking evasion of judicial duty to write out a full judgment with specific reference made to the oral and documentary evidence available in the record. This lack of sense of judicial duty should be reflected in the ACR. Both the courts below have failed in following the norms and practices to be followed in writing judgment, which is really a deviation from judicial duty and is alarming as well.

27. I find merit in this Rule and this Rule shall be disposed of with appropriate direction upon the appellate court.

28. In the result, the Rule is disposed of with the following directions.

Order
The impugned judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015, passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No. 56 of 2015, is hereby set-aside.

The appellate court is directed to hear the appeal afresh as per provisions of Rule 24 of Order 41 and to frame the relevant issues as well as to take relevant evidence, if so required, for final adjudication of the matter in dispute, as per provisions of Rule 25 and clause (b) of Sub-Rule (1) of Rule 27 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The defendant-appellant-petitioner No. 1 shall pay Taka 2,50,000 (two lac fifty thousand) to the plaintiffs-petitioners within 60 (sixty) working days from the date of receiving this judgment and order by the appellate court, failing which, this Rule shall stand absolute and the judgment and decree of the trial court shall stand affirmed, and order of remand of this Court shall become inoperative, in consequence.

The appellate court, subject to the order given above, is also directed to dispose of the appeal within the soonest possible time considering the financial hardship and mental agony conferred upon the plaintiffs-petitioners by the defendant-appellant-opposite party No. 1, who is prosecuting the case at the cost of the public.

The parties are hereby directed to maintain status-quo in respect of possession and position of the suit property till disposal of the appeal, if that is to be heard, subject to order given above.

The Rule is disposed of accordingly.

Let a copy of this judgment along with LCR be sent to the concerned Courts at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment dated 14-3-2013 passed by the learned District Judge, Chattogram, in Partition Appeal No. 57 of 2013 dismissing the same summarily as time barred arising out of judgment dated 30-1-2012 and decree dated 6-2-2012 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram in Other Suit No. 58 of 1999 decreeing the suit ex-parte in preliminary form should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, fact of the case lies in a very short compus. The opposite party No. 1, as plaintiff, filed Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram, against the present petitioner, along with others as defendants, for a decree of partition. 

3. The.petitioners as defendant Nos. 2 and 3 filed written statement in the suit. Thereafter, in usual course, the suit was fixed on 30-1-2002 for peremptory hearing. On the date fixed the plaintiff filed hajira, but the defendants did not file hazira even took any step on their behalf. When the matter was taken up for hearing, the defendants and their learned Advocate were found absent on repeated calls. Consequently, the trial court took the matter for ex-parte hearing, recorded evidence of the plaintiff as PW 1 and decreed the suit. Thereafter, the defendants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("Code") on 29-2-2012 and the same was dismissed for default on 28-11-2012. The petitioners filed an application under section 151 of the Code on the same date praying for restoration of the miscellaneous case, the court allowed the same and restored the case. Thereafter, miscellaneous case was rejected on merit by judgment and order dated 23-1-2013. After rejection of the miscellaneous case, the defendants preferred Partition Appeal No. 57 of 2013 before the District Judge, Chattogram on 13-3-2013 against the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 30-1-2012 passed in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 at a delay of 371 days with an application for condonation of such delay. The appellate court heard the matter and upon hearing disallowed the appeal by its impugned judgment dated 14-3-2013 being barred by limitation. 

4. At this juncture, the petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

5. Mr Md Anowarul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioners, submits that the petitioners in their application for condonation of delay clearly stated that the appellants being wrong advised by their learned Advocate filed miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the decree instead of filing appeal against the ex-parte decree passed by the trial court and in pursuing the said miscellaneous case, there has been a delay of 371 days in filing the appeal. As such, the appellate court ought to have considered the application for delay, but it did not do so. He further submits that before passing an ex-parte decree, the court is required to go through the records, evidence of the plaintiff and to discuss the evidences atleast at the minimum, but in the instant case the trial court in passing ex-parte decree did not even discussed a single evidence both oral and documentary. As such, the ex-parte judgment and decree passed by the trial court cannot stand good. The appellate court utterly failed to consider the grounds taken in the appeal memo, as such, committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Alfu Miah and others vs Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 1993 (1) BLT (AD) page 25 = 45 DLR (AD) 112. 

6. Mr M Belayet Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the petitioners, as defendant in suit, failed to appear before the court on the date fixed for hearing. Consequently, the suit was decreed ex-parte and thereafter, the defendants rightly filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. 

7. The said miscellaneous case also dismissed for default on 28-11-2012 and again restored on the prayer of the petitioners and finally on merit the case was rejected by the trial court on 23-1-2013. He further submits that the petitioners have had opportunity to prefer appeal against the judgment and order dated 23-1-2013 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012, but the petitioners instead of preferring appeal against the judgment and order passed in the miscellaneous case, preferred appeal against ex-parte decree dated 30-1-2012 before the learned District Judge at a delay of 371 days. As such, the appellate court rightly rejected the application for condonation of delay and dismissed the appeal being barred by limitation holding that from the very date of passing ex-parte decree, the appellants were fully aware about the judgment passed by the trial court. 

8. He further submits that once a defendant filed miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code praying for setting aside an ex-parte decree and the same is disposed of with an order of rejection. The petitioner is to prefer appeal against such order and they cannot prefer appeal against the ex-parte decree passed by the trial court by passing and or giving a go bye to the proceeding under Order IX, rule 13 and the order thereof, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catena of cases Badvel Chinna Asethu and others vs Vettipalli Kesavayya and another reported in AIR 1920 Madras 962, Harishbhai Chunilal Shah vs Nalinkumar Champaklal Shah and others reported in AIR 1995 Gujarat 197 and M/s Mangilal Rungta, Calcutta vs Manganese Ore (India) Ltd. reported in AIR 1987 Bombay 87. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, have gone through the revisional application, evidences both oral and documentary available in the lower court records and the judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

10. Opposite party No. 1 instituted Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 on 28-7-1999 in the court of Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram for a decree of partition of only 21,2 sataks property mentioned in schedule "1(1(a)" to the plaint. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were contesting the suit by filing written statement. Among other dates the suit was fixed for hearing on 30-1-2012. On the date fixed the defendants did not file hazira even took any step on their behalf. The trial court took up the matter in the absence of the defendants and heard the same ex-parte and passed the judgment and decree in preliminary form. Thereafter, present petitioner filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code on 29-2-2012 for setting aside the decree, which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012. The said miscellaneous case was contested by the opposite party No. 1 and after hearing, the trial court by its judgment and order dated 23-1-2013 rejected the same holding that there are no sufficient cause for not appearing before the court on the date of hearing of the suit. And also held that the defendants were trying to delay the disposal of the suit by filing several applications for adjournment. Thereafter, the defendant-petitioner did not move before any higher court against the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 and without taking any appeal against the judgment and order passed in miscellaneous case, the defendants preferred an appeal being No. 57 of 2013 against the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 30-1-2012 passed in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 before the District Judge at a delay of 371 days. Learned District Judge took up the matter for hearing and upon hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-3-2013 dismissed the appeal being barred by limitation hence, the present revision. 

11. Now the question before this Court, whether a defendant after taking recourse to Order IX, rule 13 of the Code by filing an application praying for setting aside an ex-parte decree can again agitate the ex-parte decree by filing a regular appeal before the appellate court. The Law of Civil Procedure, by Mahmudul Islam, volume 1, 2009 at page 376 and the case Harishbhai Chunilal Shah vs Nalinkumar Champaklal Shah and others reported in AIR 1995 Gujarat 197 clearly held that; 
"Where an application under Order IX, rule 13 has been dismissed and no appeal has been taken against the decision, no grievance about proceeding ex-parte can be put forward in an appeal against the ex-parte decree. Where after the disposal of the application under Order IX, rule 13 and appeal against the decree was filed with an application for condonation of delay caused in proceeding with the application for restoration, the court refused to treat the cause as sufficient for condonation." 

12. It is quite obvious that the defendants sought to have an ex-parte decree set-aside, by filing an application specifically contemplated and permissible under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. This application was, therefore, statutory remedy available to the defendants. In pursuing this remedy it cannot be suggested that the other remedy available to the party, like appeal before the appellate court was suspended or that the same could be exercised at some later point on time in case the proceeding under Order IX, rule 13 failed, there is absolutely, no such proposition in law. 

13. The defendants had two options to seek relief against the ex-parte decree; one is, by filing an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code and other is an appeal under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the appellate court. In the instant case, the defendants rightly availed of the proceeding for getting the ex-parte decree set-aside by filing an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. The said case when dismissed by the court below, only option remained open for the applicants to agitate the matter before the appellate court by filing an appeal against the judgment and order passed by the trial court rejecting the application filed by the defendants praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. But the petitioners did not file any appeal against the rejection order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012, under section 104 read with Order 43 rule 1(b) of the Code, but filed an appeal against the ex-parte decree passed in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 at a delay of 371 days. The appellate court rightly rejected the appeal on the ground of limitation. In the application for condonation of delay, the petitioners stated that the delay was caused because of pursuing the statutory remedy by filing a miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the code. It is in this Court's view that such contention of the petitioners do not constitute sufficient cause for condonation of delay. 

14. Apart from this, the negligence or ignorance of the learned Advocate before the trial court is not relevant in the present proceeding, as this Court finds that the learned Advocate before the trial court rightly took resort to statutory remedy under Oder IX, rule 13 of the of the code, praying for setting aside the decree. 

15. In view of the above, the findings recorded by the appellate court to the effect that no sufficient cause has been made out by the appellants in their application for condonation of delay in preferring the appeal cannot be interfered with. 

16. Consequently, this Court finds no merit in the Rule. However, the petitioners may agitate the judgment and order dated 30-1-2013 passed by the trial court in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 before the appellate court seeking condonation of delay on the ground of consuming time in pursuing the appeal against the ex-parte decree, if so advised and not otherwise barred by any law. 

17. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. 

18. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned at once. 

End.
