full_judgment:
In the instant civil revision, Rule was issued on 14-5-2017 calling upon the plaintiff-appellant-opposite-party Nos. 1-16 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 24-1-2017 (decree signed on 30-1-2017) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Cumilla (previously spelled as Comilla) in Title Appeal No. 84 of 2014 allowing the appeal upon modification of the judgment and decree dated 27-2-2014 (decree signed on 5-3-2014) passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Homna, Cumilla in Title Suit No. 606 of 2008 decreeing the suit. 

2. The plaintiff-opposite parties filed the suit for partition claiming: 
(a) 8 annas share as to 'Ka' schedule property of CS khatian No.70 comprising 23 decimals of land, 
(b) 202.50 decimals of land as to Kha schedule property of CS khatian No.280 (94 decimals of land in Plot Nos. 3443, 3450 and 3480 as exclusive possessor and 108.50 decimals of land in rest of the plots in 8 annas share, total (94 + 108.50) = 202.50 decimals of land), 
(c) 16 annas share as to `Gha' schedule property of CS khatian No.678 comprising 94 decimals of land, and 
(d) 8 annas share as to `Gha' schedule property of CS khatian No.813 comprising 78 decimals of land. 
Total = 397.50 decimals of land. 

3. The properties situate at mouza Sreepatirchar, Police Station-Homna, District-Cumilla. The basis of the abovementioned claim of the plaintiffs, as stated in the plaint, is that CS khatian No. 70 was recorded in the names of the plaintiffs' predecessor Uzir and the defendants' predecessor Wahed Ali in equal shares. Plot Nos. 3443, 3450 and 3480 of CS khatian No. 280 were recorded in the name of Uzir Ali as exclusive possessor and the rest of the plots were recorded in the names of Uzir Ali and Wahed All in equal shares. CS khatian No.678 was recorded exclusively in the name of plaintiffs' predecessor Uzir Ali. CS khatian No. 813 was recorded in the names of Uzir Ali and Wahed Ali in equal shares. Uzir Ali died leaving behind the plaintiff No. 1 Montaz Uddin alias Momtaz Uddin as only son and two daughters namely, Sabaner Nessa (plaintiff No. 2) and Moina Bibi. While the son and two daughters of Uzir Ali had been possessing the scheduled property as owner through succession, Moina Bibi died leaving behind Toyfol Nessa (plaintiff No.3) as only successor. The plaintiffs have been possessing the land in ejmali by erecting houses and growing crops. The schedule mentioned properties were not partitioned which have resulted in misunderstanding and quarrel between the parties. On 19-4-2008, the defendants refused to partition the property amicably and hence, the suit for partition. 

4. The defendant Nos. 1 to 7 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the case of the plaintiffs. The defendants' case is that the schedule mentioned properties were owned and possessed by one Ramiz Uddin. He died leaving behind two sons namely, Kalagazi and Yeakub Ali as successors. They owned and possessed the properties in equal shares. Kalagazi died leaving behind Uzir Ali and Yeakub All died leaving behind minor son Wahed Ali as successors. The defendants are the successor-in-interest of Wahed Ali. 

5. In respect of CS khatian No.70 (Ka Schedule) and CS khatian No.813 (Gha schedule), the defendants do not dispute the plaintiffs' case that these-khatians were recorded in the names of Uzir All (plaintiffs' predecessor) and Wahed All (defendants' predecessor) in equal shares.

6. In respect of CS khatian No. 280 (Kha schedule), the defendants claim that the said khatian was prepared in the names of Uzir Ali and Wahed Ali in equal shares. Subsequently, Uzir Ali sold and handed over possession of 17 decimals of land in plot No. 3443 and 14 decimals of land in plot No. 3450, both of CS khatian No 280, total 31 decimals of land to Wahed Ali, but no registered sale deed was executed. On 21-11-1944, Wahed Ali transferred the said 31 decimals of land to his wife-Arabia Khatun through a registered deed of hiba-bil-ewaj. 

7. In respect of CS khatian No. 678 (Ga schedule), the defendants' case is that although 94 decimals of land of the said khatian were owned and possessed by Uzir Ali and Wahed Ali in equal shares, but during the CS operation the same was wrongly recorded in the name of Uzir Ali. During the SA operation, the land was correctly recorded in the corresponding SA khatian No. 815 in the names of plaintiff No. 1, who is the son of Uzir Ali and these defendants as successors of Wahed Ali in equal shares. 

8. Wahed Ali died leaving behind the defendant Nos. 1-7 (five-sons and two daughters) and his wife Ambia Khatun as successors. Ambia Khatun died leaving behind these defendants. The defendants own and possess 3.341/2 acres of land. The plaintiffs are not entitled to get saham as prayed for. 

9. During the trial, the plaintiffs examined one witness and produced documentary evidences which were marked as Exhibits 1, 2-2(3). The defendants examined 3 witnesses and produced documentary evidences which were marked as Exhibits-Ka, Kha series and Ga. 

10. The trial Court held that out of 397.50 decimals of land of the four khatians as claimed by the plaintiffs, they are entitled to saham of 303.50 decimals of land in the following manner: 
from CS khatian No. 70 in 8 annas share = 23 decimals 
from CS khatian No. 813 in 8 annas share = 78 decimals 
from CS khatian No. 280 in 8 annas share = 155.50 decimals 
from CS khatian No. 678 in 8 annas share = 0.47 decimals 
Total = 303.50 decimals 
Accordingly, the trial Court passed the judgment and decree on 27-2-2014. 

11. The plaintiffs preferred an appeal which was allowed in part. The appellate Court below modified the decree passed by the trial Court by enhancing the saham of the plaintiffs from 303.50 decimals of land to 350.50 decimals of land. In so doing, the appellate Court allotted the entire land of CS khatian No. 678 (94 decimals) to the plaintiffs while maintaining equal shares in respect of the rest three khatians to the plaintiffs and the defendants respectively as allotted by the trial Court. 

12. Challenging the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below, the defendants preferred the instant civil revision and obtained the Rule. 

13. Mr Md Mostafa, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent-petitioners, submits that he has no objection as to allocation of saham to the parties in respect of CS khatian Nos. 70, 813 and 280 by the appellate Court below. The learned Advocate, however, submits that the appellate Court below committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice by allotting the entire share of CS khatian No. 678 to the plaintiffs inasmuch as in the corresponding SA khatian No. 815 the names of the plaintiff No. 1 and these defendants were recorded in equal Shares which cast cloud upon the title of the plaintiffs so far as entire share of CS khatian No. 678 is concerned and therefore, until and unless the plaintiffs' title in the entire share of CS khatian No. 678 is declared by a competent Court or the corresponding SA khatian is not declared wrong by a Civil Court, the suit for partition simpliciter is not maintainable. In support of the argument, the learned Advocate refers to the case of Rezaul Karim and others vs Shamsuzzoha and others, 49 DLR (AD) 68. 

14. Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellant-opposite party Nos.1-16, on the other hand, submits that it now settled principle of law through judicial pronouncement that in a suit for partition, the Court can determine each conflicting claims incidental to partition. In support of the argument, the learned Advocate refers to the cases of Shashi Kumar vs Nagendra Nath, 1982 BLD 36 and Cinmoy Chowdhury and another vs Mridul Chowdhury and others, 55 DLR (AD) 115. The learned Advocate next submits that order VII, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers the Court to give relief to the plaintiff as he is found entitled to but omits to pray. The learned Advocate refers to the case of Dhaka City Corporation and others vs Shamsur Rahman and others, 59 DLR 207 in support of the argument. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate Court below rightly allotted the entire share of the land of the CS khatian No. 678 to the plaintiffs as the same was recorded in 16 annas share in the name of the plaintiffs' predecessor and that there is no basis of recording 8 annas share of the same in the defendants' name in the corresponding SA khatian. In this regard the learned Advocate submits that the presumption of correctness as to CS khatian is not available with regard to the SA khatian. In support of the argument, the learned Advocate refers to the cases of Akrab Ali and others vs Zahiruddin Kuri and others, 30 DLR (SC) 81, Hindu Devi Lakshmi Gobinda Jew vs Deputy Custodian Enemy Property (now vested property) Government of Bangladesh and others, 7 BLT 133 = 51 DLR 300, Hriday Ranjan Dey and another vs Niranjan Dey being dead his heirs, Probate Dey and others, 10 
BLT (AD) 137 = 54 DLR (AD) 16. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial Court has misread the evidences. 

15. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the materials on record. 

16. In the instant suit for partition, the plaintiffs prayed for saham of land in respect of four CS khatians. Both the trial Court and the appellate Court below allotted 8 annas shares of land of three khatians to the plaintiffs. The bone of contention arises in respect of CS khatian No. 678. Plaintiffs claimed 16 annas share of land of CS khatian No.678, but the trial Court gave 8 annas share to them which, on appeal filed by the plaintiffs, was modified and the appellate Court gave 16 annas share of land of CS khatian No. 678 to the plaintiffs. Now, the defendants are the petitioners before me. 

17. Admittedly, 16 annas share of CS khatian No. 678 was prepared in the name of the plaintiffs predecessor Uzir Ali. Defendants claim that the land of CS khatian No.678 was owned and possessed in equal shares by the respective predecessors of the plaintiffs and the defendants. So, the CS khatian No. 678 was wrong which was corrected in the corresponding SA khatian No. 815 which was recorded in equal shares in the names of the plaintiffs and the defendants. 

18. The trial Court observed the plaintiffs failed to prove that neither their predecessor nor the plaintiffs are the owner, and possessor of the entire land of CS khatian No. 678. The trial Court further observed that in the corresponding SA and BS khatians, the land has been recorded in equal shares in the names of the plaintiffs and defendants which prove that the defendants own and possess 8 annas share of land of CS khatian No. 678 as successors of their predecessor. However, the trial Court did not elaborate its findings with reference to any oral or documentary evidence. The appellate Court below reversed the finding of the trial Court holding,

“এই সম্পত্তিতে (referring to CS khatian No. 678) বিবাদীর মালিকানা অজর্নের কোন প্রমাণ বিবাদী উপস্থাপন করেনি । এস, এ, খতিয়ান কোন ভাবেই মালিকানার প্রমাণ বহন করেনা । ... স্বীকৃত মতে বি, এস, খতিয়ান এখনও চূড়ান্ত হয়নি। ...সুতরাং সাক্ষ্য বিশ্লেষণে এটাই প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, ৮১৫ নং এস, এ, খতিয়ানে ভুল রেকর্ডের সুযোগে ওয়াহেদ আলীর ওয়ারিশগণ (বিবাদী-রেসপনডেন্ট) ৬৭৮ নং সি, এস, খতিয়ানের মালিক উজির আলীর সম্পত্তিতে ভিত্তিহীন হিস্যা দাবী করছেন। এই ৬৭৮ নং সি, এস, খতিয়ানে বিবাদীর কোনরূপ মালিকানা নেই। অর্থাৎ সি, এস, ৬৭৮ খতিয়ানের সম্পূর্ণ ৯৮ শতক সম্পত্তিতে ওয়ারিশসূত্রে উজির আলীর ওয়ারিশগণ (বাদী-আ্পীলকারী) একক মালিক মর্মে প্রমাণিত হয়। বিজ্ঞ নি্ন আদালত কোন ধরনের প্রমাণ ব্যতিরেকে এই খতিয়ানের অর্ধেক যা ৪৭ শতক ভূমিতে বিবাদী রেসপনডেন্ট এর মালিকানা আছে মর্মে যে সিদ্ধান্ত দিয়েছেন তা সঠিক হয়নি ।” 

19. The learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners could not show that the findings of the appellate Court are perverse or that appellate Court misread the evidence or that it failed to consider the evidence, which if considered, the findings would have been otherwise. In Halima Begum and others vs Syed Ahmed and others, 21 DLR 854, it was argued that SA khatian having recorded the disputed land in the name of the pre-emptor it should be presumed that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in respect of the said disputed land. It was held, 
"It is true that record of right indicates certain right of certain parties but that right is certainly dependent on some material evidence, oral and documentary so as to establish title in favour of persons who claim under the said record of right. The presumption of correctness as to CS record of right is not certainly available with regard to the State Acquisition Khatians. There is no presumption of correctness in respect of the State Acquisition Khatians as it is to be found in case of CS Khatians in pursuance of the provision under section 103-B of the Bengal Tenancy Act." 

20. In Hriday Ranjan Dey vs Niranjan Dey 10 BLT (AD) 137 = 54 DLR (AD) 16, which has referred to by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties, it has been held, 
"The presumption of the CS Khatian under section 103(B) of the Bengal Tenancy Act is that every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to he incorrect. Reference may be made in this regard to the case of Akrab Ali and others vs Zahiruddin Kari and others, 30 DLR (SC) 81." 

21. Reverting back to the case in hand, the defendants could not show as to how their predecessor became owner of 8 annas share in the land of CS khatian No. 678. The entire land was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs' predecessor alone. Therefore, I am of the view that the appellate Court below rightly held that the plaintiffs are the owners of 16 annas share in the land of CS khatian No. 678 as successors of the CS recorded owner Uzir Ali. 

22. I have already noted that the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners has. argued that the instant suit for partition is not maintainable due to the fact the SA khatian No. 815, which is corresponding to CS khatian No. 678, has been recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and the defendants in equal shares as owners. Thus, a determination of the respective title of parties is required which cannot be adjudicated in the suit for partition simpliciter. The learned Advocate has relied upon the case of Rezaul Karim and others vs Shamsuzzoha and others, 49 DLR (AD) 68. In the reported case, it has been held as under: 
"In a suit for partition the court will no doubt consider the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land in some details more. than in a suit for permanent injunction, but it cannot in either case convert itself into a court for determination of the respective titles of the parties if a serious dispute emerges from the pleadings as to the title of the plaintiffs to the partible property and if it is not possible to effect partition without formally determining the plaintiffs' title to the property claimed in the partition suit." 

23. In the reported-case, the apex Court further observed that, 
"Both the courts below concurrently held; without being reversed by the High Court Division, that the plaintiffs failed to prove settlement of the suit land with their mother Asia Khatun. If the plaintiffs are desirous of getting their full share as claimed in the present suit they must take the responsibility of proving their claim in a full-fledged suit for declaration of title." 

24. In the instant case, the plaintiffs have proved their title in the partible property. Therefore, the case of Rezaul Karim is of no assistance to the defendants. In Shashi Kumar vs Nagendra Nath, 1982 BLD 36, it has been held as under: 
"In a suit for partition it is incumbent upon the court not only to determine whether-the property was joint property and liable to partition but also incumbent upon the court, where there are conflicting claims to shares, under the same right under which the partition was sought, to determine each conflicting claim which are incidental to the partition and necessary for deciding the issues. In this regard the court has ample authority to determine issues of title independent of the partition, that are necessary for the purpose of allocating the respective shares. A suit for partition may involve disputed question of title and any attempt to avoid deciding such issues would only lead to needless multiplicity of suits". 

25. In Md Sultan Mia and others vs Hazera Bibi and others, 1984 BLD (AD) 23, it has been held that a question of title can incidentally be gone into a partition suit. The cases of Rezaul Karim and Md Sultan Mia were discussed in Cinmoy Chowdhury and another vs Mridul Chowdhury and others, 55 DLR (AD) 115 wherein it has been held that in a suit for partition all the incidental questions of title, however, complicated it may be, can be decided and finally disposed of. The parties should not be thrown away or driven out on the ground of maintainability of the suit and, as such, the argument as to non-maintain-ability of the suit perishes without any footing. In Cinmoy Chowdhury, it was further held, 
"Onus of proof in a civil litigation generally lies upon the plaintiff but sometimes it is splitted up between the parties and sometimes it is shifted upon the defendants as well, according to the respective cases of the parties, as they plead, in view of the concept and the meaning of the provision of sections 102, 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act." 

26. In the instant case, the plaintiffs proved their title in respect of 16 annas share in the land recorded in CS khatian No. 678. The appellate Court below categorically found that the defendants failed to prove their title in respect of 8 annas share in CS khatian No. 678. Therefore, the instant partition suit is maintainable inasmuch as no dispute emerges as to the title of the plaintiffs to the partible property and that the title of the parties can formally be determined to effect partition. 

27. The trial Court found that earlier the plaintiffs filed objection case under section 30 of the Bengal Tenancy Act in respect of plot Nos. 2934 and 3042 of CS khatian No. 678 which was rejected. This finding is a total misreading of documentary evidence. Records show that the said objection case was filed in respect of plot Nos. 3443 and 3450 of CS khatian No. 280. Therefore, this finding, which is wrong on the face of the records, does not assist the defendants. 

28. No other point urged. All the points having found in favour of the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below. I find no substance in the Rule. 

29. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay is vacated. The judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below are affirmed. No order as to costs. 

Send down the LCR at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 10-10-2018 passed by learned District Judge, Madaripur in Civil Revision No.14 of 2017 affirming judgment and order dated 5-7-2017 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur in Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 2014 having arises out of order dated 12-6-2017 passed by the same Court in Title Suit No. 124 of 2006 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

2. The petitioners herein as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 124 of 2006 impleading the opposite parties as defendants before the Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur for declaration of title by adverse possession and confirmation of possession. 

3. The suit was posted for peremptory hearing and on 12-6-2014 the petitioners sought adjournment which was rejected and the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit as plaintiffs failed to pay the cost ordered by the Court on 4-3-2014. The petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 2014 wherein defendant Nos.1-6 filed petition for recording abatement and consequently the case is abated vide order dated 5-7-2017 as the property is enlisted in 'Ka' schedule under Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001. 

4. The revisional Court in Civil Revision No.24 of 2017 affirmed the judgment and order passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2014 abating the case. 

5. Opposite party Nos.1, 3, 4 and 6 filed counter affidavit denying the assertion of the petitioners and averred that earlier by filing Title Suit No. 470 of 1980 the predecessor of plaintiffs opposite parties sought declaration of title impleading the predecessor of the present petitioner as defendant No.7 and inspite of service of summons upon the latter he did not contest the suit and the trial Court rightly decreed the suit in favour of the predecessor of the opposite parties and, as such, present proceeding initiated by the petitioners regarding the self same matter is barred by law and not sustainable. It is further stated that if the property is listed in 'Ka' schedule then any party is obligated to invoke the jurisdiction of the Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon tribunal but instead, the present petitioners filed title suit with vexatious claim and since provision is there in the special law, without invoking the provision of special law initiating any legal proceeding under general law is not sustainable. It is further averred in the counter affidavit that as the property has been enlisted in the 'Ica' list, the opposite parties initiated proceeding before the vested property tribunal for releasing the property from the vested property list and the tribunal after hearing released the property and the appellate tribunal also affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the tribunal and, as such, the present petitioners has no grievance in the instant forum, consequently as such the Rule is liable to discharge. 

6. Mr Probir Halder, learned Advocate assisted by Advocate Ms. Joya Bhattacharjee submits that the suit property is not vested property as the opposite party Nos.1-6 earlier got decree on 9-4-1981 in Title Suit No.470 of 1980 for declaration of title as well as other reliefs and Government's Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 1982 having filed for setting aside the ex-partee decree has also been dismissed-on 13-7-1985 and consequently said property has been released from vested property and opposite parties' name has been mutated and, as such, provision of section 13(1)(ka) will not be applicable in the instant case but both the Courts below failed to advert that legal provision and thereby arrived at a wrong conclusion. Mr Halder next submits that applicability of section 13 of the Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 depends upon sections 6 of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 which stipulates that no property can be enlisted as vested property regarding which competent Court passed judgment and decree and, as such, order of abatement having recorded in respect of the miscellaneous case is not sustainable in law. He further submits that if any property is declared as not vested property or if title is declared by any competent Court in that case, prottorpon of the suit land in favour of the owner is not proper prayer rather release of property from the list can be sought under section 10(4) of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001. Learned advocate further submits that in section 2 (neo) of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 the list of property to be included in the restoration list has been mentioned and, as such, the case property having not vested property, the provision of section 13 for passing order of abatement is not sustainable. He argued that the petitioners filed Title Suit No.124 of 2006 impleading the present opposite parties as defendants praying for declaration of title by adverse possession and confirmation of possession and, as such, there is no impediment to proceed with the suit as filed by the plaintiffs-petitioners but both the Courts below failed to appreciate that vital aspect of the case and erroneously passed order of abatement in Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 2014. 

7. Mr Syed Aktarul Islam, learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No.2 submits that the petitioners' father was defendant No.7 in Title Suit No.470 of 1980 having filed by the predecessor of the present opposite parties seeking declaration of title and further declaration that the suit property is not vested and non-resident property and granting settlement of the said property is illegal and as petitioners' father has no claim in the suit land he refrained from contesting the suit by filing written statement and, as such, the suit has been decreed in favour of the opposite parties and now they have filed vexatious suit with a view to cause loss to the opposite parties. He further submits that the present petitioners without invoking the provision of special law filed suit under general provisions of law and, as such, the said suit is not maintainable as there exists special law having special provision for restoration or releasing the suit property if any lawful claim is there and, as such, the present suit filed by the petitioners is not sustainable and order passed by the Courts below cannot be interfered with. He further submits that restoration and release are interchangeable terms, although the opposite parties initiated proceeding for releasing property which also will be deemed as restoration of property alternatively in favour of the opposite parties and, as such, the said terms also broadly come within the purview of section 13 of the vested property restoration Ain, 2001. Learned advocate further submits that the petitioners sought declaration of title but in earlier suit the predecessor of the present petitioners was defendant No.7 wherein same matter has been considered by the Court which declared title in favour of the predecessor of the opposite parties and, as such, the present vexatious suit filed by the petitioners is not maintainable. Learned advocate further submits that the present proceeding is barred by the principle of approbation and reprobation as the present petitioners relying upon the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.470 of 1980 to that effect that the suit property is not vested and non resident property but they are denying the title of the opposite parties which has been passed in the same suit and, as such, the present proceeding is also not maintainable by the principle of approbation and reprobation. Learned advocate further submits that the present suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, although the suit has been abated by the Courts below, but alternatively the suit is also not maintainable by the principle of resjudicata and, as such, it is futile exercise to proceed with the suit and miscellaneous proceeding and it should be buried at its inception. 

8. Learned advocate in support of his contention referred the case of Managing Director, Rupali Bank Ltd. and others vs Tafazal Hossain and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260, Abdul Jalil and others vs Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd. and other reported in 53 DLR (AD) 12, Parveen Banu @ Purnima and others vs Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, represented by its Chairman and others 42 DLR (AD) 234, Commissioner of Customs, Chittagong vs Giasuddin Chowdhuly and another 50 DLR (AD) 129, Osman Gani Mondal vs Mainuddin Ahmed and others reported in 27 DLR 61, Gopinath Das and others vs Government of Bangladesh and others 64 DLR 167, Burmah Easstern Employees Union and others 18 DLR 709, Nurul Hague (Md) and another vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Communications, railway Division and others 51 DLR (AD) 140, Jogesh Chandra Datta vs Government of Bangladesh and others 30 DLR 219 and the KK Modi vs KN Modi and others 3 Supreme Court Cases (1998) 573 in support of his contention. 

9. Having gone through the revisional application, annexures and other materials it appears that original suit being Civil Suit No. 124 of 2006 filed by the predecessor of the present petitioners before the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Madaripur was dismissed for default on 12-3-2014 which was for declaration of title and confirmation of possession impleading predecessor of present opposite parties as defendant. Thereafter the present petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2014 before the same Court for restoration of original suit under order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in the said case the present opposite parties by filing an application prayed for recording abatement of the case as the suit property in question has been enlisted in the 'Ica' schedule under section 13 of the Vested property Prottorpon Ain 2001 and upon hearing the application, learned Senior Assistant Judge by order dated 5-7-2017 recorded abatement contending that the property in question has been enlisted in 'Ica' list under section 13 of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 and the revisional Court also affirmed the judgment and order passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge. 

10. On perusal of section 13 of the Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 it appears that there is provision for recording abatement of any property if it is enlisted in the 'Ica' schedule. In section 2(13) it is mentioned that if the property is enlisted under section 13(1) then application is to be filed to the tribunal for restoration of the same and if any property comes under section 6 of the said Ain application is to be filed for releasing said property. Section 6 of the Ain stipulates that if any Court passes any decree or order to the effect that the property in question is not vested and non resident property then the said property cannot be included in the Prottarponjoggo Shampatty list. For better appreciation section 6 of the Arpito Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 is reproduced below: 

৬-_“(ক) কোন সম্পত্তি অর্পিত সম্পত্তি নহে মর্মে এই আইন প্রবর্তনের পূর্বে যথাথ আদালত চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করিয়া থাকিলে সেই সম্পত্তি;
(খ) এই আইন প্রবর্তনের পূর্বে ষে কোন সময় তত্ত্বাবধায়ক কর্তৃক অর্পিত সম্পত্তির তালিকা হইতে অবমুক্ত করা হইয়াছে এরূপ কোন সম্পত্তি;
(গ) সরকার কর্তৃক কোন সংবিধিদ্ধ সংস্থা বা অন্য কোন সংগঠন বা কোন ব্যক্তির নিকট স্থায়ীভাবে হস্তান্তরিত বা স্থায়ী ইজারা প্রদত্ত অর্পিত সম্পত্তি;

(ঘ) কোন সংবিধিবদ্ধ সংস্থার নিকট ন্যস্ত এমন অর্পিত সম্পত্তি যাহা শিল্প বা বাণিজ্যিক প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং উহার আওতাধীন সকল সম্পদ এবং এইরূপ সংবিধিবদ্ধ সংসস্থা কর্তৃক উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠান বা উহার আওতাধীন সম্পদ বা উহার কোন অংশবিশেষ হস্তাস্তর করিয়া থাকিলে সেই হস্তান্তর করিয়া থাকিলে সেই হস্তান্তরিত সম্পত্তি;
(ঙ) এমন অর্পিত সম্পত্তি যাহা কোন কোম্পানীর শেয়ার বা অন্য কোন প্রকারের সিকিউরিটি;
(চ) জনন্বার্থে অধিখ্বহণ করা হইয়াছে এইরূপ কোন অর্পিত সম্পত্তিঃ

11. Now the question arises whether the suit property is vested property or not. If the suit property is vested property in that case section 13(1) of the Ain will come into play and if any suit is pending, then it will be abated upon application by any party or automatically but if any property is declared to be not vested property, then it cannot be enlisted as Prottarponjoggo Shampatty under schedule 'Ka' under section 6 of the Ain. 

12. In the instant case it appears that earlier in Title Suit No. 470 of 1980 civil Court declared title in favour of the opposite parties and the civil Court also declared that leasing out the suit land treating the same as enemy property is illegal and subsequently miscellaneous case filed by the government being Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 1982 for setting aside the said ex-parte decree was also dismissed by the said Court and, as such, it is clearly apparent that the said property is not vested property and, as such, it cannot be enlisted in the Prottarponjoggo Shampatty list under section 13 of the Ain. Section 2 (neo) of the Ain 2001 also defined the list of Prottarponjoggo Shampatty wherein it is clearly mentioned that if any property is to be treated vested property it is to be under the custody of the government but admittedly the property in question is not under custody of the Bangladesh government having admitted by both the parties. Since it is found that the suit property is not vested property it cannot be enlisted under section 13(1) of the Prottarponjoggo Shampatty list and it is also clearly apparent from the proceeding initiated by the opposite parties that they initiated proceeding not for restoration of the property but releasing the property under section 13(2)(a) and section 6 of the said Act and they got order of release having affirmed by the appellate tribunal and, as such, it is conspicuously clear that learned Assistant Judge failed to advert that provisions of law and erroneously passed order for abating the case. Regarding the submission of the learned advocate for the opposite party that earlier in Title Suit No. 470 of 1980 title of the opposite party has been declared and, as such, the present petitioner cannot claim title again over the self same suit property and the said suit is not maintainable, but regard being had to facts of the case, the said submission is not applicable in the present case as because order has been passed regarding abatement citing a prevalent law. He can ventilate grievance for such assertion in separate forum under appropriate provisions of law. Regarding the submission of the learned advocate the present proceeding is barred by the principle of approbation and reprobation, but the said principle is also not applicable in the instant case as because the instant matter is whether the Courts below passed order as per law, abating the case. Learned advocate intended to show that the petitioners are trying to rely on portion of the judgment of earlier suit that the property is not vested property but the petitioners by denying title of the opposite parties have filed the title suit which they are not entitled but such question is also not the matter of consideration in the instant proceeding as because instant proceeding is to be considered under the perimeters of vested property and Restoration Ain 2001 and since under section 6 of the vested property restoration Ain bars enlisting any property in the vested property list the said principle is not also applicable here. The opposite parties have got ample opportunity to make such submission if the original suit is restored to its file and number. 

13. Consequently the decision referred by the learned Counsel for the opposite parties are not applicable in the instant case. 

14. In the forgoing discussion, it is clearly apparent that the suit property is not vested property and, as such, it has been enlisted in the `Ka' schedule illegally and consequently recording abatement under section 13(1) of the Vested Property Restoration Ain, 2001 is not sustainable. Learned Senior Assistant Judge without considering the legal provision passed order recording abatement having affirmed by the revisional Court which are not sustainable. 

15. In the above facts and circumstances, I find merit in the Rule and accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. 

16. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule having extended time to time is hereby re-called and vacated. 

17. Send down the Lower Court's Record. 

Communicate the order at once. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 15-12-2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1675 of 1994.)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 15-12-2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1675 of 1994 making the Rule absolute. 

2. The predecessor-in-interest of the appellants instituted other Suit No. 150 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Satkania against the respondents for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and also for perpetual injunction in respect of 1.3875 acres of land out of 1.85 acres, that is, to the extent of 12 annas shares as described in the schedule to the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the suit property is a tank and the banks surrounding to it which is popularly known as "Bureer Pukur". In Moghi Chitta Survey the scheduled property was recorded as Taraf Syed Mohammad Arshad Kishmat Malik Rahman. The said Taraf never possessed the same. Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah had been in possession of the same. During CS operation the suit land was recorded as Nayabad Mohal and the same was recorded in the names of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah. They possessed the suit property for more than 90 years. They also paid rents to the Government. The said tank was silted up gradually. Abdul Aziz and others settled .the same to Mofzulur Rahman, Abdul Gafur, Abdul Bari and All Hossain, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos.33-62. Mofzulur and others having been in possession of the said tank re-excavated the same spending huge amount. Of them, Ali Hossain was literate person and he acted as "Karjakark" of all family members. In RS operation, the tank was recorded in the names of Abdul Razzak and others, where it was mentioned that they were in permissive possession. After enforcement of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs became the raiyats under the Government. At present, the plaintiffs have been possessing the said tank. The predecessor of the defendant No.32 filed an application for drawing proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, accordingly, a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure bearing Miscellaneous Case No.8 of 1949 was started in respect of the suit property. In that Miscellaneous case, the Magistrate found the claim of the heirs of Ali Hossain, Golam Sultan and others sustainable and, accordingly, put them in possession of the suit property. The predecessors of the plaintiffs had been possessing the suit tank by rearing fish and planting trees on the bank of the tank within the knowledge of the defendants. The principal defendants have had no title and possession in the suit tank. They disclosed that the suit tank was taluki property of Azmatullah and Muzibullah and the same was purchased by Ezzad Ali and others in auction and, thereafter, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants took settlement of the suit tank from them. The principal defendants, who are rich men, have been making plan to enter into the suit tank forcibly. Thus, the plaintiffs constrained to file the suit. 

3. The defendant Nos. 1-4, the predecessors of the present respondent Nos. 1-19, contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit was not maintainable and the same was barred by principle of res-judicata. Their positive case, in short, was that the suit property was recorded in Moghi Chita Survey as Plot No.699 under Taraf Syed Md Arshad Azmatullah and Mujibullah were the tenants under the said Taraf. For arrear rent, the suit property was put in auction. Ijjat Ali, Mosharrof Ali and Anwar Ali auction purchased the same and got possession thereof. Those auction purchasers settled the same to Ali Mahmud on 25th Falgun, 1257 BS who possessed the suit tank by rearing and preserving fish therein and planting trees on the banks. Ali Mahmud died leaving behind two sons namely Abdul Ali and Nazir Ali. On 22-7-1280 BS, Nazir Ali transferred his share to Abdul Ali by registered kabala deed. In the said kabala deed Ali Hossain was an attesting witness Abdul Ali became sole owner of the suit tank and constructed house beside the bank of the tank. The land-lords collected rent from Abdul Ali and others. Meanwhile, the suit tank was recorded in the names of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah in the cadastral survey. Such record was wrong and baseless. The Government acquired no right or title in the suit land and it was never made khas land of the Government. The tank was never included in Nayabad Mahal. Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah never possessed the suit tank. Preparation of the RS Khatian following the CS record of right in the names of Abdul Aziz and others was equally wrong and never acted upon. The predecessors of the plaintiffs and proforma-defendant Nos.33-62 fabricated the so-called unregistered patta dated 10-5-1913. The predecessors of the plaintiffs claimed the suit land as their purchased land in Other Suit No. 17 of 1957 but failed to produce any deed and did not disclose about the existence of patta dated 10-5-1913. At the time of RS operation, Abdul Ali, predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4, went to Rangoon for earning money and he entrusted his brother-in-law Ali Hossain to get the tank recorded in his name but Ali Hossain managed to get the same recorded in the names of Syed Abdul Aziz and others with the remarks therewith as permissive possession of Ali Hossain. After returning from Rangoon, Abdul Ali died leaving behind two sons, defendant No.1 and Jobbar Ali, and two daughters. The defendant No. 1 and his brother Jobbar Ali and sister Amena Khatun instituted Other Suit No. 17 of 1957 and obtained a decree for declaration of their title in respect of the suit tank. The defendant Nos. 1-14 and 15 of the said suit filed two different appeals being Nos.498 of 1958 and 27 of 1959 in the Court of District Judge which were dismissed on contest and, there-after, Second Appeal No.505 of 1963 was preferred in the High Court Division which was also dismissed. The plaintiffs never had any title or possession in the suit tank and, as such, the suit filed by the plaintiffs was liable to be dismissed. 

4. The trial court held that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their title and possession in 12 annas share in the suit tank and also found that the suit was not barred by section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, since the plaintiffs or their predecessors were not impleaded in Title Suit No. 17 of 1957. The trial court, therefore, decreed the suit declaring title of the plaintiffs in 12 annas share in the suit tank, confirming their possession therein and also restraining the principal defendants from entering into the suit tank. Against that judgment and decree of the trial court, the contesting defendants preferred appeal. The appellate court also found that the plaintiffs had right, title and possession in 12 annas share in the suit tank. But it observed that the plaintiffs were not entitled to get decree of perpetual injunction against the defendants as they admitted the possession of some of the defendants in four annas share of the suit tank. The contesting defendants being aggrieved by that judgment and decree of the appellate court filed Civil Revision No. 1675 of 1994 in the High Court Division and obtained Rule.

5. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute. Thus, the plaintiffs have preferred this appeal getting leave. 

6. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of the appellants that on the basis of patta CS and RS records were duly prepared in the names of the predecessors of the appellants and they have been in continuous possession of the suit land for more than 90 years and that they produced the rent receipts, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. 

7. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Counsel, appearing for the appellants submits that the appellants and defendants Nos.33-62 have been possessing suit land more than 12 years peacefully, uninterruptedly and adversely thereby acquired valid title by virtue of adverse possession. Before that their predecessors-in-interest had been in possession of the disputed pond more than 90 years, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. 

8. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the contesting respondents, submits that the appellants are not in exclusive, peaceful and continuous possession in the suit property and that in their pleadings the appellants have failed to make out a case of adverse possession, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. 

9. In this case the plaintiffs prayed for declaration of their title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction to the extent of 12 annas share, that is, in respect of 1.38¾ acres of land out of 1.85 acres of RS Khatian No.386, Plot No.612 corresponding to CS Plot No.611 and 612 Mouza-Rasulia, Satkania. Their case was that the suit tank was recorded as Taraf Syed Mohammad Ashad Kishmat Malik Rahman and the said tank was in possession of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah who settled the same to Mofzulur Rahman, Abdul Gafur, Abdul Bari and Ali Hossain, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos.33-62. 

10. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that initially the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit land on the basis of settlement but, at the time of hearing the Rule in the High Court Division, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants, giving go by to their claim of title on the basis of settlement, asserted their title in the suit land by way of adverse possession only stating that the plaintiffs' predecessors-in-interest and, thereafter the plaintiffs had been and have been possessing the suit land for more than 90 years. It appears from the schedule to the plaint that the plaintiffs prayed for decree firstly on the basis of the settlement and, thereafter, on adverse possession in respect of 1.383/4 acres of land out of 1.85 acres. Admittedly, the nature of the land is pond. It is case of the plaintiffs that the proforma-defendant Nos.33-62 are the owners of ¼th of the total land. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that there was any metes and bound partition amongst the co-sharers of the disputed land. Since plaintiffs' case is that the defendant Nos.33-62 are the co-sharers of the scheduled tank and banks of the same and that there was no metes and bound partition amongst the co-sharers, it is difficult to accept the submission of Mr AJ Mohammad Ali that the plaintiffs have been exclusively, uninterruptedly and peacefully possessing the suit tank. To establish the plea of adverse possession against a co-owners unambiguous evidence of complete ouster to their knowledge must be established. It is rebuttable presumption that the co-sharers in exclusive possession is holding possession on behalf of the other co-sharers. Possession of one co-owner is in law possession of all the co-sharers. Nothing sought of ouster or something equivalent to ouster will put an end to that possession. In order to establish adverse possession on the part of one of the co-sharer as against another it is not sufficient to show that one of them is in sole possession and enjoyment of the profit of the property. Ouster of the non-possessing co-sharers by co-sharing possession, who claimed his possession to be adverse should be made out. For this there must be evidence of open assertion of hostile title couple with exclusive possession and enjoyment by one co-sharer to the knowledge others. The burden of making out such ouster being on the person claimed into dispute the lawful title of a co-sharer by adverse possession. The concept of adverse possession contemplates a hostile possession i.e. a possession which is expressly or impliedly in denial of the title of the true owner. It is well-recognized proposition of law that mere possession, however, long does not necessarily mean that it is adverse to the true owner. The classical requirements of acquisition of title by adverse possession are that such possession in denial of the true owner's title must be peaceful, open and continuous. 

11. In this case, the plaintiffs pleaded that Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fatta settled the suit land to four brothers namely to Mafzular Rahman, Abdul Gofur, Abdul Bari and Ali Hossain. The defendant Monir Ahmed and others as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 17 of 1957 against heirs of Ali Hossain and others for declaration of their title and confirmation of possession and got decree in respect of the disputed tank and the said decree was affirmed upto the High Court Division. All the Courts found their possession. The cunning plaintiffs impleading the heirs of Ali Hossain as pro-forma defendants No.33-62 and impleading the heirs of rest three brothers as plaintiffs have instituted the present suit for ¾th share of the disputed tank on the basis of adverse possession. In Title Suit No. 17 of 1957 heirs of Ali Hossain contended that their predecessor purchased the suit tank inasmuch as in this case his brothers pleaded that they took settlement of the suit land. In view of such circumstances, it is difficult to accept the plaintiffs case that they are in uninterrupted and peaceful possession of the suit tank if it is found that they are at all in possession of 3/4th share of the suit tank. In Title Suit No. 17 of 1957, the High Court Division held that the defendants Monir Ahmed and others have been possessing the suit tank. "The doctrine of adverse possession would arise only when the party has set up his own and adverse title disclaiming the title of the owner and establishing that he remained exclusively in possession to the knowledge of the owner, hostile to his title and owner had acquiesced to the same." (Akramulla vs Bangladesh, XI ADC 147). Adverse possession became hostile to the rightful owner when a person openly, continuously, uninterruptedly and peacefully possessing the land under a claim of right adverse to the title of the true owner for the statutory period. It is now well established that a person who set up the plea of his title of adverse possession must prove by clear and unequivocal evidence that his possession was hostile to the real owner and amounted to deny of its title to the property claimed. 

12. We have already found that the defendant Monir Ahmed and others filed Title Suit No. 17 of 1957 in the First Court of Munsif, Satkania, Chittagong against Golam Khan and others for declaration of their title and confirmation of possession in the suit land and got decree and that decree was upheld that the High Court Division. All the Courts found title and possession of defendant Monir Ahmed and others in the suit land. It further appears from the materials on record that in connection with the proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the property, in question, was attached. In view of such circumstances, it is difficult to hold that the plaintiffs have had peaceful uninterrupted and continuous possession in the suit land. 

13. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the High Court Division rightly dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get decree in the suit land on the basis of adverse possession. 

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed. 

End.
